ARSENAL raised a few eyebrows among their fans when they splashed the cash on Ezri Konsa this summer.

The Gunners had just won the title with the meanest defence in the Premier League — and still decided to spend £55million on a new centre-back.



But nine games into his time in North London, Konsa has silenced the doubters with a string of top performances.

And the biggest compliment you can pay the former Aston Villa man is that Arsenal head to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday without worrying about William Saliba’s absence.



Keeping his England team-mate Harry Kane quiet would be another feather in Konsa’s cap and he has impressively stepped up while Saliba has been out with a back injury.

That is no surprise to those who know the defender best, such as Steve Avory.

The former Charlton academy director brought Konsa to the club when he was 12, and the talent was clear even at that age.

Avory told SunSport: “He’s always had that ability to move like a Rolls-Royce. It just seemed like there was no effort needed to get to top speed.

“At times when he was in the youth teams, you thought he was lucky because he used his pace to get out of trouble.

Avory has seen that type of challenge before, but what stood out in a young Konsa was his ability on the ball.

The England star often played in midfield for Charlton’s academy teams and the decision to move him to centre-back was made only as he got older.

Jason Pearce was one of Konsa’s early partners in the heart of defence and helped him take his first steps in surroundings far different to the Allianz Arena in Munich tomorrow.



Former Addicks captain Pearce said: “He got a grounding by playing in League One at an early age.

“At that level, you’ve got to be good defensively, win your duels, win your headers — and then there’ll be moments when you can play.

“When I watch him in the Premier League now, he does the same thing he was doing when he was 18 or 19.



“If he’d have come through a little bit younger, a little bit earlier, he might have suited being a right-back or a midfielder.

“But the way the game has gone, and how composed you need to be on the ball at centre-back, he suits playing in defence.

“We all talk about John Terry and Rio Ferdinand, and I would liken him more to Rio. He’s not just a ball-playing centre-back — he’s got everything.”

Konsa earned a move to Brentford in summer 2018 after excelling for the Addicks and it proved to be a pivotal time in his career.

He was signed by the then Bees head coach Dean Smith for his composure on the ball, but the club wanted to improve his physicality.



Smith’s former assistant, Richard O’Kelly, recalls devising a programme with the fitness coaches — which Konsa religiously stuck to.

O’Kelly said: “If you’re going to build up from the back, you need people like Ezri in your team.

“The only thing that put people off Ezri when he first came in was that he wasn’t a great specimen.



“Ezri needed some work in the gym to complement the rest of the stuff that he had, so that’s what he did.

“He put in the dedication that was needed for the work — and saw the benefits of it.

“He was always working on his game and always looking at video clips. His work ethic was second to none.”

Konsa’s physique may have transformed into that of an imposing defender, but his personality is the same.

Avory is still in touch with the Gunners’ new star and has been invited to watch him play for England at Wembley.



Pearce’s contact is less regular, however Konsa is always happy to help and recently sent him a signed shirt for a charity event.

He is described as selfless, and a big reason Smith signed him for Aston Villa — as well as Brentford — was Konsa’s influence in the dressing room.

O’Kelly added: “He wasn’t just ‘me, me, me’. He cared for other people.

Sports.title: Why Arsenal, Man City and Chelsea should be worried about Brighton and their ultra-flexible ‘polo-mint’ tactic

BRIGHTON continue to impress this season with arch-rivals Crystal Palace the latest club to be at the end of a Seagull pecking.

The Seagulls have enjoyed a fantastic start to the season and sit third in the Premier League table.



Fabian Hurzeler‘s side have been extremely entertaining and are the top scorers in the division.

Brighton have scored 23 GOALS in only seven games this season, having recorded two 5-0 and one 4-0 wins already.



The Seagulls have also only conceded five times – the best defensive record alongside Arsenal.

The South Coast side’s form will have the top sides such as Arsenal, Manchester City and Chelsea worried.



If Brighton continue to perform on their current level, then they could be certain of a Champions League spot.

SunSport’s tactical guru Dean Scoggins reveals how Carrick can turn the tide and save his job at United…

Brighton’s ‘polo mint’ strategy

Brighton’s “polo mint” strategy has been devised by manager Hurzeler and has flummoxed opposition sides.

The German gets his players to drop into a 4-5-1 formation when they are unable to commit everyone up the field.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The team also completely empties the midfield area which creates a hole in the centre – much like a polo mint.

This forces the opposition players into a decision of jumping forward or holding their positions.

If they jump forward, then a possible five-v-five opens up and if they stay back then the attack is easier to defend.

Hurzeler’s tactical approach appears to be a hybrid of Pep Guardiola and Johan Cruyff.



It gives his players the freedom to disrupt the other team.

When teams have tried to counter it with a mid-block, then Hurzeler switches up his tactics.

The German gets his midfielders such as Pascal Gross and Diego Gomez to pull to the centre and adopt a box midfield.

This creates space for the wide player to receive the ball more directly.



Dunk in control

Captain Lewis Dunk is one of the main stalwarts at Brighton, having been at the club since 2003.

Hurzeler has put a lot of faith in the six-time England international in both defence and attack.

The centre-back is able to dictate the tempo on the ball and helps the team trigger pressing effectively.



He maintains the team’s intensity of pressing for 90 minutes, so players must be aware of when to push up or ease off.

The centre-back orchestrates the game state and tempo which gives his team-mates the opportunity to choose their moments rather than relentless pressing.

Gross as ‘rogue trader’

Pascal Gross has become one of the most underrated players in the Premier League during two spells at Brighton.

The German operates as the team’s tactical lieutenant and acts as the “rogue trader” with his freedom across the pitch.

Gross has created 19 chances in his seven appearances and also one possession high up the pitch 14 times.

Sports.title: Eagles QB Hurts set to miss rest of NFL season due to blood clots
Sports.content:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is set to miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

The Eagles and Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn released a joint-statement on Monday saying he will be placed on blood thinners and is unable to play football until his recovery.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts is out for the rest of the year, adding that the former Super Bowl MVP was in hospital until 4am and did not sleep prior to Philadelphia's defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

Image: Hurts is set to be out for the rest of the season

"Over the past few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition," the joint-statement read.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation [ie. 'blood thinners']. During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football."

The statement adds that a "full recovery" is expected for Hurts and no long-term effects are anticipated.

Sports.title: Bills safety Gardner-Johnson suspended for spitting
Sports.content:
Buffalo Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson has been suspended for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on Sunday.

Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers.

In issuing the suspension, the NFL cited its rule applying to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Buffalo Bills against the Los Angeles Rams from Week 5 of the NFL season

With Buffalo (5-1) entering their bye week, Gardiner-Johnson's suspension will begin on October 26 and run through November 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens.

The player has the right to appeal the suspension.

Gardner-Johnson apologised to his team-mates immediately following Buffalo's 33-30 win and posted a note on social media apologising to fans.

"I owe my team-mates an apology and to be a man about it," Gardner-Johnson said following the game.

"You got to understand that as a grown man you can't be doing [stuff] like that in a game," he added. "As a vet, I'll be better. I'll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on."

The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons, and signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March.

Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson's spitting act as being "inexcusable" and said he discussed the matter privately with the player.

"It can't happen. That's not what we're about. That's not what the game of football is about, and he knows that," Brady said.

Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits.

"I don't need a roster of everybody being the same person," Brady said.

"Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can't happen. It won't happen again. Personality-wise, I'm not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do."

Sports.content:
Tottenham claimed their first Premier League win of the season by beating Coventry 3-1 as Dejan Kulusevski made his long-awaited return after 526 days out injured.

Spurs were winless across their opening six games heading into this fixture but a week in the Marbella sunshine and a well-needed performance on home turf have helped address the doom and gloom, with brighter skies in N17 possibly on the horizon.

James Maddison, making his first competitive start for Spurs since May 2025, announced his return to the starting line-up in emphatic style, curling his opener into the top corner against the club where his professional career began.

The playmaker was influential throughout, seamlessly linking the £300m pieces of Roberto De Zerbi's squad that had previously looked disjointed and awkward, but Jack Rudoni's equaliser just four minutes into the second half punctured the positivity brewing inside the stadium.

No side has dropped more points than Spurs from winning positions at home in the Premier League since the start of the 2024/25 season (30), but Omar Marmoush's first goal for the club, arrowing a fine strike into the far corner, put them on track to ensure they would not suffer the same fate on this occasion.

The feelgood factor that comes with a win skyrocketed in the 85th minute when fan-favourite Kulusevski made his comeback off the bench, bringing an end to his lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Image: Dejan Kulusevski made a welcome return to action for Spurs

Ben Davies' surprise effort with the outside of the boot rounded off the victory, on what could prove to be the evening that kickstarted the 2026/27 season for Spurs.

They move level on six points with Coventry and above their opponents on goal difference into 16th, having previously come into the fixture rock bottom of the table, and will now be tasked with building on their victory against London rivals Chelsea when the two sides meet at Stamford Bridge, live on Saturday Night Football.

14: GOAL! Maddison curls stunning opener into the top corner on his return to the starting line-up.

18: NO GOAL! Dominic Solanke taps home Andy Robertson's cross but the offside flag had already gone up.

49: EQUALISER! Rudoni powers his way into the Tottenham penalty area to force an equaliser home after half-time.

58: GOAL! Marmoush restores Tottenham's lead with his first goal for the club as his fine strike nestles into the far corner.

86: KULU RETURNS! Spurs winger Kulusevski makes his long-awaited return to the pitch after 526 days out injured with a knee setback.

90+6: GAME OVER! Davies scores a surprise goal off the bench to guarantee Spurs' first league win of the season.

Is Maddison the missing piece that can link the £300m puzzle?

Sky Sports' Patrick Rowe:

"James Maddison was the star of the show and a big reason Spurs were able to secure the well-needed win. His goal speaks for itself.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In his first competitive start for Tottenham since their 2024-25 Europa League semi-final, James Maddison puts Spurs ahead early in their Premier League clash with Coventry

"But the rest of his play also stood out, in a slightly more understated manner.

"He was dropping deep, finding pockets of space, threading passes for the runs of Dominic Solanke and threatening from the half spaces with his crossing ability.

"Spurs, after all their investment in the summer, looked disjointed and uninspiring across the opening six games.

"Maddison looks like the piece that could link the £300m pieces of this Spurs puzzle together. Whether that is through his own finishing or the ability to bring other players into the game.

"Keeping him fit and firing is now essential to the club building on this game."

Carra: Maddison has magic in his boots!

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football:

"James Maddison definitely has more panache than Conor Gallagher in that No 10 position.

"It was a joy to see [his goal]. He is one of the real characters in the game and you don't want him not around Premier League football.

Image: Maddison celebrates scoring the opening goal for Spurs

"That was just a great moment. When you're a player with an injury like that, there will be a fear: will you ever come back or will you be the same player?

"There is still a long way to go, but he still has a bit of magic in his boots!"

The 15-time major champion ‌has not competed in an official event since The Open at Royal Troon in July 2024, where he missed the cut.

There has been no subsequent confirmation of when he might return to competitive golf.

Sports.title: Ronaldo punished over Portugal walkout with fine he can pay off in 39 seconds
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days and fined £215 over his walkout from the Portugal national team following an explosive fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus.

The Portuguese FA's disciplinary council did not specify when Ronaldo's ban begins, but Sky Sports News understands it is enforced from the date he left the squad's training camp in Denmark on September 30.

It means the 41-year-old former Manchester United and Real Madrid star is available to play in Portugal's Nations League matches next month against Denmark and Wales if he is called upon by Jesus.

Ronaldo accused Jesus of broken promises and a "breach of trust" over his involvement in the team. The new head coach denied there had been any agreement.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player ICYMI: Ronaldo's extraordinary letter airing his problems with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus explained

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner asked to be punished by the Portuguese FA when he posted a lengthy letter detailing the circumstances which led to his departure from the camp. Ronaldo said he wanted to be spared any leniency.

However, the player reported to be the highest-paid footballer in the world could pay off his fine from the Portuguese FA in 39 seconds based on his estimated wages at Saudi Pro League club Al Nassr.

Ronaldo reportedly earns £488,000 per day from his Al Nassr salary, while Forbes estimate his earnings for 2026 will reach £225m.

The captain's fall-out with Jesus began after he was an unused substitute in a 2-1 win over Norway in Oslo. Ronaldo claims he was told he would be brought on and had warmed up only for Jesus to change his mind.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Piers Morgan argues that Ronaldo is the undisputed best player of all time ahead of Lionel Messi

Ronaldo missed the game against Denmark and the home match against Norway, both of which Portugal won to leave them top of Nations League Group A4 with a perfect record from four matches.

After the second win over Norway, Jesus insisted the door remained open for Ronaldo, who subsequently apologised for his actions and admitted he deserved to be sanctioned.

The Portuguese federation's disciplinary council announced Ronaldo's punishment in a 28-page document on Monday evening, saying it was "adequate and sufficient" for the player's "serious infraction".

Ronaldo is Portugal's record goalscorer and appearance holder with 146 goals in 234 caps. He said in his near-2000-word statement last month that he hopes his international career is not over yet.

Jesus did not comment when asked for his response to Ronaldo's lengthy statement to his 679 million Instagram followers. It is up to the Portugal head coach now to decide if Ronaldo is part of his plans for the next international break.

Sports.title: Davies ensures Spurs off the bottom after first win of season against Coventry
Sports.content:
Tottenham are level with Beyoncé at last. Progress is represented in Roberto De Zerbi’s side earning only their sixth home win in the Premier League since November 2024. Cynics will point out that this spectacular stadium has hosted as many Beyoncé gigs during that time, but Spurs are finally singing a happier tune after dragging themselves out of the bottom three thanks to a messy but gritty 3-1 win over Coventry.

It was not especially convincing. Coventry raged at the second Spurs goal, delivered when Omar Marmoush responded to Jack Rudoni’s equaliser for the visitors with a vicious effort in the 59th minute. Relief poured out of Marmoush after his first goal since joining on loan from Manchester City, but should it have stood? The Egyptian forward, who otherwise had a quiet game, was fortunate not to be penalised for an elbow on Milan van Ewijk.

Frank Lampard looked bewildered. The night belonged to Spurs, who have their first win of the season. James Maddison marked his first start in 536 days by opening the scoring with a brilliant goal. Ben Davies, on as a substitute, calmed the nerves by drilling in the third goal in added time and the home fans were also cheered by Dejan Kulusevski coming on to make his first appearance after more than a season out.

The hope for Spurs was that the sight of Kulusevski on the bench would give the crowd an emotional lift. The Swede was back in the squad for the first time since sustaining a knee injury in May 2025 and has been missed. Spurs, who have struggled without Kuluseveki’s creativity, needed to cling to the positivity after their resolute draw at Manchester United.

The encouraging thing is that they have been starting games well. This time, though, there were some early jitters after De Zerbi’s switch to a back three. Mohammed Kudus was a surprise choice as an attacking right wing-back, Archie Gray partnered Sandro Tonali in midfield and Coventry had the first chance, a fast break ending with Tatsuhiro Sakamoto watching his deflected shot spin over.

View image in fullscreen Jack Rudoni beats Antonin Kinsky to give the visitors hope. Photograph: Jonny Weeks/The Guardian

There were a few groans, but Spurs showed rare mental fortitude and struck through another creator rebuilding his career after serious injury. Kudus, lively and direct, provided the spark with a dart past Jay Dasilva. The Ghanaian laid a pass off to Maddison and the No 10, whose every touch had been booed by Coventry supporters apparently still seething with the England international leaving his boyhood club 10 years ago, used his right instep to beat Carl Rushworth with a crisp bending shot from 25 yards.

It was a lovely movement for Maddison, who beamed at his first goal since scoring in a Europa League semi-final against Bodø/Glimt on 1 May 2025. He slogged through his rehab, never giving in, and his enthusiasm was infectious. Even Lampard had to smile when Maddison tracked back to stop a counterattack and apologised after smashing the ball into the Coventry bench.

Coventry were slow to respond. Not that Spurs were flowing before half-time. Maddison was involved in some bright moves and Dominic Solanke jabbed a shot over but De Zerbi must have wanted the passing to be sharper. A slick exchange between Sidiki Cherif and Brandon Thomas-Asante was a reminder that this was not over. Thomas-Asante surged past Jan Paul van Hecke and towards Antonin Kinsky, only for Micky van de Ven to intervene with a crucial challenge.

Spurs did not heed the warning. A lethargic start to the second half featured Van Hecke ambling out of defence and losing the ball. Coventry countered, Rudoni pushing down the left. The midfielder exchanged passes with Caleb Yirenkyi and Spurs froze. Rudoni shot against Thomas-Asante, retrieved possession, chested the ball down and jabbed it past Kinsky to draw Coventry level.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen James Maddison curls his shot home for Tottenham’s first goal. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

Stung into action, Spurs raised the intensity and Tonali sent two shots over. Coventry looked uncertain but they raged when the home side regained their lead. Marmoush took a pass, turned and caught Van Ewijk in the face with an elbow. Yet Andrew Madley permitted play to continue with the Coventry right-back on the floor, allowing Marmoush to spin into space and blast an exquisite shot past Rushworth from 20 yards.

It was a stunning way for the Egyptian to score for the first time since May. There was no intervention from Paul Tierney, the video assistant referee, and the away end reacted with astonishment when the goal was replayed on the big screens.

Coventry were fired by a sense of injustice. They pushed for another equaliser and produced a spell of concerted pressure, only for Spurs to defend their box with determination.

De Zerbi sought more energy by bringing on Mateus Fernandes and Conor Gallagher. The Italian took his squad to Marbella for some warm weather training last week. Spurs, who pushed Coventry into 17th place, will hope sunnier times are on the way.

Sports.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes.

This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League?

Brentford began the weekend in third and with, perhaps, a slight sense of frustration that they had drawn four games. Again, they will feel they might have done rather better on Saturday; they were leading Liverpool 1-0 when Yehor Yarmolyuk foolishly flicked his head towards Jérémy Jacquet and was sent off just before half-time. The result was a 2-1 defeat and a sense of an opportunity missed. Bournemouth have not had the easiest start under Marco Rose, but Sunday’s 2-0 win over Sunderland perhaps hints at a brighter future.

Which left Brighton to carry the charge of the B clubs, which they did in emphatic style, ending a run of four derbies without success with a crushing 5-0 win. Crystal Palace had been extremely fortunate to survive a first-half battering from Nottingham Forest last week. They were thoroughly outplayed in the early stages again, and this time found themselves 3-0 down inside 10 minutes. Perhaps the opening goal, a cross headed into his own net by Jaydee Canvot, was fortunate, but it was an error induced by the intensity of Brighton’s start. The second goal, a perfectly weighted drive from just inside the Palace half from Diego Gómez, spoke of a side playing with immense confidence. Already this season, 11 different players have scored for Brighton in the league. They have become the image of a side without stars, the whole far greater than the individuals who comprise it.

The difference from February, when Brighton last played Palace, is stark. They lost that game 1-0, meaning they had won just one of their previous 12 Premier League games. Generalised grumbling had begun to curdle into calls for Fabian Hürzeler to be sacked. When they lost Carlos Baleba, Jan Paul van Hecke, Danny Welbeck and James Milner over the summer, there were reasons to wonder whether they could keep going with the process of continuous renewal.

There were the usual assorted signings, the usual mix of Premier League experience and exotic unknowns. The 19-year-old centre-back Luka Vušković, who spent last season on loan at Hamburg from Tottenham, already looks at home (and who really thought, when Spurs and Brighton effectively swapped centre-backs, with Van Hecke moving to London, that Brighton would not end up with the better of the deal?). The 21-year-old Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés, who arrived from Stuttgart, sparkled from the bench against Arsenal and has excelled in the two games since.

But the stand-out performer this season has been a far more familiar name: Pascal Gross, who returned in January after a season and a half at Borussia Dortmund. No player in the Premier League has registered more than his four assists this season. Nobody has run further. He has three goals. He averages a league-high 3.0 key passes a game. To bring back a player who is now 35 has been a masterstroke.

The victory over Arsenal before the international break suggested a team capable not merely of accumulating points against the league’s lesser lights, or even of challenging the elite, but of overwhelming them. Arsenal were suffocated by the Brighton press and, while a couple of low-xG long-range finishes in the first half helped, the fact is that Brighton dominated the match to a remarkable extent.

The question is whether they can keep it going. Just as their transfer policy is now an accepted feature of the Premier League, so too is Brighton’s mid-season slump. They haven’t won a game in December since 2023. Is this squad strong enough to sustain the challenge? Europe seems not to be unsettling Brighton as it did on their first foray, or as it appears to be draining Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Sunderland – which may be a reflection on the relative quality of the Conference League.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

They are doing this without Kaoru Mitoma, Yankuba Minteh and Mats Wieffer, all of whom should be back at some point over the next month. That suggests the depth of this Brighton squad. It’s always a major step for a club unfamiliar with the Champions League to haul themselves into the top five. At times it often feels a mental barrier as much as anything.

But if any of those B clubs are ever going to break into the Champions League, they may never have a better opportunity than Brighton do this season.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace to give Sage more time but manager under serious scrutiny
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage has been granted more time to fix Crystal Palace’s defensive issues but he has been warned that things must improve quickly after the 5-0 defeat at Brighton on Sunday.

The Frenchman’s future was in serious doubt after his side conceded three times inside the opening 10 minutes before equalling the 70‑year record for the club’s heaviest defeat against their arch-rivals. The thrashing means Palace have conceded the most goals in the Premier League: 17 from seven games.

The club chair, Steve Parish, is understood not to have been fully convinced by Sage since the 47‑year‑old was appointed to replace Oliver Glasner in the summer. Parish is believed to have considered parting company with Sage on Sunday after 10 matches but decided against a change given that Palace are 14th and not in immediate danger.

Sage is expected to remain in charge not only for the Europa League game at Besiktas on Thursday but also the Premier League match against Newcastle on Sunday. But it has been made clear to the former Lens manager that his position is under heavy scrutiny. Kieran McKenna, who Parish approached while the Northern Irishman was at Ipswich, and Thomas Frank will be among the contenders if Sage is sacked.

Tensions between Sage and Parish date to the summer transfer window when Palace failed to secure the manager’s main targets to replace Maxence Lacroix in central defence. Two loanees, Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor –, were signed instead from Chelsea and Atalanta respectively. Palace also missed out on Malick Fofana to Sunderland on deadline day despite Sage making the Belgium forward, whom he coached in Lyon’s youth teams, a priority. Palace instead signed Darío Osorio on an initial loan and the Chile forward has played only a handful of minutes.

Parish was unhappy with Sage’s treatment of Jaydee Canvot after the France Under-21 international was dropped from the squad for the home defeat by Ipswich last month. He is also understood to have been angered by Adam Wharton being substituted in that match after Disasi was shown a red card in the first half.

Some behind the scenes at Palace have been pushing for Sage to be sacked, but Parish is thought to recognise the headache caused by Disasi’s three-match suspension and injuries to Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu and would prefer to give him an opportunity to turn things around.

Chris Richards has apologised to Palace supporters after failing to acknowledge them after the Brighton game. “I want to apologise for walking off after the game,” the USA defender wrote on Instagram.

“I was emotional and embarrassed with the result – I know how much this club means to all of you. We have to take responsibility, do better and show that on the pitch.”

Sports.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
Sports.content:
Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body.

A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair, the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review.

Uefa’s latest intervention follows last week’s meeting of the Fifa council in Zurich, the first time it had gathered since the emergence of the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) controversy in July. Infantino listened to questions on FFE and other matters, but declined to provide substantive answers, instead asking council members to submit them in writing before their next meeting in Doha on 16 December.

In a letter sent on Monday, Theodoridis wrote: “These explanations have not begun satisfactorily to address a number of fundamental questions raised by Council members.

“Others remain unanswered, and the information and documentation requested have not been provided.

“Following the invitation made during the meeting to submit our questions in writing, we therefore enclose a consolidated set of questions and requests for information.

“We formally request a substantive written response to each question, together with all supporting documentation by Monday 2nd November. Any refusal to disclose information or documents should be justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon.

“These questions require answers now. They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the Fifa Council – nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them.”

View image in fullscreen Aleksander Ceferin (centre), the Uefa president, and Theodore Theodoridis, the organisation’s general secretary, pictured in 2023. Photograph: Massimo Pinca/Reuters

The accompanying document and list of supplementary questions constitutes a damning takedown of Fifa’s leadership under Infantino, who, as it stands, is on course to be re-elected unopposed as president next year, although Uefa is increasingly hopeful of identifying a candidate to take him on before nominations close on 18 November.

Uefa also wants answers on the processes behind other major decisions taken by Fifa over the past 12 months including moving the men’s World Cup draw to Washington DC from Las Vegas, the introduction of hydration breaks and the 27-minute half-time at the World Cup final.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“A series of decisions, transactions and interventions involving the Fifa President, the President of the United States and individuals associated with him raise serious questions concerning potential conflicts of interest, transparency and institutional accountability,” Uefa states.

The amount Fifa is paying to rent office space in Trump Tower is also queried, as is a report in the Times last week that Infantino in 2024 “received substantial additional remuneration which was not disclosed in Fifa’s annual report”. Fifa has said it “does not pay a second salary to the Fifa president and complies with all reporting requirements in relation to compensation”.

Uefa also raises concerns about March’s presidential election, specifically regarding the involvement of Bruno Chiomento, the chair of Fifa’s electoral committee. “We understand that Mr Chiomento has known the Fifa President for approximately 20 years and is regularly invited to Fifa events and competitions at Fifa’s expense,” Uefa’s document states. “We further understand that he attended the entire 2026 World Cup as an accredited individual, with his expenses covered by Fifa for more than five weeks.”

Uefa has also requested a complete list of Fifa guests in VIP and VVIP areas at the World Cup final, on the grounds that “numerous guests were apparently given priority over Presidents of Member Associations and Secretaries General of Confederations”.

Fifa has been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkout
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese ⁠FA after leaving the national team camp following a rift with the coach, ⁠Jorge Jesus, over ⁠his role in the side. The federation’s disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against ⁠the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of €255 (£215).

Ronaldo left Portugal’s base in ⁠Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark this month, having accused ‌Jesus of twice ‌breaking his word about his role after he was an ‌unused substitute against Norway. Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but left the door open for his return after Portugal’s 2-1 win.

The disciplinary council’s non-professional section found Ronaldo had intentionally committed an offence under Article 160(1) ‌of the federation’s disciplinary regulations. Proceedings were opened on 9 October over facts reported two days earlier.

The statement did not specify which matches or activities the suspension would cover, or whether time already served under a provisional suspension would count towards the 30-day sanction.

Ronaldo later ⁠apologised for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates, saying he remained available for selection after serving any ‌punishment arising from the incident.

The Portuguese FA president, Pedro Proença, has said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved.

Meanwhile, Fifa has suspended the Egypt coach, Hossam Hassan, and the forward Mostafa Ziko for ⁠three and five matches respectively, the Egyptian Football Association said on Monday, after they ⁠criticised the referee ⁠following their ​3-2 defeat by Argentina in the World Cup.

The 60-year-old Hassan was sanctioned after blaming ⁠refereeing errors for his country’s elimination from the tournament in the last 16, while Ziko insulted the ⁠referee in a post-match interview.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ibrahim Hassan, Hossam’s twin and ​Egypt’s national team director, ‌has also been suspended ‌for three matches.

“The decisions include the suspension of Hossam Hassan ‌and Ibrahim Hassan for three matches each, while Ziko has been suspended for five matches,” the EFA said in a statement.

Sports.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said.

At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that, whatever that was, in Istanbul – an “almost rabona”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote.

To which Lamine Yamal responded by doing another strange thing that same afternoon, scoring another brilliant goal to set Barcelona on the way to a 5-2 win over Betis in a game that made history. And if Lamine Yamal had been a little lucky three days before, momentarily losing control only for the rebound to bounce back to him like the ball knew where it would rather be, this was all him and very him. The move started with Gerard Martín losing his boot and ended with pretty much everyone else losing their heads. In Martín’s momentary absence, Rodri dropped into defence and began it from there, the ball moved across the box and back until it was played up to Lamine Yamal. His superb pass with the outside of the boot unlocked everything and then, receiving again just inside Betis’s half, he set off.

There’s a moment, Lamine Yamal says, when you can sense the anticipation, feel people getting up one after the other all along the stand, a wave accompanying you, moving with you. At that moment, he says, there’s some inner power and you feel like Superman or Spider-Man; the defenders are robots, he says, and however good a robot is, however well programmed to stop him, a human is better. Too fast, too agile, too inspired. Too much thought gone into this, too much psychology. Man against the machines, code this. He rolled the ball one way with his left foot, flicked it the other with the heel of his right, and from the edge of the box, sent it flying into the far top corner.

View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal tries to get away from Dani Ceballos and Facundo Bernal. Photograph: Antonio Pozo/Pressinphoto/Shutterstock

Somehow. Sometimes you have nothing new to say, you know? It’s not big and it’s not clever but sometimes only swearing will do: sometimes only holy shit! hits the spot. Sometimes you can be sitting alone on the sofa and still shout: “Oh, my God!”, call them in to watch this. But it won’t be the same when they do, even if it’s sort of better: a chance to slow it down and break it down, see the detail, work out how he did it, like you’re ever going to do that. Because for all the expectation, it’s still a shock seen live, the purest reaction of all.

Words? Pah! This weekend, Gabriel Jesus put it best: as the ball passed him, he just held his head in his hands. Lamine Yamal ran to the corner. Fermín López chased, wiping his brow: woah, what was that? Karim Adeyemi went wagging his fingers. On the touchline Flick almost took off his assistant’s hand with the hardest high five. Teammates ran towards him not so much celebrating as laughing, so good it’s funny and even funnier for being repeated, an outrageous goal his catchphrase. Lamine Yamal sat alongside Jules Koundé on the advertising board, arms crossed like it was easy, like “what are you lot losing your heads about?” Maybe it is. And there is something in the way he hit it that felt a little like he put it in the top corner because, well, why not? Might as well.

Lamine Yamal got up, stood holding the corner flag, looking about: will that do? If this was the first test Barcelona have faced, it hadn’t taken him 10 minutes to score again, and like that. And that’s the thing. Who knows, this might not even have been the best goal of the weekend: there were glorious moments from Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappé in Real Madrid’s win against Sevilla. Javi Rodríguez’s run was wonderful for Celta Vigo against Alavés. And Pablo Martínez’s shot in Málaga’s 2-5 loss to Real Sociedad was ridiculous. It might not have even been the best shot of this game had Gio Lo Celso’s “goal” not been ruled out. And it definitely might not even be the best Lamine Yamal has scored, but this keeps happening. Statement after statement.

He didn’t stop there either: there was an absurd pass from which Adeyemi should have scored. A run through three. Another assist. And the moment that got the Betis fans whistling him: when, with López on the ground and Lamine Yamal going over, Facundo Bernal pushed him, he took a run-up and pushed Bernal back, and the defender head-butted him, seeing red. The game hadn’t stopped with his first either; instead, Rodri said afterwards, it had “everything”. Always watch Betis, especially when they’re playing Barcelona: unbeaten in 15 home games, the last time anyone beat them here was Barça too. And it finished 5-3. This time they were only one short.

View image in fullscreen Barcelona’s Gabriel Jesus celebrates scoring their third goal with Lamine Yamal. Photograph: Marcelo del Pozo/Reuters

Barcelona had dominated the first 25 minutes, the ball theirs alone but Valentín Gómez headed in to make it 1-1 before Rodri made it 2-1. Within two minutes, Lo Celso had smashed in an extraordinary 25-yard shot on the bounce and the turn to make it 2-2, only for it to be ruled out for a handball 14 seconds earlier. All that before half-time. And yet it was summed up better by the 30 seconds that passed between Álvaro Valles making a superb save at one end and Joan García matching it at the other; by the 59 seconds that passed between that and Jesus getting the third. Or the two minutes 59 seconds between that going in and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli making it 3-2. Then the fight that followed it, Lamine Yamal tumbling maybe a touch too hard and Bernal walking.

By the time Lamine Yamal did, at last encouraged to rest, Eric García had scored the fourth and it was done. “With this result, we had to make the change,” Flick said; with tensions rising too. Dani Olmo added a neat fifth and it finished. Betis were furious. Asked how it had left him feeling, their manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said: “impotent”. Lo Celso’s goal shouldn’t have been ruled out and Jesus’s should, he said. Ask how he felt, Fran García said “frustrated, angry … and tired”. They had given everything, the ovation as generous as their effort had been. “This is one of the hardest games in La Liga,” Rodri said, but Barcelona had won again.

That’s nine from nine, a new record. Now, a word of advice from Mr Wolf. When it comes to historic starts, Barcelona’s previous record was under Tata Martino, who you may remember but probably don’t. “This is a nice thing but we want to win titles,” Flick said; Martino did not. Betis were the first team Barcelona have played in the top half of the table. The rest currently sit in 19th, 18th, 17th, 16th, 15th 14th, and 11th. Harder games are coming: Paris Saint-Germain next, then Real Madrid. They also have an injury crisis at the back. But no one is playing like them, and certainly not scoring like them. They have scored 39 league goals, 48 in 11 matches in all competitions.

Quick Guide La Liga results Show Deportivo A Coruña 1-1 Levante, Espanyol 0-1 Atlético, Villarreal 0-0 Elche, Real Betis 2-5 Barcelona, Valencia 0-0 A Bilbao, Osasuna 2-0 Racing Santander, Celta Vigo 2-1 Alavés, Málaga 2-5 Real Sociedad, Real Madrid 4-1 Sevilla Monday: Getafe v Rayo Vallecano Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

When Robert Lewandowski, Ferran Torres and Marcus Rashford went in the summer, when they didn’t manage to sign Julián Álvarez, you couldn’t help asking where the goals were going to come from. The answer was everywhere. Thirteen different players have scored. It turns out that they have the best striker in Europe: Raphinha, the man who is just filling in there, has scored more than anyone else. They may also have the best player at 19, the kid who came back a World Cup winner and still wasn’t satisfied.

“After the game against Elche at the start of the season, people were saying: ‘He’s not right,’” Lamine Yamal said. “But I was calm at home, thinking: ‘I’ve just won the World Cup, I’ve not had a break, I know my body: bit by bit I’ll get to the point where I explode and start to score. And those same people will suddenly be saying I’m the best.’” In the first two games, against Elche and Athletic Bilbao, Lamine Yamal did little. Since then he has scored or assisted in every match. Nine goals, 10 assists, and most of them brilliant. He went to the international break and scored after 104 seconds at Wembley, 70 in Seville, and 320 in Oviedo. Here, on the day they said this time it’s for real, it took him 530, heads in hands, words stuck in throats, and another win on the way.

“It was amazing, a match for all the people who love football,” Flick said. “For me Lamine is the best in the world. I’m happy about his performance; this is what I love to see. And when you see the first goal, it’s unbelievable.”

Unbelievable. That’ll do.

Sports.title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland
Sports.content:
Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday.

Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has admitted previously that Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised.

“To replace Erling it’s always difficult but we have some different options; we’ll see tomorrow,” Maresca said. “To lose Antoine or any player for us is not good. Then in terms of Erling, we said that we can use Antoine as a 9 but also we have different players that we are going to try and to find new solutions.”

Maresca witnessed a number of his players limp away from the win against Ipswich: Haaland, Semenyo, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly, who all featured at the World Cup. Maresca had made six changes, showing the need to rotate amid a hectic schedule of seven games in 21 days in October for City, many of whose players also had international commitments at the start of the month.

“We try to manage all the players in the best way, try to keep them fit,” Maresca said. “Even sometimes things happen that you cannot control, like Antoine’s injury. We try to save him, we try to keep him fresh.”

The fixtures mean it is difficult for Maresca to get training time as he tries to instil his style. “We try and do what we can on the pitch to go through a few things and tactics before the games,” the defender Marc Guéhi said. “It’s just a lot of recovery, sleep, to make sure the body is right for the next game,. It’s been enjoyable, to be honest; not to train, just playing games, which is fun.”
