World.title: Liberia Conducts First National Honeybee Survey to Boost Beekeeping
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Ministry of Agriculture(MOA), in collaboration with the Society for the Conservation of Nature Liberia (SCNL) and other partners, has convened a national workshop to validate findings from Liberia’s first national honeybee survey, aimed at establishing baseline data to guide the development of the country’s beekeeping industry.

By Francis G. Boayue

The validation workshop held over the weekend brought together stakeholders in agriculture, beekeeping and conservation to review the survey findings, identify challenges facing honey producers, and recommend measures to strengthen production, improve market access, and promote sustainable beekeeping practices.



The survey covers Liberia’s 15 counties and seeks to establish baseline information on the number and distribution of beekeepers, honey production trends, harvesting methods, and the marketing of honey products.

Austin G. Yeanay, Director of Extension at the Ministry of Agriculture, welcomed participants and expressed optimism that the findings would provide useful information to advance the sector.

Yeanay acknowledged that the survey process had faced delays but said the information gathered from the field would provide a basis for discussions and further action. He encouraged participants to carefully review the findings and contribute to deliberations that would help move the beekeeping sector forward.

Cecil S. Wilson, Country Director of Universal Outreach, said the survey presented an opportunity to understand the current state of beekeeping in Liberia, particularly in areas where organizations have supported the activity for several years.

Wilson, who said he had spent 14 years working in Liberia, noted that the initiative would help stakeholders assess developments in the sector and identify barriers to its growth.

He urged participants to pay close attention to the findings and provide meaningful contributions to ensure the final report accurately reflects the realities of beekeeping across the country.

Michael E. Taire, Program Manager of SCNL, described the survey as significant, noting that Liberia had not previously conducted a national assessment of honey production.

According to Taire, the findings will establish a baseline against which future changes in the number of beekeepers, production levels, and market participation can be measured.

He explained that the survey examines the number of farmers engaged in honeybee production, their geographic distribution, harvesting practices and the plant species that attract bees.

The assessment also considers how beekeepers process, package and market their products, including whether they sell locally or supply supermarkets and other larger markets.

Taire said the information would help stakeholders determine whether honey production is increasing or declining and identify opportunities to improve the competitiveness of Liberian honey.

He added that the findings could inform strategies to expand market access and explore opportunities for exporting Liberian honey to other countries.

The initiative is supported by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) through the Apimondia program, with the Ministry of Agriculture taking the lead in collaboration with SCNL and other organizations involved in beekeeping development.

Other partners identified during the workshop included the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation, Samaritan’s Purse, Universal Outreach, and the Association of Beekeepers of Liberia. The names and roles of participating organizations will need confirmation before publication.

Beyond agricultural production, Taire said beekeeping also contributes to environmental conservation because honeybees depend on flowering plants, including those found in forests and agricultural areas.

He encouraged communities, particularly those living near forest areas, to embrace beekeeping while protecting forests and planting trees that provide suitable habitats and food sources for bees.

According to him, maintaining healthy forest ecosystems can support honey production while advancing broader conservation efforts. The validated report is expected to provide the Ministry of Agriculture and its partners with information to guide interventions, address challenges confronting beekeepers, and strengthen the development of Liberia’s honey production industry.

World.title: Solwezi residents calls for sidewalk on Mitec-Mine Boom road
World.content:
Road users in Mushitala area of Solwezi district are appealing to the government and Kansanshi Mining PLC to put up a sidewalk on the Mitec-Mine Boom gate dual carriage way road upgrade.

Dorcus Mokya, expressed concern that the road which is under construction will not have a sidewalk for pedestrians.

She explained that the road is very busy with a lot of schools stressing the need for the government to put up a sidewalk as construction is still ongoing.

“We appreciate that the road is being constructed into a dual carriageway but our concern is the safety of road users especially school going children,” Ms Mokya said.

Meanwhile, another road user, William Kamalata, has thanked the government for upgrading the road adding that it will help reduce congestion.

Mr Kamalata stated that once the road is completed, it will reduce the challenges motorists faced in repairing vehicles due to the poor condition the road was in.

He has called on Kansanshi to put up sidewalks for easy and free movement of pedestrians.

Mr Kamalata has further called for the erection of shelters at the designated bus stops.

“This development is commendable, and we have to work together to safeguard the signage that will be put on the road,” he emphasised.

World.title: ACC arrests former Mkushi DEBS over K2.49 million
World.content:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has arrested and charged Chama District Education Board Secretary, Titus Mbewe, over alleged irregularities involving K2.49 million in contracts for the supply of maize and dried beans under a School Feeding Programme.

Mbewe, 56, faces two counts of abuse of authority of office and one count of willful failure to follow applicable procedure under the Anti-Corruption Act, Chapter 91 of the Laws of Zambia,

It is alleged that between January and December 2025, while serving as District Education Board Secretary for Mkushi District, Mbewe facilitated payments of K1,424,115 to Frelun Commodities Limited for the supply of white maize and K1,073,000 to Ichikwanka Multi-Purpose Cooperative for dried beans before the contracts were approved by the Mkushi Council Secretary.

The total value of the two contracts was K2, 497,115.

It is further alleged that Mbewe authorised full payment to the suppliers before the goods were delivered.

In the third count, allegations are that Mbewe, acting with other persons unknown, facilitated the circumvention of procurement procedures by purporting that the Evaluation Committee and Procurement Committee had evaluated the tenders when they had not.

The alleged offences relate to procurement activities in Mkushi District during the period when Mbewe served as its District Education Board Secretary.

This is according to a statement issued to ZANIS by Anti-Corruption Commission Head – Corporate Communications Joseph Mwenya.

Mr Mwenya stated that Mbewe had been released on bond and would appear in court soon.

World.title: Nine months Chipata baby shot while sleeping
World.content:
A nine-months-old baby girl is battling for her life at Chipata Central Hospital after she was shot by unknown person(s) while sleeping in her house in Mchenga Compound, Chipata District.

Mr Mweemba said Chipata Central Police Station received the report yesterday, 18th October 2026 at 18:30 hours, from the mother of the victim, Karen Phiri aged 24 years of Mchenga Compound.

He said brief facts are that at around 21:00 hours, the mother was sleeping with her child in the house before she went to the toilet outside, leaving the child inside.

“Whilst outside, the grandmother of the victim who was inside the house heard a bang and immediately the child cried. Upon hearing that, she rushed to the bedroom where the child was and found that the child was in a pool of blood with a wound on the forehead,” Mr Mweemba said.

He said the mother who was outside also rushed back into the house and found the child injured, and later rushed her to Chipata Trades Mini Hospital where she was attended to and referred to Chipata Central Hospital.

Mr Mweemba said while the mother was at the hospital with the victim, the grandmother, Agness Daka aged 57 years of the same abode, discovered a projectile where the child was sleeping, and at the hospital it was discovered that the child had sustained another wound at the back of the head.

He said police officers who visited the scene discovered a hole on top of the roof suspected to be the entrance of the bullet.

“The projectile was picked from the scene and has been kept as an exhibit. The victim is currently admitted at Chipata Central Hospital Intensive Care Unit and is in a stable condition,” Mr Mweemba said.

He said investigations have since been instituted into the matter.

World.title: Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka Golf Tournament attracts 72 golfers
World.content:
The Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka Golf Tournament has been held at Lusaka Golf Club, attracting 72 golfers ahead of the 2026 Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka, scheduled to run from October 19 to 23 at Mulungushi International Conference Centre in Lusaka.

Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development Permanent Secretary, Hapenga Kabeta, said the ZAMII Golf Tournament provides an opportunity for stakeholders in the mining industry, the investment community and cooperating partners to strengthen relationships and exchange ideas ahead of the Insaka.

Officiating at the event today, Dr Kabeta called for stronger partnerships between the government, mining companies and other stakeholders to unlock the full potential of Zambia’s mining sector.

Dr Kabeta said increased investment, responsible mining practices and value addition to mineral resources are critical to driving economic growth, creating jobs and promoting industrial development.

He expressed optimism that the spirit of collaboration demonstrated at the golf tournament would continue during the 2026 Mining and Investment Insaka and future editions.

Dr Kabeta added that discussions at the Insaka should focus on identifying investment opportunities, addressing challenges affecting the sector and developing strategies to maximise the benefits of Zambia’s mineral resources.

He further stressed the need to increase the participation of Zambian businesses in the mining industry and promote value addition within the country.

Meanwhile, Lusaka Golf Club President, Pravin Patel, said the Insaka Corporate Golf Tournament provides an opportunity for stakeholders in the mining, investment and corporate sectors to build relationships and explore partnerships that can contribute to Zambia’s economic growth.

Mr Patel noted that golf offers a platform for stakeholders to interact outside the boardroom, fostering trust, friendship and business partnerships in a relaxed environment.

World.title: Luangwa parents urged to immunise under-fives
World.content:
Luangwa District Health Director Chabota Munga’mbata has called on community members to take their under five children for immunisation and vaccination during the forthcoming Child Health week.

Dr Munga`mbata says Child Health Week is an important exercise which all parents or guardians should not miss.

He says this provides an opportunity for safeguarding the wellbeing of the children, which eventually results in a productive society in accordance with the Agenda 2030.

He was speaking to the media in an interview in Luangwa District.

Dr Munga’mbata has explained that health care providers will be going around the community to provide health services.

“Health care providers will carry out services such as HIV check-ups, nutrition, deworming, vitamin A supplementation and immunisation targeting over 7000 children,” he explained.

Dr Munga`mbata has disclosed that this coming Child Health Week will be the first which will include malaria vaccination.

He says the exercise will commence on 26th October, 2026 and will end on 30th October, 2026.

Luangwa District Health Promotions Officer Dasty Mungoni has appealed to stakeholders to continue supporting the programme, adding that this has enabled the district to record a reduction in the number of ailments in children.

Mr Mungoni says that all those that missed the last child health week should ensure that their children are attended to.

“We are urging all those that missed the last Child Health Week to ensure that their children receive the immunisations and supplements,” he said.

He has thanked the traditional leadership in the district for the massive support they render through community mobilisation.

World.title: Ngabwe DC bemoans persistent pontoon breakdowns
World.content:
Ngabwe District Commissioner, Stanley Mwendachabe has bemoaned the persistent breaking down of the pontoon that services the people of Ngabwe to cross the Kafue River.

Mr Mwendachabe has appealed for the installation of a temporary bridge to ease the movement of goods and services.

The District Commissioner said the pontoon lacks the capacity to withstand the loads of goods, especially with the bumper harvest that the district recorded during the previous harvest.

He observed that the three Food Reserve Agency (FRA) depots in the district are full of maize which needs to be transported, hence the need for a steady flow of traffic which is being hindered by the persistent breaking down of the pontoon.

And Kairos Samaki, a local farmer, also called for the construction of a bridge to avert the transportation challenges.

Mr Samaki said the security of the maize at FRA depots is being compromised due to the constant breakdown of the pontoon.

Some people are reported to have resorted to using canoes to transport their maize across the Kafue River.

World.title: President Hichilema urges mining firms to prioritise local content
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has implored mining companies to prioritise local content as well as support the local supplier development programme so as to equip domestic businesses with the capacity to provide quality, competitively priced goods and services on time.

Mr Hichilema cited the use of locally manufactured electrical cables and mill balls in mining operations as examples of how local content could improve supply-chain efficiency while creating business opportunities for Zambian companies.

He further said that the benefits of mining should extend beyond corporate social responsibility projects to include employment, skills development, technology transfer and business opportunities for host communities.

President Hichilema was speaking today in Lusaka during the official opening of the third five days 2026 Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka (ZAMII), which is being held under the theme: “Transforming Africa’s Mining Landscape: Regional Value Chains, Shared Prosperity and Empowering Communities.”

Mr Hichilema disclosed that government plans to establish skills training centres in all 116 districts, urging mining companies to collaborate with the public sector to ensure training programmes respond to local industrial needs.

He pointed out that Zambia needs to increase investment in mineral exploration to sustain production growth and achieve its target of producing three million tonnes of copper annually.

Mr Hichilema also said the government has invested nearly US$100 million in a high-resolution geophysical survey covering the country’s 752,000 square kilometres to help investors identify mineral prospects and guide further exploration.

He explained that the survey, which was nearing completion, will provide investors with valuable geological information to support targeted exploration and the development of new mines.

He called for increased regional cooperation among Zambia, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Botswana to develop mineral value chains, attract investment and expand cross-border industrial partnerships.

President Hichilema said the three countries could jointly invest in energy infrastructure, electric vehicle manufacturing and battery value chains to ensure that more value from their mineral resources was retained within the region.

Mr Hichilema also urged government institutions to improve the efficiency of regulatory processes and create a predictable investment environment, while ensuring that mining activities complied with environmental protection requirements.

He also said stronger cooperation among African countries will enable the region to attract larger pools of capital, access advanced technologies and create opportunities for its growing young population.

And President of Botswana Duma Boko in a speech read on his behalf by his Minister of Minerals and Energy Bogolo Kenewendo, said Botswana and Zambia are exploring the establishment of a regional mining equipment manufacturing and advanced engineering hub to reduce reliance on imported mining machinery and strengthen local industrial capacity.

President Boko said the proposed facility in Botswana, could support mining equipment manufacturing, precision engineering, fabrication, refurbishment and technical services, with significant participation from Zambian businesses.

He further said the initiative is part of broader efforts to deepen regional integration and develop mineral value chains within Southern Africa.

Mr Boko disclosed that the proposed manufacturing campus is expected to be complemented by a 300 megawatt solar photovoltaic project and a 130 megawatt battery energy storage system, subject to ongoing technical and commercial assessments.

Also at the event, DRC Preside Felix Tshisekedi in a speech read on his behalf by his Minister of Mines Louis Kabamba has called for stronger regional cooperation with Zambia to promote mineral value addition, develop cross-border industries and ensure that more economic benefits from mining remain within Africa.

President Tshisekedi said the two countries should leverage their shared mineral resources to develop regional value chains, create employment and accelerate industrialisation rather than continue exporting largely unprocessed minerals.

He noted that Zambia’s target of producing three million tonnes of copper annually by 2031 presents an opportunity for the entire region to strengthen economic cooperation instead of engaging in unnecessary competition.

He explained that shared mineral deposits between the two countries provide a strong foundation for joint industrial development.

Mr Tshisekedi pointed out that the continued export of partially processed minerals and dependence on imported mining equipment and processing materials demonstrates the need for Africa to retain more value from its natural resources.

He cited the proposed development of electric vehicle battery value chains in Zambia’s Copperbelt Province and the DRC’s Lualaba Province as an example of how the two countries could complement each other’s industrial ambitions.

Meanwhile, Canadian High Commissioner to Zambia Corry Van Gaal disclosed that Canada aims to make Zambia its leading global mining investment destination by 2032, from its current position as the country’s fifth-largest mining investment destination.

Ms Van Gaal said Canada remains committed to deepening and diversifying investments in Zambia, citing growing interest from Canadian mining companies and ongoing expansion projects as evidence of confidence in the country’s mining sector.

She also said Canada’s cumulative investment in Zambia reached approximately US$12 billion in 2024, according to Natural Resources Canada.

She further said the two countries should strengthen their commercial partnership to ensure that mining investments generate mutual benefits through job creation, skills development, local business participation and community empowerment.

Ms Van Gal advised that responsible mining should be measured not only by mineral production but also by the skills, businesses and stronger communities left behind for future generations.

World.title: Mining sector records tech advancement
World.content:
Acting Minister of Mines and Minerals Development Gilbert Siame has disclosed that Zambia has experienced significant technological advancements in the mining sector with increased investment inflows and improved management within local companies.

Mr Siame was speaking during the official opening of the third Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka at Mulungushi International Conference Centre in Lusaka.

Mr Siame said that the technological advancement in the sector is a result of clear and transparent reforms.

“As government we will continue to reform the mining sector so that we achieve three million tonnes of copper production annually,” he said.

The Minister also encouraged responsible mining from all players in the sector.

“We will not encourage pollution and as the ministry we will do everything possible to ensure sustainable mining,” he said.

And Chinese Mining Enterprise Association president of Zambia Wang Jingjun says that the Association remains committed to supporting Zambia’s goal of producing three million tonnes of copper annually through technology and investment.

Mr Jingjun added that Chinese mining companies are expanding their presence across the Copperbelt and North Western provinces to support this national strategy.

“This will be done through increasing cumulative investment to generate tax revenue and jobs,” Mr Jingjun said.

He added that China will align corporate development with Zambia’s National development strategy and deepen cooperation through the China- Africa mining cooperation proposal.

Mr Jingjun highlighted that digitalisation and intelligent technologies are being used to transform mining productivity and safety.

Meanwhile, Zambia Chamber of Mines Chief Executive officer Sokwani Chilembo says that the recent technological advancement indicates renewed innovation within the Zambian mining landscape.

Mr Chilembo added that mining is playing its part to ensure that it achieves the three million metric tonnes of copper production by 2031’

World.title: Africa: Macky Sall Officially Withdraws His Candidacy for UN Secretary-General Position
World.content:
Former Senegalese President Macky Sall announced on Saturday, October 17, 2026, his withdrawal of his candidacy for the post of Secretary-General of the United Nations.

In a statement released from Marrakech, the former head of state said he wants to promote an international consensus. This announcement follows the vote held on October 16, 2026, at the United Nations headquarters in New York. Sall said that he made this decision with a profound sense of institutional responsibility, and that various consultations and indicative votes held within the Security Council revealed, from the outset, a preference for a candidate from the Latin America and Caribbean region - possibly a woman.

In his written statement, the former head of state said his initiative was motivated by his desire to put nearly forty years of experience in public life at the service of multilateral governance. He expressed his gratitude to the heads of state who supported him in this endeavor, particularly acknowledging the sponsorship of Évariste Ndayishimiye and the support provided by President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. He also thanked the member states of the Security Council who gave him their votes during the consultations.

Macky Sall thanked his campaign team, religious and traditional authorities, as well as all Senegalese citizens, political actors and representatives of civil society, in Africa and elsewhere in the world, who mobilized around his candidacy.

The continent, Sall said, must continue to make its voice heard and advocate for more equitable representation within international bodies, and needs to strengthen its role in global governance.

The former president concluded his statement by expressing his best wishes for success to the person who will succeed António Guterres as head of the United Nations.

World.title: Kenya: Court Convicts All 29 Shakahola Accused of Murder, Sets Sentencing for November 6
World.content:
Mackenzie was among those convicted on all 191 counts of murder, alongside the other accused persons.

Nairobi — The High Court has convicted all 29 accused persons in the Shakahola starvation cult case linked to self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie, finding them guilty of the murder of 191 people, including 190 children.

The judge, Diana Kavedza, said the sentence would be delivered in open court on Friday, November 6, with the convicts to be physically produced in court.

In its judgment delivered on Monday, October 19, the court rejected the defence argument that the victims, all but one of whom were children below the age of 16, had voluntarily fasted to death.

"I am satisfied that the prosecution has proved the case against all the 29 accused persons for the murder of 190 children and one adult contrary to Section 203 of the Penal Code," the court ruled.



"I reject the defence by the accused persons that the victims, who were all below the age of 16 years, voluntarily fasted to death."

The court subsequently found all 29 accused guilty and convicted them under Section 322 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

Mackenzie was among those convicted on all 191 counts of murder, alongside the other accused persons. One of the accused pleaded guilty to all the counts and was convicted on his own plea, with sentencing pending.

The case stems from the Shakahola tragedy in Kilifi County, where followers of Mackenzie's Good News International Church are believed to have died after being subjected to extreme fasting practices.

The court directed the Probation and Aftercare Services to assign each convict an individual probation officer to prepare pre-sentence reports. It ordered that no probation officer should interview more than one convict.

The reports will be presented in court on October 30, after which the defence will make mitigation submissions ahead of sentencing.

The court also noted that it had received 68 victim impact statements from probation officers across the country. The judge said the statements had already been taken and would not be repeated, leaving mitigation as the remaining stage before sentencing.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe's Women Cotton Farmers Stitch More Value From Their White Gold
World.content:
Women cotton farmers in Zimbabwe’s Shamva district are turning to sewing and collective savings to diversify their incomes and adapt to a changing climate. Making school uniforms and taking clothing orders, they are creating earning opportunities beyond the crop they call their “white gold”.

For Brenda Dzuda, cotton is “white gold” that helps support her household in a community where, she says, women have few alternatives for earning a living.

But the 48-year-old widow who farms four hectares in Shamva, Mashonaland Central, says unpredictable weather, poor seed and disappointing prices are making it harder to realise the value in her gold.

“Shamva is a very dry region, and most men survive on illegal gold mining. But for us as women, cotton is our white gold,” she said.

Dzuda and other women farmers say cultural expectations and traditional restrictions limit their participation in mining. Cotton offers a way to earn, but increasingly, they are looking beyond the fields to sustain their households.

Through sewing and collective savings, women in Shamva are creating another source of income when harvests disappoint, or cotton payments arrive late.



When the Weather Becomes an Economic Burden

Across the fields, dry stalks remain where cotton plants once stood. The harvest has been packed into sacks, some already sold by farmers hoping to turn a season’s labour into household income.

But returns have not always matched expectations. Seed, fertiliser, chemicals and labour demand investment before farmers know what the harvest will bring. Unpredictable rainfall, prolonged dry spells and high temperatures add to the uncertainty.

“Cotton does not require much water, but the rains are no longer reliable. Sometimes they come earlier than expected or heavier, and sometimes the dry spells last longer than cotton can withstand. We are worried because our livelihoods depend on this crop,” said Dzuda.

Zimbabwe’s Meteorological Services Department had forecast an erratic start to the 2025–26 rainfall season, followed by improved rainfall prospects from December. For farmers such as Dzuda, the timing and distribution of rain shape planting decisions and crop development.

Dzuda said she was selling her cotton for US$0.24 a kilogram, questioning both the price and the quality of seed supplied to farmers.

“The money we are selling per kilogram versus the world market price is very upsetting. We are also not getting the best seed, then our cotton is sold as a third grade; then on the other side we are constantly attacked by the shift in weather patterns. This is a double blow for us,” she said.

For her, adapting means getting the crop through the season and earning enough to justify the investment. She also wants support for women to turn cotton into products beyond the raw crop.

“We had an exchange with women cotton farmers in Malawi, and they are doing value addition. As Zimbabwe Women in Cotton, we also wish to have backyard industries because in cotton we get toilet paper, cooking oil, stock feed and many others. We can do that on our own,” she said.

Seventy-four and Still Waiting

About 60 kilometres from Dzuda’s farming area, 74-year-old widow Getrude Motsi faces another part of the struggle.

At her home, sacks of harvested cotton remain stored, waiting to be sold. The crop represents months of work and money that could meet household needs or help finance another season.

“I have been growing cotton since 2014, and for the past seasons everything seemed to be going well; weather conditions are worsening, and the severity of it is the most scariest,” she said.

Motsi said delayed payments compounded the difficulties caused by the weather, weakening the economic security she had relied on cotton to provide.

Her experience shows how uncertainty can continue after the work in the fields is complete. A farmer must grow and protect the crop, harvest it, find a buyer and then receive payment.

Until then, the value of that work remains tied up in the cotton.

How Cotton is Priced and Paid For

Responding to farmers’ concerns about prices, grading and payments, the Cotton Company of Zimbabwe (COTTCO) said producer prices were benchmarked against international market fundamentals in consultation with regulators.

A company representative said cotton was graded from A to D based on fibre maturity, cleanliness, colour and trash content.

Farmers initially receive a base payment at the lowest grade, D, paid 70% in US dollars and 30% in Zimbabwe Gold, or ZiG. COTTCO said these initial payments had been made in full for the past season.

The company said it was completing laboratory grading and raising funds for additional payments to farmers whose cotton qualified for Grades A, B or C.

COTTCO also said it worked with the government’s Presidential Input Programme to provide subsidised seed, fertiliser, chemicals, herbicides and mechanised tillage services.

Addressing concerns about seed quality and weather risks, it said it supplied certified seed, including drought-tolerant, early-maturing varieties. Extension officers trained farmers in moisture conservation, input placement, weed control and integrated pest management.

For farmers, payment timing and the income remaining after production costs help determine whether they can support their households and plant again.

Another Way to Earn

Patience Zhakata, national chairperson of Zimbabwe Women in Cotton, said the restrictions women described around mining reflected wider questions about their ability to make economic decisions, own productive assets and control the proceeds of their labour.

“So as an organisation, cotton is white gold because that is the only field we can mine without restrictions,” she said.

Cotton has offered women a route into agricultural enterprise. Now, they are working to create income beyond the crop.

In 2022, the group approached Zimbabwe’s First Lady, Auxillia Mnangagwa, who assisted them with sewing machines, to which they started a sewing project in February 2023. Women are using the machines to make clothes and mend garments for people in their communities.

Close 

Happiness Marape, a trainer in the sewing project, said 60 women in Shamva participated, meeting on different days so everyone could use the machines.

“The initiative has 60 women in Shamva who meet weekly but on different days so that we all get access to the sewing machines. The sewing machines initiative came as an idea to counter climate shocks which are always attacking women, cotton farmers.”

The group takes orders for school uniforms and other garments, as well as repairs. Members also save together, creating a fund they can draw on for household needs and farming expenses.

“We also do savings as a group to assist each other financially or loan when we want to buy farming inputs,” Marape said.

The sewing work provides income beyond the agricultural season and another source of earnings when farming falls short.

“The sewing initiative is helping us a lot. When the fields fail to produce, we then rely on sewing, telling people that we work from cotton to the fabric. We get money from there and put it in our savings, and we all benefit,” she said.

Sewing does not resolve the problems of cotton prices, production costs, or delayed payments. But it gives the women another way to earn while they continue farming.

Back in Shamva, Dzuda’s description of cotton as women’s “white gold” still carries hope. For the women building savings from stitches as well as harvests, its value is measured in what their work can provide: money for their households and a way to begin the next season.

World.title: East Africa: Ghana Set to Overtake Ethiopia As Africa's Eighth-Largest Economy After Kenya Takes East Africa Lead
World.content:
Addis Abeba — Ghana is projected to overtake Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy in 2026, with its gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to reach US$128.64 billion, exceeding Ethiopia's projected US$127.15 billion by US$1.49 billion, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook (WEO), as reported by African Business Insider on 17 October.

The projected shift comes after Kenya overtook Ethiopia as East Africa's largest economy in nominal US dollar terms, marking another change in the continent's economic rankings driven partly by exchange-rate movements rather than differences in real economic growth.

The IMF's latest estimates place Ghana eighth among Africa's largest economies, ahead of Ethiopia in ninth place and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), whose economy is projected at US$122.28 billion. While Ghana's nominal GDP is expected to edge ahead of Ethiopia's, the two countries have markedly different growth forecasts.

Ethiopia's economy is projected to expand by 9.2% in real terms in 2026, compared with Ghana's forecast growth of 5.7%. However, the depreciation of the Ethiopian birr following the government's July 2024 foreign-exchange reforms has reduced the dollar value of the country's economic output, narrowing its position in nominal GDP rankings despite strong projected domestic growth.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Ghana's recovery and economic position

Ghana's projected rise comes as the West African country continues to recover from a severe financial crisis marked by currency depreciation, high inflation, mounting public debt and pressure on government finances.

In 2023, Ghana secured a US$3 billion IMF support programme aimed at restoring macroeconomic stability, addressing debt vulnerabilities and rebuilding investor confidence. The government subsequently pursued fiscal reforms, debt restructuring and measures to stabilise prices and the national currency.

The country's economic position is also supported by exports of gold, cocoa, oil and gas, alongside financial services and a growing consumer market. Gold remains a major source of export earnings and foreign exchange, with higher international prices providing additional support to inflows.

However, an improved position in nominal GDP rankings does not necessarily translate into higher living standards or stronger productive capacity. Sustaining the recovery will depend on Ghana's ability to attract long-term investment, create employment and expand industrial production.

Ethiopia's growth versus dollar-denominated output

Ethiopia's projected position reflects the distinction between real economic growth and nominal GDP measured in US dollars. While real GDP growth captures changes in domestic production after accounting for price changes, nominal GDP expressed in dollars is also affected by inflation and movements in the exchange rate.

The depreciation of the birr following Ethiopia's July 2024 shift toward a more market-determined foreign-exchange system substantially reduced the dollar valuation of its output. The reform formed part of the government's broader economic programme, supported by an approximately US$3.4 billion IMF Extended Credit Facility.

As Addis Standard reported last week, Kenya's emergence as East Africa's largest economy in dollar terms was similarly shaped by exchange-rate movements, with the comparatively stronger performance of the Kenyan shilling increasing the dollar value of its economic output.

The IMF's October projections indicate that Ethiopia's economy is expected to grow by 9.2% in 2026 and 7.8% in 2027, while Kenya's growth is forecast at 4.5% and 4.7%, respectively. The figures highlight how an economy can record faster real growth without maintaining a higher ranking when GDP is measured in US dollars.

The projected shift involving Ghana therefore does not, by itself, establish that its underlying economy is growing faster than Ethiopia's. Rather, it underscores the influence of exchange-rate movements and macroeconomic conditions on the relative dollar value of African economies.

Close 

The IMF projects Sub-Saharan Africa's economy to grow by 4.5% in both 2026 and 2027. However, its October WEO, titled Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices, warns that high debt-servicing costs, limited foreign-exchange reserves and declining aid are constraining governments' ability to respond to economic shocks.

For Ethiopia, the projected change in Africa's economic rankings highlights the challenge of sustaining rapid domestic growth while managing currency pressures, inflation and foreign-exchange constraints. For Ghana, moving ahead in nominal GDP terms would mark a recovery in its relative economic position, but translating that ranking into lasting gains in investment, employment and industrial development remains a separate challenge.

World.title: Tanzania: Anaesthesia Fears Delay Surgeries At Bugando
World.content:
Mwanza — FEAR of anaesthesia, fuelled by misconceptions about its safety, is among the challenges facing Bugando Zonal Referral Hospital, with some patients postponing or abandoning surgical procedures until their conditions become more complicated.

Head of the hospital's Anaesthesia Department, Dr Rebecca Shija, said initial assessments had identified misconceptions surrounding anaesthesia as one of the reasons some patients were reluctant to undergo surgery.

Speaking during the commemoration of World Anaesthesia Day at the hospital yesterday, Dr Shija said some people wrongly believed that anaesthesia was equivalent to half-death, creating unnecessary fear about undergoing surgical procedures.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

She said others feared that spinal anaesthesia, which involves administering medication into the fluid-filled space surrounding the spinal cord, could cause permanent back pain.

"These misconceptions have made some patients avoid surgery, with others returning for treatment only when their conditions have advanced, making their recovery more difficult to predict," she said. Dr Shija added that some patients abandoned the process altogether and never returned to the hospital for the recommended procedures.

To address the challenge, she said Bugando was intensifying public education to explain the role of anaesthesia in surgery and reassure patients about the safety measures used by trained specialists.

She emphasised that modern equipment, qualified personnel and careful monitoring were essential components of safe anaesthesia services.

"Medical teams monitor patients before, during and after surgery to assess their condition and identify potential complications, allowing them to respond promptly, when necessary," she said.

Dr Shija further said patients with serious non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, cancer, kidney disease and heart conditions, required careful assessment before anaesthesia and surgery to identify risks and determine appropriate management.

She also called on stakeholders to support government efforts to increase the number of anaesthesia specialists at the hospital, saying the department needed to expand its workforce to meet growing demand.

According to Dr Shija, the hospital's anaesthesia services handled at least 500 patients a week, while the department had six specialists, highlighting the need for additional trained personnel.

She said Bugando was also working with stakeholders to strengthen the capacity of healthcare providers in other hospitals across the Lake Zone, particularly in the use of modern anaesthesia machines and related medical equipment.

The initiative aims to improve the quality of anaesthesia services and bring appropriate care closer to communities outside major referral centres.

Close 

Dr Shija further proposed the introduction of degree programmes in anaesthesia at the Catholic University of Health and Allied Sciences (CUHAS) in Mwanza as part of efforts to address the shortage of specialists.

Bugando Director General, Dr Alicia Massenga, thanked the government for supporting improvements at the hospital, including the provision of modern medical equipment and medicines, as well as sponsorship for staff training to strengthen their anaesthesia skills.

Dr Massenga said the hospital had five anaesthesia specialists and 46 non-physician anaesthesia providers, underscoring the importance of continued investment in the workforce.

"The commemoration served as a reminder to the public of the critical role anaesthesia plays in surgical care. Safe surgery depends on safe anaesthesia," she said.

World.title: Ghana: Mahama Explains Ghana's BRICS Move
World.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has said Ghana's decision to seek partnership with the BRICS countries is part of efforts to broaden its development partnerships and deepen South-South cooperation.

He gave the explanation when he swore in four envoys at the Presidency in Accra last Friday, charging them to clearly explain the country's approach to international engagement and attract investments to support national development.

"Explain this approach clearly as we seek wider opportunities for trade, investment, industrialisation, and value addition, while sustaining our long-standing relationships and working relations with our traditional partners," he said.

The new envoys are Nana Antwiwaa Dodoo, Ambassador to Angola; Louis Kwame Obeng, Ambassador to Qatar; Evelyn Korantemaa Ofosu-Amable, Ambassador to Israel; and Jedidiah Reuben Adogla, Ghana's Permanent Representative to Switzerland.

World.title: Nigeria: Dangote Group Didn't Advertise Thousands of Jobs At Kenyan Refinery - Ads Circulating On Facebook Fake
World.content:
Dangote Group didn't advertise thousands of jobs at Kenyan refinery - ads circulating on Facebook fake

IN SHORT: Job ads circulating on Facebook claim Dangote Group is recruiting thousands of workers for its planned refinery in Lamu, Kenya. But be warned: the advertised vacancies don't appear on the company's official careers portal, and the ads direct applicants to unverified email addresses.

On 30 September 2026, construction of the Dangote oil refinery began in Lamu county, northeastern Kenya, as Kenyan president William Ruto and Dangote Group founder Aiko Dangote broke ground.

The refinery is expected to process 700,000 barrels of crude oil per day and create thousands of jobs, making recruitment claims bearing the Dangote name particularly attractive to job seekers in Kenya.



In this context, an advert started circulating on Facebook, claiming that Dangote Group had thousands of vacancies for the Lamu plant.

The listed positions include 412 electricians, 221 plumbers, 750 brick masons, 142 iron workers, 110 carpenters, 179 tile setters/flooring installers, 65 excavator/equipment operators, 157 welders, and 1,870 general labourers.

It asks interested users to send applications to the provided email address by 14 October 2026 and warns them to apply for only one position, saying multiple applications will result in disqualification.

This job ad and a similar version have also been posted here, here, here, here and here.

But can they be trusted? We checked.

Fake job ad

We searched Dangote Group's official careers portal, as well as its Facebook and X accounts, but found no announcement confirming the advertised vacancies.

The adverts direct applicants to email addresses that do not match the official Dangote Group email domain, @dangote.com. One lists an Outlook address, while the other provides a Gmail address. They also don't link to the company's recruitment portal. These are major red flags.

The adverts also provide limited information about the vacancies. Although they list numerous positions across different departments, they lack detailed job descriptions and responsibilities. Some posts don't even specify the application deadline.

All signs point to fake job adverts using the group's name.

Remember, do not send your personal or banking information to unverified email addresses. Follow official channels for genuine vacancies.

World.title: Africa: A New SAPS Oath Could Help Restore Police Pride and Public Trust
World.content:
analysis

Building a professional police identity based on a strong ethical commitment is as important as discipline and accountability.

There is no question that the South African Police Service (SAPS) is in trouble. Whether measured by low public trust or the evidence of organised criminal infiltration presented to the Madlanga Commission, it is clear that serious steps must be taken to turn the SAPS into a trusted, credible police service. But what should these steps be?

A critical issue is police integrity. Many reforms currently envisaged involve subjecting members to greater scrutiny in order to expose those involved in wrongdoing and remove criminally oriented staff.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia's 'police reset agenda' includes measures to improve the SAPS disciplinary system and encourage the reporting of crime committed by members. Those convicted of offences involving dishonesty, corruption or violent crime, including rape, should face mandatory dismissal, he said.

The Madlanga Commission report, to be submitted to President Cyril Ramaphosa in January 2027, will likely also call for stronger scrutiny of SAPS personnel through better vetting, financial disclosures and lifestyle audits.

Cachalia says the main purpose of the reset agenda is to 'build a disciplined, professional and ethical police service that commands public confidence and supports honest police officers in carrying out their duties effectively.'

Considering the current allegations it faces, turning the SAPS into a trusted and respected service requires engagement with the foundations of policing. As much as it needs more scrutiny, the SAPS - and members of metro and other policing formations - also need strong moral leadership.

The SAPS Code of Conduct was adopted in 1997, making it nearly 30 years old and out of date. In its 2024 report on strengthening policing in South Africa, the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) recommended measures to build 'a more positive and professional police identity' that restores pride in wearing the SAPS insignia and uniform. The ISS said 'building greater self-respect within the SAPS' was an 'essential element of building public trust in the SAPS.'

The ISS motivated for 'a succinct new SAPS oath or declaration' to which members should commit. This should convey core principles that are meaningful to honest police officers. It should be clear that only police who are true to these principles are worthy of wearing the SAPS uniform and badge.

The International Association of Chiefs of Police model Code of Ethics emphasises a similar point. It requires officers to recognise that only if they are 'true to the ethics of police service' should they be entitled to wear the badge.

How a new oath or declaration is written may be as important as what it says. It should be concise and easy to understand. Police codes of conduct often refer vaguely to upholding the law. An exception is the 74-word statement of ethical policing principles published by Britain's College of Policing, which foregrounds courage, respect, empathy and public service.

Alongside the 1997 Code of Conduct, the SAPS Code of Ethics, first published in 2011, should also be interrogated. For instance, it narrows down the principle of respect to respect for diversity. Britain's College of Policing, by contrast, defines respect more broadly, linking it to empathy. It calls for police to understand the views of others and 'recognise and respond to the physical, mental and emotional challenges that we and other people may face.'

This is not to say that South Africa should replicate codes adopted in other countries. The ISS recommended that the new oath or declaration emphasise 'dignity and respect.' SAPS members should conduct themselves, it said, 'in a manner that is based on treating members of the public with respect, and that promotes respect for the SAPS.'

Building respect for the SAPS is connected to questions of integrity. The British College of Policing embeds integrity in an ethic of 'courage' that asks police to be accountable for decisions and stand 'against anything that could bring our profession into disrepute.'

In South African policing, courage and integrity are also intertwined. The physical courage required to help people in danger must be combined with the moral courage to withstand pressure from corrupt colleagues to stay silent about their wrongdoing.

Studies show that police often see loyalty to colleagues as a moral duty. But the positive solidarity involved in defending colleagues who are in danger must be distinguished from the unethical solidarity of the code of silence that conceals police criminality. Recognising that providing support to colleagues is fundamental to policing, ISS recommended that police commit to 'support their colleagues, but not at the expense of professional policing standards.'

Close 

Ideally, supporting colleagues should include being attentive to other situations in which police need help, considering that officers face a high risk of stress-related mental and physical ill-health. The duty of care that SAPS members carry towards the public should also extend to their colleagues and themselves.

A new oath will work best if used by police commanders in their day-to-day engagement with officers. It will not get corrupt and dishonest police to change their ways. But it can help honourable members embed the ethics of policing within the work, and reputation, of the SAPS. Rather than a burdensome obligation, a well-considered, concise new code can inspire police to uphold high standards.

Honest, committed officers are the most important asset that South Africa has for building an honourable and trusted SAPS. To win public respect, the SAPS should help such members maintain clarity about the standards they must uphold.

For permission to re-publish ISS Today articles, please email us. In South Africa, News24 has exclusive rights to republish ISS Today articles. In Nigeria, Premium Times has exclusive rights to republish ISS Today articles.

David Bruce, Independent Researcher and ISS Consultant

World.content:
A professional python hunter who doubles as a professional alligator wrestler, according to his Instagram bio, helped catch "the longest live captured reticulated python ever caught in Puerto Rico."

This gigantic snake was held up by eight people standing shoulder-to-shoulder to show just how big of a snake they're dealing with. They tracked it down after it was "spotted strangling a pet cat behind a house."

EVA SHOCKEY SAYS SHE RECEIVED 'THOUSANDS AND THOUSANDS' OF DEATH THREATS FROM ANTI-HUNTING ACTIVISTS

World.title: Lung cancer can grow silently for years, here’s who qualifies for screening
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Cancer can strike at any age, often without symptoms. For many cancers, routine screening remains the best way to detect the disease early and reduce the risk of death.

For lung cancer, screening guidelines can vary, as the disease doesn’t always show obvious signals and can occur in both smokers and never-smokers.

Daniel J. Boffa, M.D., chair of the American College of Surgeons Commission on Cancer and a thoracic surgeon at Yale University, noted that lung cancer screening is "one of the most powerful ways" to boost survival.

POPE LEO'S LUNG TUMOR RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT CANCER RISK FOR NONSMOKERS

"It reduces the chance of people dying of lung cancer by 20%," he told Fox News Digital.

The share of Americans who are eligible for screening but don’t comply translates to "tens of thousands of preventable deaths every year," according to Boffa.

"I'm hoping that within four or five years, a screening CT scan will only be confirmatory after they have a positive blood test done at your doctor's office," he added.

That approach could make screening easier and potentially help detect more lung cancers, according to the doctor.

Potential symptoms

In a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Lary Robinson, M.D., an oncologist at Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida, noted that in most cases, early-stage lung cancer will not come with any symptoms.

In those who do have symptoms, however, the most common are related to the lungs, including a persistent cough, shortness of breath or coughing up blood.

DOCTORS PUSH NEW BLOOD TESTS FOR COLON CANCER AS CASES SURGE IN YOUNGER ADULTS

Unexplained weight loss can result from any form of cancer, according to the oncologist. Neurological symptoms, like persistent headaches, may also warrant seeing a doctor.

Current guidelines

Current lung cancer screening guidelines recommend an annual low-dose CT scan for people between the ages of 50 and 80 who currently smoke or have a history of smoking or have at least a 20 pack-year history of smoking, according to the American Cancer Society (ACS).

Before making the decision to get screened, individuals should speak with their healthcare providers about the purpose of the screening and how it’s done, as well as the benefits, limits and possible harms, ACS advised.

Those who still smoke should be counseled about quitting and offered interventions and resources to help.

Individuals with serious health problems that will "likely limit" their lifespan should not be screened, according to ACS, as well as those who won’t be able to get treatment if lung cancer is detected.

NEVER SMOKED A CIGARETTE? YOU COULD STILL BE AT HIGHER RISK FOR LUNG CANCER

Although one out of seven lung cancers will affect someone who has never smoked, there is currently not a set screening guideline for never-smokers.

Finding individuals who would benefit from screening is an "intense area of research," according to Boffa. For now, people with a direct family history of lung cancer without smoking should consider annual screenings, as should higher-risk demographics like Asian women.

"I would anticipate that in the next year or two, we will have better guidance for people who are at risk for lung cancer, but never smoked," Boffa predicted.

What to expect

Boffa noted that advances in lung cancer treatment have improved survival, even at advanced stages, so screening should not be viewed as a pathway to a terminal diagnosis.

CLICK HERE TO 

"People are really reluctant to be diagnosed with lung cancer because it does carry a stigma," Boffa said. "For years, there was a reputation that it was a terminal diagnosis. It's just been amazing what research has done for lung cancer."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Most screenings detect a lung nodule or other abnormality, which is more often an infection, scar or inflammation than a tumor, he said.

In about one-third of patients, lung cancer screenings also detect unrelated health issues, including the hardening of heart arteries or a nodule in another part of the body.

"The reality is over 99% of nodules are actually benign," Boffa said. "And so, you need to have a conversation about what you are going to do with that information."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I think having that conversation ahead of time is really important so that expectations are set – it's not uncommon to find something. Most of the time, it's not something that's going to affect how long you live."

The doctor noted that the CT scan only takes a couple of minutes to perform and does not take place in an enclosed space like an MRI.

"People who get claustrophobic usually don't have a hard time with lung cancer screening," Boffa said. "And it usually takes a few days to get a report back."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For those who are over 50 with a history of smoking, Boffa reiterated that getting screened is "one of the most powerful things you can do to reduce your chances of having your life shortened by lung cancer."

World.title: Calgary Opera removes singer waving Palestinian flag during opening night curtain call
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Calgary Opera removed a cast member from its remaining performances of "Tosca" after he displayed a Palestinian flag during the opera's opening-night curtain call Friday.

Bass-baritone singer Gabriel Sanchez-Ortega pulled out the flag during the curtain call following the opening-night performance. The opera company later released a statement calling Sanchez-Ortega's actions "unexpected and unauthorized," confirming that he would be replaced for the remaining performances.

"Individual political protest contravenes not only company policy, but also our responsibility to create a more connected, caring, and civil society through shared artistic experience," the statement read, according to OperaWire. "We recognize that this moment may have affected the audience — as well as cast members, crew, orchestral musicians, and Jubilee staff — in different ways, and we regret any discomfort and distress it caused."

AUSTRALIAN POLICE INVESTIGATING PRO-PALESTINIAN RALLY IN SYDNEY WHERE PROTESTORS CHANTED ‘GAS THE JEWS’

"We have addressed this matter directly with the cast member and reinforced our expectations with the cast and production team," the statement continued. "Our commitment is to provide a welcoming and respectful environment for our artists, audiences, and community. The role of Angelotti will be performed by another artist for the remaining performances. We thank everyone who joined us for opening night and look forward to welcoming audiences to the remaining performances of ‘Tosca.'"

Sanchez-Ortega, who posted a video of himself holding the flag on Instagram, released a statement saying he has "no regret" over his actions and claimed that Calgary Opera was faced with "financial threats" over the move.

"I have been informed that I have been removed from further performances of ‘Tosca’ with the Calgary Opera following my display of the Palestinian flag during curtain call. I have no regret," he said.

"This is the state of cultural institutions in Canada," Sanchez-Ortega wrote on social media. "I was informed that financial threats had been made against Calgary Opera. I hold no resentment. After the theatre, (political or otherwise) we all have to go home, and look at ourselves in the mirror. It was my honor to play the role of Angelotti, an escaped political prisoner."

MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Calgary Opera declined to comment on "personnel matters" but added that all forms of personal protest, regardless of the political symbol, are prohibited on stage.

"Calgary Opera prohibits personal protest on our stages and at our events," it said. "The display of any protest symbol or action would result in similar consequences. We have reiterated this prohibition to all artists and staff, and will continue to apply it universally in response to all cases of unauthorized protest, regardless of the symbol or action that protest takes."

"With respect to the cast member in question, he did not appear in yesterday’s performance of Tosca, and will not appear in the October 24, 2026, closing performance," the statement added. "Beyond that, Calgary Opera does not comment on personnel matters."

GORILLAZ FRONTMAN DAMON ALBARN HOLDS UP PALESTINIAN FLAG DURING SHOW AFTER MACKLEMORE TOUR REMOVAL

World.title: NFL suspends Buffalo Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson after grotesque spitting incident
World.content:
The NFL announced on Monday that they have suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game, without pay, after he spit at Las Vegas Raiders' Brock Bowers on Sunday. Officials ejected Gardner-Johnson for spitting at the Raiders tight end late in the second quarter.

BILLS CORNERBACK DISMISSES EFTON CHISM'S MIRACULOUS ONE-HANDED TOUCHDOWN: 'PROBABLY WON'T HEAR FROM HIM AGAIN'

Referees immediately flagged Gardner-Johnson for unsportsmanlike conduct and sent him to the lockers at Allegiant Stadium early.

The penalty positioned the Raiders comfortably down the field before halftime, allowing Las Vegas to boot a field goal and tie the game going into the break. The Bills ultimately held on to win the game, 33-30.

Following the game, Gardner-Johnson issued an apology on social media.

NFL REFS HAVE SET ALL-TIME RECORD FOR FLAGS THIS SEASON, AND IT'S CHANGING THE OUTCOME OF GAMES

"The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game," Gardner-Johnson posted on his Instagram stories.

"There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability," the statement read in part. "No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard."

Gardner-Johnson being a problem for his team is frankly nothing new.

Just last season, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter was slapped with a $57,222 fine and stripped of a game check after spitting on Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott during Week 1.

THREE COWBOYS PLAYERS FINED MORE THAN $33,000 COMBINED AFTER SEASON-OPENING LOSS TO GIANTS

Back in 2020, his own New Orleans Saints teammate Michael Thomas punched him during practice after Gardner-Johnson reportedly provoked him. Later that season, Chicago Bears receiver Javon Wims threw a right hook at him during a live game after Gardner-Johnson ripped Wims' mouthpiece off his helmet. The following year, another Bears receiver, Anthony Miller, was ejected for throwing a punch at Gardner-Johnson during a playoff game.

Whether he is suiting up for the Saints, Eagles, Lions, or Bills, Gardner-Johnson's conduct remains exactly the same. He will now miss Buffalo's upcoming game against the Baltimore Ravens simply because he could not act like an adult on the field.

World.title: Amanda Seyfried faces harsh criticism as viewers rip her behavior in Elizabeth Holmes documentary
World.content:

Amanda Seyfried landed in the hot seat after her appearance in the latest Elizabeth Holmes documentary unleashed a wave of criticism online.

Seyfried surprised viewers when she appeared alongside Nathan Fielder in "You Can See Everything," a documentary that followed Holmes in the last 34 days leading up to the start of her prison sentence. Holmes reported to Federal Prison Camp Bryan on May 30, 2023.

Seyfried revisited her connection to the disgraced Theranos founder, whom she portrayed in Hulu's "The Dropout." The new documentary, released Oct. 16, explored Seyfried's evolving perspective on Holmes, including her reactions to Holmes' personal life and relationship with Billy Evans. Stepping back into Holmes' shoes for the documentary, Seyfried helped Fielder recreate conversations he had with the disgraced Theranos founder after she reported to prison.

Throughout the film, Seyfried grappled with her growing sympathy for Holmes, even as the convicted fraudster challenged the way the actress portrayed her in the Hulu series.

'YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING' REVIEW: THE BUZZY ELIZABETH HOLMES DOCUMENTARY IS WORTH THE HYPE

"Amanda Seyfried defending Holmes as a victim of male manipulation until Holmes accused her of participating in a sensationalized version of the Theranos scandal and then flipping out about how it is just TV was a [sic] truly gross," one X user wrote. "I hope she gets redragged for it."

Other viewers piled on, accusing Seyfried of changing her tune when the scrutiny shifted toward her own role in bringing the Theranos scandal to television.

"Lots of 'women protecting women' posturing from her until she gets accused of perhaps also causing Elizabeth some degree of pain, after which she immediately deflects and starts engaging in female emotional manipulation by accusing Nathan of covering up for Elizabeth based on her 'intuition,'" another user said.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Another viewer echoed the criticism, arguing that Seyfried's behavior only reinforced their negative impression of the actress.

"This is maybe the number one reason why I loved 'You Can See Everything.' Seeing Amanda Seyfried for her true colors in full hypocrisy was such a cathartic feeling," one user said. "It reminds me why we should never take people like her seriously."

Not everyone agreed with the harsh criticism. Some viewers came to Seyfried's defense, arguing that her changing opinion of Holmes wasn't a sign of hypocrisy but rather an essential part of the documentary's larger message.

"imagine walking away from this blaming amanda seyfried," a user wrote. "the point is, amanda herself changes her opinion on elizabeth holmes. so does nathan fielder. so does the audience. thats the literal point."

Another added, "At no point in the movie does Elizabeth Holmes reckon with how anyone other than her was harmed by the downfall of Theranos. Amanda Seyfried earnestly reckons with the consequences of her actions even when she is (correctly) pretty sure she didn't do anything wrong."

Fox News Digital reached out to Seyfried's representative for comment.

Holmes was convicted in January 2022 on four federal fraud charges for misleading investors about her blood-testing company's technology and capabilities. A jury found her guilty of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and three counts of wire fraud, all related to defrauding investors.

She was sentenced in November 2022 to 11 years and three months in federal prison.

"You Can See Everything" examined Holmes' efforts to reclaim control of her public image after the spectacular collapse of Theranos, the blood-testing company she founded. As she prepared to begin her prison sentence, Holmes confronted the fallout from her fraud conviction, the intense scrutiny surrounding her personal life and the Hollywood portrayal of her downfall.

The film offered a closer look at the disgraced entrepreneur's attempts to navigate life beyond the scandal that destroyed her reputation, while exploring the complicated divide between how Holmes viewed herself and how the public perceived her.

World.title: Veteran CNN anchor Christiane Amanpour announces exit from network, will go off the air next June
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Veteran CNN International anchor Christiane Amanpour announced Monday she's leaving the network next summer after more than four decades at the network.

"After more than 43 years at CNN, Christiane has decided that the time is right to begin a new chapter," CNN CEO Mark Thompson told staffers in a memo. "Early in 2027, she will scale back her CNN International show, ‘Amanpour,’ to once a week. The program will conclude in May, and she will leave CNN at the end of June."

"Christiane has thought carefully about this decision, and she and I have been discussing it for some months. Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I’m very sorry to see her go, but I’ve come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally," Thompson wrote.

CHRISTIANE AMANPOUR POINTS TO 'HEMORRHAGING' AT CBS TO WARN OF DAVID ELLISON'S POTENTIAL TAKEOVER AT CNN

Amanpour thanked her viewers and alluded to the "pressures" she and her CNN colleagues face during an on-air address.

"Now, you know I've always been fiercely independent, and I will continue to be that for you for as long as I am here and beyond," Amanpour said. "That's especially important today as we face unprecedented pressures from all sides, political, financial and also from the rising dangers in the field. I'll always be rooting for CNN maintaining its history of independent journalism."

"Remember: always be truthful, not neutral," she also said in a written statement.

NEW CNN BOSS MARK THOMPSON SUPPORTIVE OF CHRISTIANE AMANPOUR AS LEFT-WING ANCHOR LAUNCHES WEEKEND SHOW

The announcement came as a shock to CNN staffers. One called her CNN's "reigning titan." Another described themselves as a "Christiane loyalist" and called her "the heart and soul of this company," but admitted her stature in journalism can continue without CNN.

"She has the power to chart her own course. Yes, she is synonymous with a brand, but she is also a bigger than the brand," the CNN staffer told Fox News Digital.

While the 68-year-old journalist is revered among her CNN colleagues and members of the liberal media, she has her critics as well. As she referenced in her statement, Amanpour rejects the notion of neutrality when it comes to reporting, insisting the truth should remain the north star.

"Both-siderism — on the one hand, on the other hand — is not always objectivity. It does not get you to the truth," Amanpour told graduates at the Columbia Journalism School in 2023. "Drawing false, moral or factual equivalence is neither objective or truthful. Objectivity is our golden rule. And it is in weighing all the sides and all the evidence hearing everyone reporting everything, but not rushing to equate them when there is no equating and look at the damage that that has done in the climate debate, in the political arena and in the field of battle."

CNN'S CHRISTIANE AMANPOUR CALLS OUT BOSS CHRIS LICHT, OFFERS STUNNING REBUKE OF TRUMP TOWN HALL

Her coverage of the Israel-Hamas war and her past commentary have also raised eyebrows. Amanpour claimed in October 2023, just weeks after the terrorist attack on Israel, "the rest of the world" agreed with Jordanian Queen Rania Al Abdullah's complaint that the Western world shows more support for Israel than the Palestinians. She also reported that third-party negotiators were trying to implement a "hostage release on both sides," implying Israel, too, is keeping civilian hostages and not just the Hamas terrorists. Earlier in the year, she was forced to apologize after she claimed the murder of an Israeli rabbi's family was the result of a "shootout."

In November 2020, she was condemned by the Israeli government and the Anti-Defamation League for comparing the Trump presidency to Kristallnacht, known as the "Night of Broken Glass" when Nazis terrorized Jews throughout Germany and Austria, resulting in at least 91 deaths and 7,500 Jewish businesses vandalized during the Holocaust. Amanpour walked back her comments following the intense backlash.

Amanpour's forthcoming exit from CNN marks the first major journalist set to leave the network under its new corporate ownership. Skydance CEO and Paramount owner David Ellison recently closed on his $111 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, merging two legacy Hollywood studios as well as several television networks including CNN and CBS under Skydance.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

While there's been no indication her decision was tied to Ellison's takeover of the network, Amanpour isn't shy to publicly challenge her bosses, most notably Thompson's predecessor Chris Licht, for airing the now-infamous Trump town hall in 2023. Earlier this year, Amanpour expressed concern about Ellison owning CNN over how he's handled CBS News since he bought Paramount and installed Bari Weiss as its editor-in-chief.

"I’m concerned based on what’s happened to the other things that he’s taken over already, like CBS News, right?" Amanpour said in May. "I mean, do I have to list what’s happening there? I mean, hemorrhaging viewers, probably hemorrhaging money, this ideological realignment of CBS and the destruction, potentially, of ‘60 Minutes.’"

MAN ARRESTED AT TRUMP GOLF COURSE AHEAD OF PRESIDENT’S VISIT ALLEGEDLY HAD WEAPONS CACHE

World.title: Texas Democratic candidate for governor sues to review emails between Elon Musk and Greg Abbott
World.content:
Texas state Rep. Gina Hinojosa, the Democratic nominee for governor, announced a lawsuit Monday against Gov. Greg Abbott over emails between his office and Republican ally Elon Musk.

Hinojosa — who is challenging Abbott in a tight contest — said at a news conference that she filed the suit to obtain redacted documents that “Abbott refused to release,” claiming they were being withheld because they are “intimate and embarrassing.”

A spokesperson for Abbott called the lawsuit “baseless” and “nothing more than an act of desperation.”

“Even worse, State Representative Gina Hinojosa is abusing her official capacity as an outgoing lawmaker to generate headlines for political purposes,” Abbott’s press secretary, Andrew Mahaleris, said in a statement. “Texans see this for what it is: a political stunt.”

Musk, who is CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Hinojosa’s lawsuit alleges the “documented connections between Abbott and Musk are extensive,” including “personal interactions, joint public appearances, large political contributions, economic-development incentives, and public praise for one another.”

She claims that Abbott and Musk speak “frequently” and that Musk has “contributed approximately $366 million to Republicans and Republican-supported PACs,” including “large amounts, directly and indirectly, to help Abbott.” It also details the millions of grant dollars given to SpaceX for its operations in Texas, Musk’s home state.

Musk in recent months has donated about $250 million to Republican groups, much of it finding its way into Texas races.

Hinojosa filed a public information request last month for inspection of all documents exchanged between Abbott’s office and Musk and his companies.

In a Sept. 29 letter addressed to the governor’s office, she said the people of Texas are “concerned over the growing power of tech giants in Texas regarding our tax dollars, resources, and data.”

Her request followed the release of nearly 1,400 pages of records to The Texas Newsroom, detailed in its 2025 reporting. However, “all but about 200 were redacted or completely blacked out,” according to Monday’s lawsuit.

Abbott’s office responded to Hinojosa’s request for the records last Tuesday but “refused to release the unredacted versions,” according to court documents.

“Quite simply, Governor Abbott has failed and refused to comply with the law by allowing Representative Hinojosa access to the Abbott-Musk communications,” the lawsuit reads.

Hinojosa’s attorney, Cris Feldman, said the governor’s office “has continued to obstruct her ability to review these intimate and embarrassing emails, despite clear statutory language.”

In an affidavit, Hinojosa said she seeks the records for “legislative purposes.”

She said at the news conference, “The people have a right to know, and I, as their representative, have a right to see them.”

Early voting began in Texas on Monday. Hinojosa said she has already cast her ballot.
