US calls at the UN for an end to the Decolonisation Committee, key to Argentina’s claim

19th Monday, October 2026 - 19:50 UTC Full article

The Argentine government has not commented on the US position, which contrasts with the close alliance between Milei and President Donald Trump

The United States has called at the UN for an end to the mandate of the Special Committee on Decolonisation, the body before which Argentina presents its sovereignty claim over the Falklands every year, and described some of its activities as “a waste of resources”, according to the official summary of the General Assembly Fourth Committee session held on October 15.

The committee approved more than 20 draft resolutions that day, many of them recommended by the Special Committee, “even as the representative of the United States called for an end to that body’s mandate”, according to the UN statement. Washington has not tabled a formal proposal to dissolve it, which could only be approved by the General Assembly, where there is no veto and the committee enjoys the support of a broad majority of states.

The committee, created in 1961, reviews each year the situation of 17 non-self-governing territories, ten of them administered by the United Kingdom, including the South Atlantic archipelago. Successive foreign ministers under Javier Milei’s government have attended its June sessions to call for the resumption of sovereignty negotiations; the current one, Pablo Quirno, did so on June 25. The United Kingdom maintains that the islanders have the right to self-determination and that in the 2013 referendum they chose to keep their status as a British overseas territory.

The Argentine government has not commented on the US position, which contrasts with the close alliance between Milei and President Donald Trump. According to the newspaper Infobae, the issue could be raised during this week’s visit to Buenos Aires by Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau and Assistant Secretary for Western Hemisphere Affairs Juan Pablo Segura.

At the same session, Argentina abstained on a Russian-backed resolution on contemporary forms of colonialism. At the General Assembly in September, Milei had described the islands question as “a national cause” and called for Resolution 31/49, which urges the parties not to introduce unilateral changes while the dispute persists, to have consequences.

World.title: Argentina spent US$445 million on weapons and military equipment under Milei
World.content:
Argentina spent US$445 million on weapons and military equipment under Milei

19th Monday, October 2026 - 19:46 UTC Full article

The largest acquisition was 24 F-16 fighters from Denmark, agreed in April 2024 for US$301.2 million payable in five annual instalments

Argentina’s government spent some US$445 million on weapons, military and security equipment from when Javier Milei took office in December 2023 to August 2026, according to an analysis by the newspaper Infobae based on the state’s official procurement system and agreements signed with other countries. The figure already exceeds what was invested during the full terms of Alberto Fernández and Mauricio Macri.

Of the total, US$381.4 million went to the armed forces and US$63.7 million to federal security forces. Spending was concentrated in 2024, at US$357.8 million, against US$59.4 million in 2025 and US$27.8 million in the first seven months of this year. The calculation excludes salaries and running costs and converts peso purchases at each year’s average dollar rate.

The largest acquisition was 24 F-16 fighters from Denmark, agreed in April 2024 for US$301.2 million payable in five annual instalments. The first six aircraft arrived in December 2025 and another six in September; the Air Force expects the remaining twelve could arrive before December 2027. The F-16s restore to Argentina a supersonic combat capability it lost in 2015 with the retirement of its Mirages. The United Kingdom has in the past blocked sales to Argentina of aircraft with British components.

The government also bought eight Stryker armoured vehicles from the United States for US$20 million, with a letter of intent to acquire up to 235, and 48 Unimog trucks. Some of the equipment received under this administration was contracted by the previous government, such as four P-3 Orion maritime patrol aircraft bought from Norway for US$60 million and six Bell helicopters.

“Argentina needs armed forces with greater capabilities, readiness and resources to defend its sovereignty and strategic interests,” said Defence Minister Carlos Presti. According to the analysis, spending on these items under Fernández totalled US$428.7 million, and under Macri, US$72 million.

World.title: Lula asks Bolsonaro whether he will wield “Milei’s chainsaw” in a heated debate
World.content:
Lula asks Bolsonaro whether he will wield “Milei’s chainsaw” in a heated debate

19th Monday, October 2026 - 06:15 UTC Full article

The face-off, lasting more than two hours, was held at the headquarters of the Band network in São Paulo and was the first of the campaign: neither candidate had attended the first-round debates

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva asked his rival, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, on Sunday whether he intends to apply Argentine President Javier Milei’s “chainsaw” to cut 250 billion reais in public spending, during a first televised debate marked by mutual accusations of corruption, a week before the October 25 runoff.

The face-off, lasting more than two hours, was held at the headquarters of the Band network in São Paulo and was the first of the campaign: neither candidate had attended the first-round debates. Bolsonaro, of the Liberal Party, opened with attacks over an alleged influence-peddling case involving the president’s eldest son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, based on an interview given the previous day to CNN Brasil by a lobbyist implicated in the matter. Lula responded by pointing to investigations into his rival, including one linked to the Banco Master case.

Besides the spending cuts plan, Lula asked Bolsonaro whether he would hand Brazil’s natural resources to the United States, to which he accused him and his family of being “subservient”, and accused him of planning to privatise the state oil company Petrobras. Bolsonaro focused much of his time on security. Asked about sovereignty, he spoke of Brazilians’ “loss of sovereignty” in neighbourhoods controlled by drug trafficking: “The streets will be ours again and not those criminals’.” He reiterated his proposal to create a Ministry of Prosperity and urged voters to vote “without fear”.

The debate ended with a disturbance in the audience that forced the moderator to intervene as Lula began his closing statement.

Polls show a statistical tie, with a slight edge for Bolsonaro, who won the first round with 47.03% of the vote against Lula’s 45.16%. The two will face each other again on Friday 23 on TV Globo, two days before the vote.

World.title: Rioting returns to Paris after a day of protests that saw 1,800 arrests across France
World.content:
Rioting returns to Paris after a day of protests that saw 1,800 arrests across France

19th Monday, October 2026 - 06:13 UTC Full article

From early afternoon, groups built barricades from burning rental bicycles in the streets around the square and looted some shops, while police responded with tear gas

Clashes between police and groups of protesters returned to central Paris on Sunday around the Place de la République, a day after a nationwide day of protests against the cost of living and conditions in schools ended with the looting of hundreds of shops and at least 1,800 arrests across the country, according to police.

From early afternoon, groups built barricades from burning rental bicycles in the streets around the square and looted some shops, while police responded with tear gas. There were similar scenes in Lyon. President Emmanuel Macron convened a crisis meeting and is due to address the nation.

On Saturday, some 550,000 people took part in 110 marches across the country, according to the Interior Ministry; organisers put the figure at 800,000. The day was called by trade unions, student organisations and former members of the “yellow vest” movement. There were 855 arrests in the Paris region, and looting was reported in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Bordeaux. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez defended the right to protest but said that “deliberately and collectively sowing disorder through violence” is not.

The protests began in mid-September at a high school in Créteil, on the outskirts of Paris, where pupils protested over dilapidated buildings, overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages, and spread across the country. Human rights organisations have denounced a disproportionate use of force against minors, who make up most of those arrested since then.

Far-right leader Marine Le Pen blamed the violence on left-wing leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who took part in the Paris march. Her party’s president, Jordan Bardella, said that “order no longer exists in this country”.

World.title: US fears Falklands-related sanctions could hit American companies
World.content:
US fears Falklands-related sanctions could hit American companies

18th Sunday, October 2026 - 21:56 UTC Full article

According to Clarín, Washington has put forward two options: freezing the bill, its preferred choice, or amending it so that US companies are excluded

The US government has conveyed to Javier Milei’s administration its concern that the National Sovereignty Defence bill, which toughens sanctions against those involved in exploiting resources in the Falklands, could reach American companies, the Argentine newspaper Clarín reported, citing unnamed officials in Washington.

“We see that the law is going to affect US companies, we are in contact with them and they have received notifications. Our interest is that they are not affected,” one of them told the newspaper. Others warned that the sanctions could become “a market barrier for trade and investment”. The concern centres on the fact that the bill extends penalties not only to companies operating in the archipelago but also to their affiliates, financial intermediaries, shareholders and suppliers.

According to Clarín, Washington has put forward two options: freezing the bill, its preferred choice, or amending it so that US companies are excluded. The newspaper says the issue has opened a rift within the Argentine cabinet. Neither the State Department nor the Argentine government has commented. On the sovereignty dispute, the US position remains one of neutrality, with no intention of mediating, according to the same source.

The concerns come ahead of a regional visit by Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau and Assistant Secretary for Western Hemisphere Affairs Juan Pablo Segura, who will be in Asunción and Buenos Aires between October 19 and 26. The State Department said they will meet senior officials and business leaders to advance the Andes-Atlantic Corridor, an infrastructure project worth some US$7 billion. Clarín suggests the bill could be on the agenda, though nobody has confirmed this.

The 133-article bill failed to secure committee approval in the Chamber of Deputies last week and was left off the agenda of the session planned for October 21, amid opposition objections to its security and defence chapters. The United Kingdom announced on Tuesday measures to prevent its companies from having to comply with Argentine sanctions.

World.title: Lula’s campaign takes alleged Meta favouritism towards Bolsonaro to the UN and federal police
World.content:
Lula’s campaign takes alleged Meta favouritism towards Bolsonaro to the UN and federal police

18th Sunday, October 2026 - 19:43 UTC Full article

The incidents reported include reduced reach for Lula’s Instagram profiles, WhatsApp searches for the “Lula’s Army” channel suggesting the “Flávio’s Troop” channel instead

The coalition backing Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election on Saturday reported to the UN alleged unequal treatment by Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, in favour of his rival, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and asked the Prosecutor General’s Office and the Federal Police to investigate possible illegal funding of his campaign. Meta attributes the incidents to technical errors.

Lula’s campaign submitted to the UN Special Rapporteur on freedom of opinion and expression a technical report on what it describes as “serious events that interfered with equal conditions between the candidates”. It asks Prosecutor General Paulo Gonet and the Federal Police to determine whether Bolsonaro obtained economic advantages in content distribution from Meta’s systems, which would amount to an electoral crime. It also requests that the candidate, his campaign treasurer and Meta executives in Brazil give statements, that the company’s internal communications be preserved and that judicial cooperation be sought from the United States to obtain records from the parent company.

The incidents reported include reduced reach for Lula’s Instagram profiles, WhatsApp searches for the “Lula’s Army” channel suggesting the “Flávio’s Troop” channel instead, and Meta’s artificial intelligence tool refusing to generate images supporting Lula while doing so for his rival. According to the newspaper El País, Meta employees acknowledged in internal messages that the reach of Lula’s accounts had been restricted.

“The integrity of an election does not depend exclusively on the security of the ballot boxes,” the campaign says in its filing, but also on voters being able to form their views “without undue manipulation” or “imbalance in the digital contest”. There was no response on record from Bolsonaro’s campaign.

Polls show a statistical tie, with Bolsonaro slightly ahead, a week before the October 25 runoff. The two candidates face each other on Sunday in their first televised debate, on the Band network.

World.title: Pressure mounts on Paraguay’s Central Bank over doubts about some lenders’ solvency
World.content:
Pressure mounts on Paraguay’s Central Bank over doubts about some lenders’ solvency

18th Sunday, October 2026 - 17:51 UTC Full article

“We ask the Central Bank to report on the solvency of all entities that received facilities in merger processes. That way doubts will be cleared,” the association said

The Association of Banks of Paraguay, which groups 14 private lenders, on Sunday asked the Central Bank of Paraguay to report on the solvency of institutions that received facilities in merger processes, days after senators from the ruling party and the opposition called on President Santiago Peña to remove the institution’s leadership.

“We ask the Central Bank to report on the solvency of all entities that received facilities in merger processes. That way doubts will be cleared and, if any entity does not comply, action can be taken in time,” the association said in a statement released by local media. It added that the soundness of lenders cannot rest on “differential treatment”.

The request comes after the Central Bank reported to the Senate, at its request, on the conduct of several private lenders, including Ueno Bank, which according to local media has attracted substantial public deposits in just a few years. The association considers that report “incomplete” and says concern persists over the credit exposure of a private bank, which it does not identify, to companies in its own group.

On Wednesday, senators from several parties urged Peña to dismiss the Central Bank’s board, and in particular its president, Carlos Carvallo. Days earlier, the president had publicly backed the institution and called for calm amid rumours about Ueno Bank. Neither the Central Bank nor the lender has commented on the association’s statement.

In 2024, Peña described as a “media campaign” and “lies” reports on the purchase by the Social Security Institute of 250 billion guaraníes in Ueno Bank bonds. The bank’s head, Juan Manuel Gustale, said at the time that Peña was a shareholder in Ueno Holding and not in the bank, and the president said in April 2025 that he had sold those shares.

World.title: Tesla’s new Roadster uses compressed air and fans to jump and drive upside down
World.content:
Tesla’s new Roadster uses compressed air and fans to jump and drive upside down

18th Sunday, October 2026 - 12:31 UTC Full article

In the demonstration, held at SpaceX’s test site in McGregor, the prototype drove up a ramp, turned upside down, separated from it and completed a rotation before touching the ground

Tesla unveiled on Thursday in Texas a redesigned version of its Roadster electric sports car, developed with SpaceX, which combines suction fans and compressed-air thrusters to climb near-vertical surfaces, drive upside down and flip in the air. The company plans to begin production in 2028.

In the demonstration, held at SpaceX’s test site in McGregor, the prototype drove up a ramp, turned upside down, separated from it and completed a rotation before touching the ground. According to Tesla, the vehicle uses two systems. Fans reduce the pressure under the chassis so that outside air pushes it onto the track, producing up to 4,700 kilograms of downforce that boosts grip even at standstill. In addition, two carbon-fibre tanks holding 600 litres of compressed air feed ten nozzles that provide thrust to accelerate, jump and correct the car’s position, with no combustion.

Do a kickflip! https://t.co/DJ1Bq1yu8m — Tesla (@Tesla) October 16, 2026

The company announced thrust of more than 80 kilonewtons and acceleration from zero to 97 kilometres per hour in 0.81 seconds. “It can basically fly like a rocket. It can do flips, crazy gymnastics, whatever you want really,” said Elon Musk, who acknowledged: “This is not necessarily a car optimised for safety.” The stored air allows only bursts of a few seconds, not sustained flight.

Tesla will offer three versions. Performance and Thrust, two-seaters, are already taking reservations with deposits of US$50,000 and US$250,000 respectively. Rocket, a single-seater with thrusters around the body, will be available by invitation only and is not approved for use on public roads. The company has not given dates for driver testing or explained how manoeuvres that lift the vehicle off the ground will be regulated.

Musk first unveiled the Roadster in 2017, with deliveries promised for 2020 that never materialised.

World.title: New Chiapas lab repairs and protects Indigenous clothing, helping to preserve a valued tradition
World.content:
A museum in southern Mexico devoted to Maya textiles has opened a conservation laboratory to help preserve its 3,400-piece collection.

The Maya World Textile Center — located in a former convent in the colonial city of San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas — houses collections of traditional clothing and other textiles from the region, including Chiapas and Guatemala.

Its new lab, which opened last week, includes equipment to repair damaged pieces and combat the insects and fungi that threaten them.

Specialists can wash textiles, remove stains, reinforce damaged areas, and identify materials and techniques.

The collections include everyday and ceremonial garments, with pieces mostly covering the last century. Pre-Hispanic, colonial and 19th-century artifacts are housed in the same building at the Museum of the Chiapas Highlands.

The goal is to extend the pieces’ lives so they remain available for research and exhibition in the Maya World Textile Center, described as the largest textile collection of the Maya world when it opened in 2012. It has received more than 342,000 visitors since then, according to figures reported by Diario de Chiapas.

Fomento Cultural Banamex — the Mexican bank’s nonprofit that supports arts, traditional crafts, exhibitions and heritage conservation — helped equip the center. Financial support from Fundación Diez Morodo, established by longtime Grupo Modelo executive Valentín Diez Morodo, helped fund staff and additional equipment.

Two apprentices who speak the Indigenous languages Tsotsil and Tseltal are training in handling, assessing, documenting and conserving the collections.

The opening comes as Indigenous communities pursue separate efforts to preserve the knowledge behind their crafts and defend designs against unauthorized copying.

Artisans from San Andrés Larrainzar — a Tsotsil Maya municipality located in the highlands of Chiapas — have documented 208 textile symbols through the Jolom Mayaetik cooperative. The catalog includes names and meanings passed down through generations; however, its copyright protection covers the research, not necessarily the designs, cooperative members said.

Meanwhile, in neighboring Oaxaca, officials have begun a process to register and protect Villa Hidalgo Yalálag’s traditional huarache designs after the controversy over Adidas’ Oaxaca Slip-On shoe in 2025. Adidas and designer Willy Chavarria apologized for developing the sandal-inspired shoe without the community’s involvement.

Preservation efforts also face economic pressures. Female textile artisans in Mexico earned an average of 3,699 pesos (about US $200) monthly, compared with 7,399 pesos (about US $400) for men, the news source Animal Político reported in August, citing national employment data.

Only 2.4% of female textile artisans in Mexico had social security coverage, compared with 12.4% of their male counterparts, it reported. Mexico’s social security system provides protections that include medical care, disability benefits and maternity leave, in addition to retirement benefits.

With reports from Diario de Chiapas, La Jornada, La Crónica, Clarín and Animal Político

World.title: Public healthcare workers plan more protests this week to demand better pay and working conditions
World.content:
Disgruntled healthcare workers will take to the streets of Mexico City again this Wednesday, eight days after participating in a large protest march to demand higher pay, better working conditions, increased funding for healthcare and an end to shortages of medicines and medical supplies.

Current and former Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) workers agreed to hold another march at a meeting in the capital on Sunday.

“La Gran Marcha en CDMX” (The Great March in Mexico City) will set off from the Siglo XXI National Medical Center on Cuauhtémoc Avenue in the Doctores neighborhood at 3 p.m. on Wednesday. The endpoint has not been defined, but it appears likely that workers will once again march to the IMSS offices on Paseo de la Reforma, where a protest camp was set up 10 days ago.

At Sunday’s meeting, held outside the IMSS offices, IMSS workers called on social organizations, other workers and citizens in general to join their march this Wednesday, according to the news magazine Proceso.

They also called on IMSS workers to protest in other states around the country, as occurred last Tuesday.

The IMSS workers have a range of demands, including a 10% pay rise; the adequate supply of medications and medical supplies in IMSS hospitals and clinics; the hiring of additional healthcare personnel in order to ease excessive workloads; the allocation of resources equivalent to 7% of GDP to healthcare; changes to their pension system; and the resignation or dismissal of Rafael Olivos Hernández, head of the National Social Security Workers Union.

In addition to organizing another march on Wednesday, IMSS workers will hold a press conference this Tuesday at the same time as President Claudia Sheinbaum’s morning presser (mañanera) at the National Palace.

According to the workers, at the press conference — dubbed the IMSS resistance mañanera — representatives of their protest movement will present “verifiable information about the real state of [IMSS] medical facilities, [their] operational deficiencies and the status of our demands.”

Sheinbaum said last week that IMSS workers’ “legitimate demands” are being addressed. She said that IMSS director Zoé Robledo had been instructed to draw up an “action plan” to “immediately” address “all the legitimate demands of IMSS workers.”

On Monday, she said Robledo’s ongoing tenure at the helm of IMSS was “not in doubt.”

Sheinbaum also said the IMSS healthcare system is “better” now than it was “before,” asserting that the current situation is not comparable to that when Mikel Arriola was director of the social security institute and public healthcare provider during the presidency of Enrique Peña Nieto (2012-18).

Sheinbaum pledges to ‘completely modernize’ Mexico’s public healthcare system

During an address in Umán, Yucatán, on Saturday, Sheinbaum pledged to “completely modernize” Mexico’s public healthcare system, which includes services provided by IMSS, the Institute for Social Security and Services for State Workers (ISSSTE) and IMSS Bienestar, which treats patients without social security coverage.

“I already put together a team to completely modernize the healthcare system,” she said.

“… We have to provide results, … and I’m sure we’re going to improve the healthcare service every day,” Sheinbaum said.

“Resources aren’t lacking, money isn’t lacking, but we have to improve the way we’re working because a lot of processes come from 50 or 60 years ago and they haven’t been updated,” she said.

Sheinbaum once again acknowledged that there are problems related to the distribution of medicines to public healthcare facilities, but stressed that her government is working to resolve them, as well as staffing shortages.

“We’re hiring [more] doctors and nurses and guaranteeing the supply of medications,” she said.

Earlier this month, Sheinbaum noted that her government was preparing to launch Mexico’s Universal Health Service on Jan. 1, 2027.

“From Jan. 1, some services are going to be universal and we’re going to increase the [universal] services so that at the end of the six-year term of government, you can go to any healthcare center, doctor’s office or hospital regardless of which institution you are a beneficiary of,” she said on Oct. 6.

Sheinbaum said the “first step” in the process toward the commencement of the Universal Health Service is the issuance of universal healthcare cards. Those cards are currently being issued to seniors ahead of their rollout to younger Mexicans and eligible foreigners.

With reports from La Jornada, Proceso, Latinus and EFE

World.title: Mexican plastic-free makeup line named a top invention of 2026 by TIME
World.content:
Published annually since 2000, TIME magazine’s list of the best inventions recognizes products and developments that transform the way we live, work and relate to the world. This year, AORA’s plastic-free cosmetics have been recognized among the top 300 innovations, alongside notable products like Apple’s iPhone Duo and Bosch’s new microplastic filter.

Announced on Oct. 15, TIME’s Best Inventions of 2026 list highlights AORA’s use of materials such as aluminum, tinplate and wood to manufacture reusable and recyclable packaging. “A sustainable ingredient list rings hollow if the packaging isn’t earth-friendly too,” TIME wrote.

Founded in Mexico City in 2022 by Nour Tayara and Rodrigo Peñafiel, AORA has built its identity around bright colors, ingredients of Mexican origin and designs that seek to make beauty products more appealing while reducing reliance on single-use plastic.

Its goal is to offer high-end makeup without conventional plastic packaging — a feature that also helped it make history as the first plastic-free brand sold at global beauty retailer Sephora.

“The beauty industry is full of trash, and we’re on a mission to change that, not just by eliminating plastic from our products, but by helping clean up the industry’s waste,” Nour Tayara, co-founder of AORA, told Mexico News Daily.

“We set out to make sustainability sexy, cool, colorful and fun while tackling what seemed impossible: creating incredible makeup people want to cherish, without plastic,” Tayara added. “Years of research, development and innovation later, being named one of TIME’s Best Inventions proves the answer is a big, resounding yes.”

To compile the list, TIME gathers nominations from its editors and international correspondents, as well as submissions made online. It then evaluates these proposals based on criteria such as originality, effectiveness, ambition and impact.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Guadalajara unrest over water crisis intensifies as presumed infiltrators provoke violence
World.content:
A second major march in a week drew some 10,000 people protesting the unresolved issue of contaminated water in the Guadalajara metropolitan area, but alleged infiltrators turned the otherwise peaceful demonstration violent.

Incidents of vandalism and looting occurred along the route of the march in downtown Guadalajara, which culminated with Molotov cocktails being hurled at the state Congress building.

State police officers, riot squads and emergency personnel were immediately deployed to the area to extinguish the flames, prevent protesters from forcibly entering the government building and ensure the safety of the administrative staff and legislators present.

Participants insisted the vandals were not part of the protest group, some speculating they were agitators sent by the Citizens’ Movement party (MC) — the dominant political group in the state — to discredit the demonstration. Others suggested the provocateurs were sponsored by the nationally dominant Morena party in an effort to weaken the MC ahead of next year’s elections.

The newspaper La Jornada reported that citizens themselves drove out a group of at least 30 masked individuals before the march began, while also confiscating firecrackers, clubs and Molotov cocktails.

The protest started two hours later than planned as organizers sought to remove those identified as potential instigators.

Even so, a masked group of people trailed the march through the Historic Center, hurling firecrackers, looting shops and spray-painting buildings.

“At least six restaurants, department stores and sporting goods stores were damaged by acts of vandalism, graffiti, broken windows and looting,” the state government reported later Sunday.

The government also reported five arrests, adding that another eight people required medical attention.

By 2 p.m., the peaceful protesters had filled the Plaza de Armas, making the march one of the largest on record since Governor Pablo Lemus came to power in December 2024.

While banners demanding clean water fluttered in the breeze, cries of “Resign, Lemus” and chants for a recall referendum filled the square.

By then, the agitators had begun hurling rocks and explosives at the Congress building about three blocks away.

Sunday’s protest took place a week after the first mass demonstration was met with repressive tactics by state authorities who pepper-sprayed demonstrators and turned high-pressure fire hoses on the crowds. Dozens were beaten and arrested.

Governor Lemus subsequently apologized for the heavy-handed tactics, released those who had been detained and ordered an investigation.

This time around, there was minimal police presence until the violence began.

Later Sunday, Oscar-winning director Guillermo del Toro, a native of Guadalajara, declared his support for the protesters during his appearance at the Morelia International Film Festival.

With reports from La Jornada, Reporte Indigo and UDG-TV

World.title: Former Chihuahua AG arrested on treason, conspiracy charges in connection with illegal CIA operation
World.content:
The former attorney general of Chihuahua, César Jáuregui, was taken into federal custody Sunday on a charge of treason related to allegations that U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) officers participated in a drug lab raid in Chihuahua in April without the knowledge or authorization of the Mexican government.

Jáuregui, Chihuahua’s attorney general from January 2023 until his resignation in April 2026, was detained by Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) agents in Chihuahua city Sunday night after appearing in a state court on two charges brought by the Chihuahua Attorney General’s Office: unlawful exercise of public office and conspiracy by public officials.

He was subsequently flown to Toluca, México state, and transferred to the Altiplano federal prison, located northwest of Toluca, on Monday morning.

Jáuregui was first arrested on state and federal charges on Saturday. On Sunday night, a judge ruled that he did not need to be held in pretrial detention on the state charges. However, any hope Jáuregui had of regaining his freedom was short-lived, as federal agents took him into custody on the federal treason charge.

The treason charge stems from the allegation that the ex-attorney general allowed CIA officers to participate in a drug lab raid without authorization from the Mexican government. If convicted, Jáuregui faces a prison sentence of five to 40 years.

His arrest came six months after four CIA agents allegedly participated in a drug lab raid led by Chihuahua’s State Investigation Agency (AEI). Two CIA agents and two Chihuahua state police officials, including the head of the AEI, died in a car accident after the operation was carried out in the municipality of Morelos, located in the Sierra Tarahumara.

President Claudia Sheinbaum assigned most of the blame for the allegedly illegal security collaboration between Chihuahua and the United States to Chihuahua authorities, although she also accused the U.S. government of interference in Mexican affairs.

Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos said in May that she didn’t authorize or have knowledge of the presence of the CIA in the northern border state. If CIA officers did indeed participate in the drug lab operation, their involvement would have violated Mexico’s Constitution and National Security Law, according to federal authorities.

According to a report published by The Los Angeles Times in April, the raid in Chihuahua on the weekend of April 18 and 19 was “at least the third time this year that CIA operatives joined authorities in the northern border state of Chihuahua in an operation against a drug target.”

Guillermo Arturo Zuany Portillo, former head of the Strategic Operations division of the Chihuahua Attorney General’s Office, is wanted in connection with the drug lab raid in April, but has not yet been detained.

Godoy: ‘No justification whatsoever’ for the CIA agents’ participation in the drug lab raid

In a video message on Saturday, federal Attorney General Ernestina Godoy described the drug lab raid in Chihuahua in April as an “irregular operation” that constituted “an attack on the federal pact and the separation of powers.”

“It should be noted that our Constitution and the National Security Law restrict states’ ability to assume powers reserved to the federal government or to transfer governmental powers to foreign authorities,” she said.

Mensaje sobre orden de aprehensión contra César “N”. 171026

Watch this video on YouTube

Godoy said that an FGR investigation determined that Jáuregui allegedly engaged in conduct that could constitute the offense of treason.

“This is because he allegedly allowed foreign nationals to operate without authorization on Mexican territory and to carry out activities reserved exclusively for federal forces,” she said.

“This undermines the nation’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as such conduct is expressly prohibited by the Constitution,” Godoy said.

“It is clearly established in the investigation file, including through information provided by the [Chihuahua] State Attorney General’s Office itself, that the participation in the operation by these foreigners had no justification whatsoever,” she said.

“… State authorities lacked the legal authority to carry out activities reserved exclusively for the federal government,” Godoy said, referring to the dismantlement of drug labs.

“The National Security Law expressly prohibits states from doing so.”

The attorney general also said that Jáuregui allegedly “concealed information” from federal authorities.

“The State Attorney General’s Office, through its head, was required to inform the federal government [about the operation]. It did not do so,” Godoy said.

Sheinbaum: FGR is investigating Jáuregui’s alleged involvement in ‘other matters’

At her Monday morning press conference, Sheinbaum also said that the Chihuahua state government doesn’t have the authority to “dismantle a [drug] laboratory.”

“The Federal Attorney General’s Office has that authority,” she said.

“… The truth is that it was very irresponsible, to say the least, to not only allow the participation of foreign agents, against the law, in a ground operation, but also to do so in the way they did,” Sheinbaum said, highlighting that Chihuahua officials and CIA agents traveled on a dangerous, winding road at night after the drug lab raid.

World.title: Army detains ‘El Talibán’ and 4 others in Vizsla Silver kidnapping case
World.content:
Members of Mexico’s Ministry of National Defense (Defensa) arrested five alleged members of the Los Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, seizing weapons, a vehicle and tactical equipment, in two separate operations on Friday and Saturday.

Those arrested are suspected of involvement both in the kidnapping of 10 employees of the Canadian mining company Vizsla Silver in Concordia, Sinaloa, in January and in the abduction of four tourists from México state in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, in February.

Among those arrested was Jesús Abraham “N,” also known as “El Talibán,” who is believed to be a trusted associate of Juan Benito “N”, alias “Beny 17,” Los Chapitos’s regional leader in southern Sinaloa.

Four additional men were arrested, including a Colombian citizen, in a separate operation in the municipality of El Rosario, located approximately 70 kilometers south of Concordia and Mazatlán.

According to Defensa, all four are security personnel of Óscar Luciano Martínez Larios, known by the names of “El Casco” (the helmet) and “El 81,” who allegedly leads a cell of Los Chapitos in Sinaloa. Martínez Larios is also reportedly part of the “Los Hermanos Martínez” (The Martínez Brothers) criminal group, whose membership also includes Gabriel Nicolás Martínez Larios, arrested in June of this year, and Eduardo Jonathan Martínez, who was killed on Oct. 9 during an armed riot at the “El Castillo” prison in Mazatlán.

Los Chapitos are accused of orchestrating the kidnapping of the 10 Vizsla Silver workers on Jan. 23 after allegedly mistaking them for members of the rival group “Los Mayos.” Nine of the ten workers have since been found dead, while the tenth remains missing.

En Sinaloa, como resultado de trabajos de inteligencia militar, elementos de @Defensamx1 y @GN_MEXICO_, en coordinación con @sspsinaloa1, detuvieron en dos acciones realizadas en El Rosario y Mazatlán a Jesús Abraham “N”, alias “Talibán”, y a cuatro integrantes de una célula delictiva, además de asegurar armamento y equipo táctico. Los detenidos están vinculados con el secuestro y homicidio de 10 trabajadores de una empresa minera en La Concordia, así como con el secuestro de cuatro turistas originarios del Estado de México, ocurrido en Mazatlán. El Gabinete de Seguridad mantiene acciones coordinadas de inteligencia e investigación para detener a generadores de violencia, desarticular estructuras criminales y combatir la impunidad. — Gabinete de Seguridad de México (@GabSeguridadMX) October 19, 2026

The criminal group has also been linked to the kidnapping of four tourists on Feb. 3 when six members of the same family from Santa Ana Ixtlahuaca in México state were intercepted by armed men on Sábalo-Cerritos Avenue in Mazatlán after renting off-road vehicles to explore the area.

A 28-year-old woman and a nine-year-old girl were rescued alive the following day in the town of El Habal, while the remaining four brothers remain missing, despite significant media attention to the case and multiple search operations.

The five arrests made this weekend bring the total number of arrests in the Vizsla Silver case to 19. The Sinaloa Attorney General’s Office is conducting further investigations to determine the next steps of the case.

With reports from La Jornada, Infobae and El Economista

World.title: MND Local Guadalajara: New water protest draws thousands, Zapopan officials scrutinized over abandoned pet euthanasia
World.content:
This week, we take a look at local authorities in Zapopan who have come under fire for the city’s heavy reliance on euthanasia of homeless cats and dogs. But first, we have details on the second mega-march for clean water in Guadalajara this past weekend.

Guadalajara residents turn out in force for second clean water march

The second march for clean water on Sunday, Oct. 18, drew thousands of residents from across the metropolitan area.

Protesters for the latest rally gathered at Parque Rojo along Avenida Vallarta and marched to the Government Palace in Guadalajara’s historic center in yet another attempt to pressure the city to improve the public water supply.

The vibe Sunday was more political and defiant than at the march a week earlier. There were notably fewer elderly and child attendees this past week in light of the violence that broke out at the protest on Oct. 11.

In addition to calling for improvements to the city’s water, attendees were vocal in demanding justice for those detained during the Oct. 11 march. Numerous signs called for the ouster of Governor Pablo Lemus.

Second march monitored for human rights abuses

Many have condemned aggressive policing of protesters at the Oct. 11 rally. Officers’ use of tear gas, water cannons and brutal tactics on unarmed attendees resulted in numerous serious injuries.

The National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) sent staff to monitor Sunday’s march while calling on the Jalisco state government to guarantee citizens’ rights to free expression and peaceful demonstration.

Protesters’ signs shared a mixture of sentiments. Some expressed anger over the prior week’s violence and vitriol toward Lemus. Others chanted for Lemus’ ouster, while many more signs simply decried the continued poor quality of public water supplies and warned that privatization was not an acceptable solution to the crisis.

At various times, march organizers called on attendees to support those who had been detained and beaten for speaking out against the failure to deliver clean water by the Inter-Municipal Services for Water Supply and Sewerage (SIAPA). Many raised their fists in solidarity, while others knelt in a display of respect and gratitude.

Organizers could also be heard reminding the crowd that they were gathered in peace. Still, numerous attendees brought gas masks and goggles, not knowing what to expect.

The latest protest also included a handful of masked people — a so-called “black bloc” — who started throwing firecrackers and Molotov cocktails near Parque Rojo amid the gathered protesters. Organizers briefly paused the march while those individuals were expelled from the group. I personally witnessed numerous explosive devices detonating on Avenida Vallarta.

Some of these masked people later reportedly vandalized and looted several area businesses.

Instead of addressing the root causes of pet abandonment, Zapopan punishes animals

Zapopan’s city government earlier this month confirmed that it has euthanized 14,016 dogs and cats over the past four years, citing the need to eliminate health risks and remove aggressive animals from city streets.

This amounted to nearly 10 animal exterminations per day, every day, between 2022 and 2026, at the ironically named Zapopan Comprehensive Animal Health Center (CISAZ) located in the Jardines del Vergel neighborhood.

Amada Yamile Lofte Galán, director of animal protection for Zapopan, stated that euthanasia is carried out only on homeless animals exhibiting aggressive behavior, based on citizen reports. She also confirmed that Zapopan assists nine other municipalities with euthanasia. While not publicly identified, these cities most likely include neighboring Guadalajara, Tlaquepaque, Tlajomulco and Tonalá.

Low adoption rates trigger fierce legislative backlash

Galán also stated that the animals create trash and pose a risk to other animals, as most are not sterilized or vaccinated. While these observations are generally true, she has not addressed why the city has put so little effort into sterilization and adoption.

Since 2022, Zapopan has completed fewer than 150 adoptions annually. Unsurprisingly, Zapopan’s pitiful adoption record has fueled an outcry from several public officials and animal activists. One prominent critic is state legislator Tonantzin Cárdenas Méndez, who recently offered a new initiative to Jalisco’s State Congress.

Citing ongoing activities at CISAZ, Méndez condemned its practice of prioritizing euthanasia over adoption. “Article 39 of the Zapopan Regulations states that euthanasia is permitted after five business days (in city custody) if an animal has not been claimed,” she noted.

This amounts to a death sentence for nearly all of the animals taken into custody, as the statistics confirm. Since 2022, Zapopan has adopted just 4% of the animals city workers have taken off the streets, while killing the other 96%.

Critics demand structural reforms to animal welfare laws

Moreover, because there is no transparency in CISAZ’s system as to when animals are acquired or exterminated, independent observers cannot verify whether the city is even complying with its own minimum standards.

Méndez also called out the City Council’s published goal (it appeared within the administration’s budget matrix) of euthanizing 3,300 animals in 2026. She questioned why they set a death goal rather than something more humane, such as an adoption goal.

Underscoring the city’s seeming indifference to animal welfare, others have faulted CISAZ’s lack of proper hygiene, food and shelter for the animals in its care, as well as its failure to address any of the causes of animal homelessness, namely pet abandonments and low sterilization rates.

Méndez’s initiative to standardize the Federal Animal Health Law seeks to integrate with other previous animal welfare proposals, including a measure by legislator Itzul Barrera.

Their reforms call for new restrictions on euthanasia, limiting it to cases of animal illness, injury or serious untreatable conditions.

MND writer Dawn Stoner is reporting from Guadalajara.

World.title: The deadly brain-eating amoeba that killed a Mérida man has now been detected in 6 artificial lakes
World.content:
Health authorities in the state of Yucatán have detected in six artificial lakes the same brain-eating amoeba that caused the death of a 34-year-old man last month. All six lakes have been closed.

State officials ordered an investigation after an aquatic sports instructor was determined to have died in the state capital of Mérida last month from Naegleria fowleri, an amoeba which causes a rare and nearly always fatal brain infection known as primary amebic meningoencephalitis (PAM).

The authorities say it is the first — and so far only— death recorded in the state, famous for freshwater sinkholes known as cenotes. They said in a public statement that the organism is contained and poses no further risk.

The government also increased health surveillance protocols.

After the death was confirmed as being caused by the brain-eating amoeba, tests were conducted at artificial lakes in and near Mérida. The organism was found in six of the nine lakes examined.

Naegleria fowleri thrives in stagnant freshwater in lakes, rivers, ponds and hot springs, especially between 35 and 46 degrees Celsius (95-115 F).

State Health Minister Alberto Alcocer urged the public to contact health personnel if they have been in contact with water from the six artifical lakes in the following five locations: Plaza La Isla (where the parasite was originally detected), the Cabo Norte complex (two) , the Centenario Zoo, the Gran Parque La Plancha and the Poniente Ecological Park.

“Finding this amoeba in the environment does not indicate an epidemic or that people who visited these places are sick,” Alcocer said.

The amoeba enters the body when water containing the organism goes up the nose. It then travels up the olfactory nerve directly to the brain, where it destroys brain tissue and causes severe swelling.

The contaminated areas have been marked with barriers and warning signs, and users are strictly prohibited from coming into contact with the water. Remediation efforts in collaboration with specialists from the Autonomous University of Yucatán and the Instituto Politécnico Nacional have already begun.

Additionally, the state government opened an investigation against the companies in charge of the maintenance and water quality of the lake at Plaza la Isla, the site at which the victim had been teaching wakeboarding.

With reports from El País and El Economista

Arabica coffee futures for December delivery settled at US$3.157 per pound in New York on Monday, 19 October, up 3.3% and the highest level in a month, as stocks in ICE warehouses stayed near a 27-year low. A stronger Brazilian real, which firmed to about R$5.04 per US$1, also weighed on selling by farmers in the world’s largest coffee producer, according to Reuters.

Notícias Agrícolas, a Brazilian farm-news site, reported the settlement at 315.7 cents, up 10.1 cents. Coffee is one of the best-known products of the Brazil economy, and US buyers pay close attention to its price.

What Moved Arabica on Monday

The December contract rose 10.10 cents to 315.70 cents, while the March 2027 contract settled at 302.25 cents, according to Notícias Agrícolas. Reuters described the level as the highest in a month.

Analyst Vicente Zotti of NRT told Notícias Agrícolas that the jump reflects traders covering short positions, meaning bets on falling prices that must be closed. He pointed to low exchange stocks and high price premiums for some origins as limits on switching to other supply.

Why the Real Matters for Coffee

Coffee trades in US dollars, but Brazilian farmers pay their costs in reais. When the real gains, each dollar buys fewer reais, so growers get less at home for the same sale and tend to hold back beans, as Reuters reported.

The real closed at R$5.0356 per US$1 on Monday, from R$5.0627 on Friday, a gain of about 0.5%, according to RT market data. Our dollar-to-real guide explains what drives the exchange rate.

Warehouse Stocks Near a 27-Year Low

ICE-certified arabica stocks are near a 27-year low, according to Notícias Agrícolas and Reuters. Traders worry that Brazilian supplies will not reach ICE warehouses before the December contract expires.

Notícias Agrícolas also lists El Niño, a weather pattern that can upset harvests, as a risk for future harvests. Robusta, the cheaper bean grown mostly in Vietnam and Brazil, settled at US$3,484 per metric ton for November delivery in London, up US$70.

What It Means for US Readers

The United States was the largest buyer of Brazilian coffee in the first nine months of 2026, with about 3.8 million 60-kilogram bags, according to Cecafé, the Brazilian coffee exporters’ council. Higher New York futures usually reach US roasters first and shelf prices later, with a lag of months.

Investors who follow the Brazil stock market can watch the real and the dollar together. Cecafé data also showed US imports of Brazilian coffee rising 86% in September, as our earlier report explains.

What Is Not Known

It is not clear whether the rally will last once the December contract expires and short covering fades. Brazilian farmers’ stock-holding is also hard to measure, so the size of the supply squeeze is uncertain.

Brazil’s benchmark stock index, the Ibovespa, fell 0.17% to 205,079 points on Monday, 19 October, as oil eased and traders watched tight polls ahead of the presidential runoff. Petrobras, the state-controlled oil company, lost 2.82% on its preferred shares, while fashion group Azzas 2154 jumped 13.25%.

The index touched 207,387.56 during the session, about 1% above Friday’s close of 205,430.33, before it slid to a small loss. The retreat came six days before the vote, with the Brazil stock market and the wider Brazil economy waiting for the result.

How the Session Unfolded

Investors reacted to new polls on the second round between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a left-wing Workers’ Party leader, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of the conservative Liberal Party. An AtlasIntel poll for Bloomberg showed Bolsonaro with 49.8% of total voting intentions against 47.6% for Lula, while a BTG/Nexus poll the same day was reported as a technical tie.

Estadão reported that Citi upgraded both Azzas and MRV to buy, and Exame also credits the Azzas jump to the Citi upgrade. Our conversions use a rate of about R$5.05 per US$1.

What the Central Bank Survey Shows

The central bank’s Focus survey, published on Monday, left the median forecast for 2026 inflation at 5.22%. That is unchanged from the previous week and 0.72 percentage points above the 4.50% ceiling of the bank’s target range, which is 3% with a 1.5-point tolerance.

Economists also kept the year-end Selic rate forecast at 13.25%. A high Selic keeps borrowing costly for Brazilian households and companies.

What It Means for US Readers

For a dollar investor, Monday’s stronger real softened the index’s small loss: in dollar terms the Ibovespa was slightly higher, by our calculation. Brazilian shares held in the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ) and ADRs such as Petrobras (PBR), Vale (VALE), Itaú (ITUB) and Nubank (NU) react to the same two forces, oil and the runoff.

World.title: Lagos Otedola Bridge Tanker Fire Injures Two
World.content:
Key Facts —Who. A diesel-laden tanker of about 33,000 litres and its two adult male occupants, who were reported injured. —What. The tanker fell from the Otedola Bridge section into the underpass below and caught fire, and the fire was later put out. —Where. Otedola Bridge on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, near Berger, Lagos, Nigeria. —When. Late afternoon on Monday 19 October 2026, around 4:10 pm to 4:25 pm local time (about 15:10 to 15:25 GMT). —Casualties. Two injured men were taken to an emergency centre, and a conflicting report of two deaths is unconfirmed. —Cause. A preliminary finding of speeding in a lone crash; no further cause is established. —As of 19 October 2026, 21:30 GMT

A fuel tanker fell from the Otedola Bridge in Lagos, Nigeria, and caught fire on Monday 19 October 2026, the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Nigeria’s road safety agency, said. The Lagos-Ibadan Expressway is a main road out of Nigeria’s largest city, so Americans visiting or working in Lagos should expect delays.

The FRSC says two people were injured, but one newspaper headline speaks of two deaths, and The Rio Times could not confirm any deaths. Below we set out what is known, what is not, and what it means for US readers with ties to Lagos.

What We Know

The tanker was carrying diesel and other petroleum products from a depot, and the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) put its capacity at 33,000 litres. It fell from the Otedola Bridge section of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway into the underpass beneath it, near the Berger area, and caught fire.

The FRSC called the incident a lone crash on the outward section of the expressway. Its Lagos Sector Command put the time at about 4:10 pm local time, which is about 15:10 GMT.

File photo: Lagos skyline from Tafawa Balewa Square, Onikan.

Other agencies logged the incident a few minutes later. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said it received an alert at about 4:24 pm, so we give a range of around 4:10 pm to 4:25 pm.

Premium Times reported that the fire service received a distress call at 4:09 pm. Firefighters from the Alausa and Ikeja stations arrived at 4:16 pm, and the fire was put out, with crews staying on to deal with residual hotspots.

The FRSC rescue unit arrived at 4:20 pm, according to a statement issued by Sector Public Education Officer Elizabeth Jayeola. The statement said two adult male occupants were injured and taken to the Lagos State Accident and Emergency Centre.

The FRSC added that no fatalities were recorded in the initial crash report. Its preliminary findings identify speeding as the reported cause of the crash.

Lagos Sector Commander Kehinde Hamzat said speeding is a serious threat, especially for tankers carrying fuel. He urged drivers not to speed and asked the public not to approach burning tankers to film them.

LASEMA spokesperson Olawale Afolabi confirmed the fire and said the agency’s Tiger team had been deployed. LASTMA managed traffic and assisted the victims, and it advised drivers to drive cautiously.

BusinessDay reported severe traffic congestion around the scene. Drivers should plan extra time on routes near the bridge.

The reports on casualties conflict. The FRSC says two people were injured and none died in its initial report, while the headline of a BusinessDay report says two lives were lost.

The Rio Times could not confirm any deaths, and we are not reporting that anyone has died. Casualty figures may change as the agencies update their accounts.

What Is Not Known

The condition of the two injured men has not been made public, and neither have their identities. It is also unclear whether anyone died, given the conflicting reports.

Officials have not said whether other vehicles or property were damaged. It is also not known how long the expressway section was disrupted.

The driver’s own account has not been reported. The cause beyond the FRSC’s preliminary finding of speeding is not yet established.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

The Lagos-Ibadan Expressway is a main road out of Lagos, so a fire at Otedola Bridge can slow traffic well beyond the site. Americans and other visitors in Lagos should expect delays and follow local traffic officials.

Fuel tankers are a recurring road hazard in Nigeria. The Otedola Bridge area has seen earlier tanker explosions, including a gas truck explosion reported by Channels TV on 11 March 2025.

Hamzat’s appeal to keep away from burning tankers applies to visitors as much as residents. Travellers who see a fire should stay back and let emergency crews work.

For background on road risks, see our Nigeria Highway Safety Guide: Tanker Risks for Visitors, and for an earlier case, read Tanker Crash Kills 5 in Ibadan, Nigeria. More reporting is available in our Nigeria coverage section.

Agencies should clarify the casualty figures and the state of the road in the coming hours. Clearer figures should follow once the agencies publish further details.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened at Otedola Bridge in Lagos?

A tanker carrying petroleum products fell from the Otedola Bridge section of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway into the underpass below on Monday 19 October 2026 and caught fire. Firefighters put the fire out, and crews stayed on for residual hotspots.

Did anyone die in the Otedola Bridge tanker fire?

The FRSC says two adult men were injured and that no fatalities were recorded in its initial crash report. a BusinessDay headline says two lives were lost, and The Rio Times could not confirm any death, so casualty figures may change.

What caused the tanker crash?

The FRSC called it a lone crash, and its preliminary findings identify speeding as the reported cause. No other cause has been established, and the driver’s own account has not been reported.

Should travellers expect delays on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway?

BusinessDay reported severe traffic congestion, so travellers should expect delays and follow local traffic officials. How long the expressway section was disrupted is not known.

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Monday, 19 October, 5:20 p.m. ET · Source: Lula campaign, CNN Brasil

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Monday 19 October, Lula’s campaign said he will sign an authorisation letting courts open his own bank and phone records, and those of his family.

The condition His spokesman said the step depends on Flávio Bolsonaro granting the same access for himself and his family.

Where it goes The papers are to go to the presidents of the electoral court (TSE), Kássio Nunes Marques, and the Supreme Federal Court (STF), Edson Fachin.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 23.5% (19 October, 5:04 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 76% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 24% and 22% ), as of 19 October, 7:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open Flávio Bolsonaro had not publicly accepted the challenge at the time of writing, and answered it on stage only with a jab at Lula.

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will authorise courts to open his bank and phone records, his campaign said on Monday 19 October at about 4:37 p.m. ET. It is the latest move in the Brazil election 2026, 6 days before the vote.

The offer is a challenge to his rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, to do the same before the runoff on Sunday 25 October. For investors and voters abroad, it keeps corruption at the centre of a race that polls call close.

What Lula Promised

Campaign spokesman Camilo Santana said the president will officially authorise the opening of his bank and phone records, and those of his relatives, according to CNN Brasil. Santana said the plan was for Lula to sign it that same day, and that he will challenge Flávio to do the same.

The papers are to go to Kássio Nunes Marques, president of the electoral court (TSE), and Edson Fachin, president of the Supreme Federal Court (STF), CNN Brasil reported. Santana signalled that the waiver depends on Flávio also giving his consent.

In an Instagram video on Monday, Lula said he would prepare powers of attorney covering himself and his children, if Flávio does the same with his parents and brothers, O Liberal reported. He gave Flávio one week to accept, according to Correio Braziliense, and pressed him over a costly house he bought, saying the two earn the same salary.

How the Debate Set This Up

Lula first raised the idea at the first runoff debate on the Band television network on Sunday 18 October. He questioned Flávio about alleged ties to ex-banker Daniel Vorcaro, while Flávio asked about lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is linked to the INSS social-security fraud case, according to CNN Brasil.

O Liberal reported that Flávio neither accepted nor refused the proposal on stage, and instead hinted that Lula receives “dirty money on the side”. In his video, Lula said the goal was to “prove who is corrupt in this country”.

What the Offer Changes

A letter of consent from a candidate is a political gesture, and the reports do not say any court has acted on it. Whether judges would open any records is not yet known.

Both men have faced corruption claims from the other side, and our debate fact-check found errors in claims from each. The offer gives Lula a way to turn the debate attack back on his rival in the final week.

What It Means for US Readers

Corruption and campaign-finance questions can move Brazilian assets as quickly as a poll can. If you hold Brazilian stocks, bonds or US-listed shares of Brazilian companies, headlines like this add to the swings expected before 25 October.

The Brazil runoff poll tracker lists every survey, so you can see whether voters react. Any change would show up in new polls over the coming days, not in this announcement itself.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 23.5% (19 October, 5:04 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has about US$188.2 million in total bets.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Lula has already signed the letter or when it reaches the two courts. Flávio Bolsonaro has made no public commitment to open his own records.

It is also unclear whether the courts will act on a letter that depends on a rival’s consent.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Lula announce about his bank records?

His campaign said on Monday 19 October that he will authorise courts to open his bank and phone records, and those of his family. He wants Flávio Bolsonaro to do the same.

Who will receive the papers?

They are to go to Kássio Nunes Marques, president of the electoral court (TSE), and Edson Fachin, president of the Supreme Federal Court (STF). CNN Brasil reported this on Monday.

Has Flávio Bolsonaro accepted the challenge?

Not publicly, at the time of writing. He neither accepted nor refused when Lula raised it in the Band debate on Sunday 18 October.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are the two candidates.

World.content:

ALGERIA · DIPLOMACY

Key Facts — The country Algeria is Africa’s largest country by area and a major gas supplier to southern Europe. It has been a close partner of Moscow since the Cold War.

— What happened On Thursday 15 October, Putin called Algeria “one of our close friends and allies” by video link to a Russian business forum.

— The trade link Russia’s farm minister said dry-milk shipments to Algeria rose fourfold this year, and TSA in Algiers reported the remark on Monday 19 October.

— The echo On Saturday 3 October, Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune denied any chill with Russia and said he would not refuse closer economic integration.

— The UN link On Friday 9 October, a Russian deputy foreign minister told Algeria’s ambassador that Moscow wants the UN mission in Western Sahara kept in its current form.

— What it means for you Washington backs Morocco on Western Sahara, so Algeria and Russia voting alike at the UN Security Council could matter for US diplomacy.

— Still open No gas, arms or trade deal accompanied the remarks, and no Algerian government reply to Putin has been published.

Putin calls Algeria “one of our close friends and allies”, the Russian president said by video link on Thursday 15 October. Algeria’s news site TSA reported the remark on Monday 19 October, after the Russian embassy in Algiers posted it online.

For US readers the message lands before a United Nations vote on Western Sahara, where Washington and Algiers stand on opposite sides. Algeria also supplies gas to Europe and spends more on its military than any African state.

What Putin Said in Moscow

Putin spoke on Thursday 15 October by video link to Business Russia, a national employers’ association, at its 21st forum-congress, the Kremlin transcript shows. “Algeria is one of our close friends and allies,” he said, adding that relations are good “in many areas.”

He said the two sides “have never let each other down” in economic work and called the Algerians “very responsible partners”. TSA, an independent Algiers news site whose name means Everything About Algeria, carried the remarks in an article by Ali Idir.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Dairy Exports Prompted the Remark

Stefan Duerr, head of the dairy group EkoNiva, asked Putin to extend a state scheme for Algerian milk-powder sales to other BRICS countries. Agriculture Minister Oksana Lut said Russian dry-milk shipments to Algeria rose fourfold this year.

Algerian news site Awras reported the remark in Arabic on Friday 16 October. It recalled a joint declaration from Tebboune’s June 2023 Moscow visit, which promised direct bank links and wider use of national currencies in trade.

Tebboune Set the Tone on 3 October

Putin calls Algeria a close ally about two weeks after Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, in office since December 2019, praised the same relationship. In a periodic meeting with national media broadcast on Saturday 3 October, Tebboune said ties “go back to before independence and have not changed.”

He added that if the friendship grows into economic integration, Algeria “will not say no”. Tebboune noted that Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov had visited only once in seven years, yet a phone call with Putin settles matters.

Russia Backs the UN Mission, Washington Backs Morocco

On Friday 9 October, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Alimov met Algeria’s ambassador in Moscow, Toufik Djouama, TSA reported from a Russian foreign ministry statement. Alimov backed keeping the UN presence in Western Sahara “in its present form” until a settlement.

That presence is MINURSO, the UN mission watching a ceasefire between Morocco and the Polisario Front since 1991. The Polisario is an independence movement backed by Algeria, and the Security Council votes on the mission at the end of October.

When Putin calls Algeria an ally, the United States stands on the other side of the Western Sahara argument. On Friday 25 September, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau backed Moroccan sovereignty over the territory, as the Rio Times reported on 26 September.

Morocco and Algeria have had no diplomatic relations since August 2021, and Western Sahara is the sharpest of their disputes. Moscow’s public support for the UN mission lines it up with Algiers, not with Washington or Rabat.

Why Algeria Matters Beyond Russia

Algeria covers 2.38 million square kilometres, and its gas pipelines under the Mediterranean, Transmed to Italy and Medgaz to Spain, feed southern Europe. It spent about US$25.4 billion on defence in 2025, the most in Africa, says SIPRI, the Stockholm peace research institute.

Algeria also courts other partners, and Awras reported that Tebboune stressed balanced relations with the United States and China as well as Russia. The wider contest for influence is mapped in the Rio Times piece on who backs whom in Africa.

What It Means for US Readers

Energy investors and diplomats should read the fact that Putin calls Algeria an ally as a signal of alignment, not a new contract. Algeria sells gas to Europe, so any shift in its ties to Moscow would feed into European energy security and the sanctions debate over Russia.

If Putin calls Algeria an ally and Moscow votes with Algiers, the result would test US efforts to settle the dispute for Morocco. US companies eyeing the Maghreb should expect Algeria to keep both Moscow and Washington at the table.

What Is Not Known

Putin’s remarks came with no gas, arms or trade figures, and neither government has announced a new agreement. Algeria’s presidency and foreign ministry have not published a reply to the remark at the time of writing.

The Security Council has not yet voted on the mission, so Russia’s final position is still to be seen. It is also open whether Putin and Tebboune will meet again before the end of the year.

More: Algeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Putin say about Algeria?

Putin calls Algeria one of Russia’s close friends and allies, in remarks of Thursday 15 October. He added that the two countries have never let each other down in economic cooperation.

Where and when did Putin make the remark?

He spoke by video link to the 21st forum-congress of Business Russia, an employers’ association, in a reply on dairy exports. Algeria’s TSA site reported it on Monday 19 October after the Russian embassy in Algiers shared it.

Did Algeria answer after Putin called Algeria an ally?

No reply has been published. Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune said on Saturday 3 October that relations with Russia had not changed and that Algeria would not refuse closer economic integration.

Why does the Putin Algeria ally message matter to the United States?

Algeria is a gas supplier to Europe and Africa’s biggest military spender. It also sits on the opposite side of Washington over Western Sahara, ahead of a UN Security Council vote at the end of October.

What is MINURSO?

MINURSO is the UN mission in Western Sahara, set up in 1991 to watch a ceasefire between Morocco and the Polisario Front. Russia says it wants the mission kept in its present form.

Sources: Kremlin transcript, Business Russia forum, 15 October 2026; TSA Algérie, 19 October 2026; TSA Algérie, 10 October 2026; Awras, 16 October 2026.

SOUTH AFRICA · US TRADE

Key Facts — The country South Africa is Africa’s most industrialised economy, a country of about 63 million people led by President Cyril Ramaphosa since 2018.

— Why it matters AGOA, the African Growth and Opportunity Act, lets eligible African countries sell thousands of products to the United States without import duties.

— What happened On Monday 19 October 2026, Ramaphosa said he must prepare South Africans for the possible loss of AGOA, Nigeria’s Punch and The Whistler reported.

— His words He said, “I need, as president, to prepare us if it ever happens,” and called the effect on jobs devastating.

— The backdrop Trump signed a two-year extension on Wednesday 2 September 2026, but eligibility is reviewed every year.

— What it means for you American importers of South African goods could face new duties after an AGOA loss.

— Still open Washington has not said it will remove South Africa, and the date of any decision is not public.

An AGOA loss became a planning topic on Monday 19 October, when President Cyril Ramaphosa said he must prepare South Africa for it. Nigeria’s Punch newspaper reported his remarks from Johannesburg.

South Africa is one of the largest users of AGOA, the US scheme that removes import duties on many African goods. Ramaphosa said losing it would be devastating for jobs, and that his government is already looking for other buyers.

What Ramaphosa Said on 19 October

Punch reported that Ramaphosa told South Africans he has a duty to get the country ready if AGOA access ends. He said, “I need, as president, to prepare us if it ever happens.”

He described the impact on jobs as devastating, the paper reported. He added that he and Deputy President Paul Mashatile are exploring other markets for South African goods.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on South Africa Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What AGOA Is and Why It Matters

The African Growth and Opportunity Act is a US law from 2000 that gives eligible sub-Saharan countries duty-free access to the American market. The US president decides each year which countries qualify, and Congress sets how long the scheme lasts.

South Africa supplied about half of the US$8.23 billion in goods exported under AGOA in 2024, Business Day reported, citing Oxford Economics. Roughly 22% of South African exports to the United States benefit from the scheme, BusinessTech reported.

The Extension That Did Not End the Worry

President Donald Trump signed a bill on Wednesday 2 September that moves AGOA’s end date to December 2028, BusinessTech reported. South Africa had asked for a 15-year extension, Business Day reported.

The AGOA country list can still change before January 2027. The US Trade Representative, America’s trade office, opened its 2027 review in June, and two 2025 bills to exclude South Africa have stalled.

Jobs and Exports at Stake

BusinessTech cited estimates that about half a million South African jobs depend on AGOA. The trade union Solidarity warned that exclusion would put thousands of specialised jobs at risk.

South African vehicle exports to the United States fell to R8 billion (about US$0.49 billion) in 2025, from R17.7 billion (about US$1.08 billion) in 2024. Business Day also reported a 25% US tariff on cars, parts, steel and aluminium.

Pretoria Looks to China and Others

Punch reported that Ramaphosa pointed to China’s zero-tariff scheme for African exports, which began in May, as one route to new buyers. He did not give figures for what the Chinese scheme could be worth to South African exporters.

Washington, Beijing and Moscow compete for African partners, as set out in this guide to who backs whom in Africa. The car industry faces more pressure after the end of state support for kit-car plants, covered in this report on the kit-car decision.

What It Means for US Readers

American companies that import South African vehicles, steel, aluminium and other goods could face higher duties after an AGOA loss. Investors in South African exporters should watch the January 2027 eligibility decision.

After an AGOA loss, Ramaphosa pointed to China as a possible new buyer while ties with Washington stay strained. That matters for US firms competing for South African contracts and for American officials who want a trade partner on the continent.

What Is Not Known

Ramaphosa did not say that Washington has told South Africa it will lose AGOA access, and its eligibility is unchanged. No date for a US decision on South Africa’s eligibility has been made public.

The remarks were reported from Johannesburg, and the Presidency has not yet released the full text of his statement. The size of any duty South African exporters would face without AGOA depends on a US decision that has not been taken.

More: South Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is AGOA?

AGOA is the African Growth and Opportunity Act, a US law that lets eligible sub-Saharan countries sell many goods to the United States duty-free. It passed in 2000 and now runs to December 2028.

Has South Africa lost AGOA?

No, South Africa stays eligible for now, and an AGOA loss is only a possibility. Ramaphosa said he must prepare for the possibility that it ends.

How many jobs depend on AGOA in South Africa?

BusinessTech cited estimates of about half a million jobs. The union Solidarity warned that thousands of specialised jobs would be at risk if South Africa were excluded.

When could South Africa be removed from AGOA?

The eligibility list can be changed before January 2027, and the US Trade Representative opened its 2027 review in June. No decision on South Africa has been announced.

Why does AGOA matter to American readers?

US importers and investors buy South African goods that enter under the scheme. Loss of AGOA could raise import costs and shift supply chains.
