World.title: Colombia Army Black Hawk Crashes in Cauca
World.content:
Key Facts —Who. The Colombian Army: four crew and 15 soldiers of the platoon Báltico 2, Third Division. —What. A Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk crashed on a supply and personnel transport flight; all 19 aboard are alive. —Where. On the route between Popayán and Inzá, Cauca department, Colombia. —When. Monday afternoon, 19 October 2026, local time (UTC-5). —Injuries. Four people with fractures and 15 with bruises, all in stable condition. —Cause. Not known; Army specialists and technicians are being sent to investigate. —Why it matters. The helicopter is US-built, and Colombia’s Army flies US-made aircraft. —Status. As of 20:15 GMT, 19 October 2026

A Colombian Army Black Hawk helicopter crashed in Cauca on Monday afternoon local time, with 19 people aboard. All survived, the Army says, and the aircraft is a US-built Sikorsky.

What We Know

The Army confirmed that a UH-60 Black Hawk crashed between Popayán and Inzá in Cauca department. The accident happened on Monday afternoon local time (UTC-5).

Nineteen people were aboard: four crew members and 15 soldiers. The soldiers, one non-commissioned officer and 14 professional soldiers, belong to the platoon known as Báltico 2.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

El Tiempo places the platoon in the Army’s Third Division. It links the unit to Brigade 29 and the BILOP7 light infantry battalion.

One El Tiempo headline mentions only the 15 soldiers, while other outlets count 19 including the crew. We use 19, because that figure includes the four crew members.

The Army says no one died, stating that everyone is alive. El Tiempo and El Espectador report four injured with fractures and 15 with bruises, all in stable condition.

The aircraft was flying a military supply and personnel transport mission. El Tiempo identifies it by the registration EJC 2175.

The Army is sending specialists and technicians to begin an investigation into what happened. No cause has been announced so far.

El Espectador reports system failures that caused a loss of altitude. The Army has not confirmed that account.

What Is Not Known

The cause of the crash is not known. The Army says an investigation will begin.

The exact crash site and the terrain are not known. Neither is the condition of the aircraft.

It is also not known whether hostile fire has been ruled out. We do not speculate, and we will report what investigators say.

Background: A US-Built Helicopter in Cauca

The Black Hawk is a US-designed helicopter built by Sikorsky. Militaries around the world use it for troop and cargo transport.

Colombia’s Army operates US-made aircraft such as this one. Any link to US-supplied equipment will depend on the Army’s investigation.

Cauca lies in south-western Colombia. The reports on this crash describe an accident and do not mention an attack.

Peru also flies Black Hawks, as we reported in Peru Pays US to Keep 9 Black Hawks Flying. For more on the country, see our Colombia coverage.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

No deaths were reported, and the aircraft is US-made. The Army’s investigation has only just begun.

Travelers in Cauca should follow official local guidance and the US State Department’s travel advisory for Colombia. The reports we reviewed describe an accident involving military personnel only.

We have no information on road closures or other disruption in Cauca. We will report any new official details on the injured and the cause.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened to the Colombian Army Black Hawk in Cauca?

A UH-60 Black Hawk crashed on Monday afternoon local time on the route between Popayán and Inzá. The Army says all 19 people aboard are alive.

Were there any deaths in the Colombia Black Hawk crash?

No deaths have been reported. Four people suffered fractures and 15 suffered bruises, according to El Tiempo and El Espectador.

What caused the Colombian Army helicopter accident?

The cause is not known, and the Army is sending specialists and technicians to investigate. El Espectador reports system failures that caused a loss of altitude, which the Army has not confirmed.

Why does the Cauca crash matter to US readers?

The Black Hawk is a US-designed Sikorsky helicopter, and Colombia’s Army operates US-made aircraft. The crash caused no reported deaths, and the cause is still under investigation.

World.title: Brazil Shifts US$4 Billion in Next Budget
World.content:
The National Congress in Brasília, where the Senate would try any impeachment of a Supreme Court justice. File photo, 2024. (Photo: Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Brazil Economy · Federal Budget

Published Monday, 19 October, 4:05 p.m. ET · Source: Brazil’s Ministry of Planning and Budget

Key Facts —The number. About R$20 billion (US$4.0 billion) of 2027 federal spending will be moved to make room for new measures. —The scale. The ministry says the sum is a little over 1% of the spending that counts against Brazil’s legal spending cap. —The promise. The ministry says the total spending cap and the primary budget target will not change. —The reason. The government has announced a Bolsa Família increase and debt renegotiation for small business owners since the start of the year. —Still unknown. Which spending lines will shrink; the ministry gave no list.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 76.3% · Lula 23.5% (US$188 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 79% · Lula 22% As of 19 October, 7:20 pm ET (00:20 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Brazil’s Ministry of Planning and Budget said on Monday, 19 October, that it will move about R$20 billion (US$4.0 billion) within the federal budget for 2027 to pay for measures adopted in recent months. The ministry said the sum is a little over 1% of the spending that counts against the cap, a rule that limits how fast federal spending can grow.

For investors holding the real or Brazilian bonds, the question is whether the Brazil economy can pay for election-year promises without loosening its fiscal rules. The ministry says it can, and that the adjustments will keep both the total cap and the primary result target, the budget balance before interest payments.

The real traded near R$5.05 per dollar on Monday afternoon, according to RT market data, and our real to dollar guide explains what moves it.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Ministry Said

The ministry issued its note to the press on Monday afternoon and did not name the spending lines that will be cut or delayed. It said the changes will go to Congress once a rapporteur, the lawmaker who steers the bill, is named for the 2027 budget bill.

The reallocation covers measures the government has announced during the year, among them a Bolsa Família increase and debt renegotiation for micro-entrepreneurs, known as MEIs. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a leftist who is seeking re-election, faces a runoff vote on 25 October.

The Praça dos Três Poderes in Brasília, with the National Congress towers in the background. File photo. Photo: Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the New Measures Cost

Bolsa Família, Brazil’s cash-transfer programme for low-income families, will rise 15.04%, at a cost of about R$22.7 billion (US$4.5 billion) in 2027, according to reports of the ministry’s figures. That one item alone is larger than the R$20 billion being moved.

Desenrola 3.0, a debt-renegotiation programme for households, is put at R$15 billion (US$3.0 billion) through 2028, of which R$5 billion (US$1.0 billion) falls in the first year. The ministry also lists credit lines for app-based drivers, an expanded Pé-de-Meia student stipend, free public transport and support for MEIs.

Dollar figures here use the RT rate of R$5.05 per dollar on 19 October. The R$20 billion is a reallocation inside the cap, not new spending on top of it, and it is not the total cost of the measures.

What It Means for US Readers

The sum is small against a federal budget of this size, but investors watch it as a test of discipline. Brazil’s spending cap and primary target are the anchors for Brazilian bonds and for the real, and for US funds such as the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ).

If Congress accepts the shift without raising the cap, the plan will read as fiscally neutral. If lawmakers or the next government loosen the cap instead, the risk premium on Brazilian assets could rise, a point that matters to anyone holding reais or planning to relocate there.

What Is Not Known

The ministry has not said which programmes will give up money, or when it will send the proposal to Congress. Lawmakers can change the proposal before it takes effect.

The next data point is the September budget balance, due on Friday 30 October at 7:30 a.m. ET, according to the RT calendar. The central bank’s rate committee follows with its interest-rate decision on Wednesday 4 November at 4:30 p.m. ET.

Our guide to the Brazilian economy follows the budget and rates as the numbers arrive.

Background: Brazil Election Results Put Lula and Flávio in Runoff.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Brazil’s government announce about the 2027 budget?

The Ministry of Planning and Budget said on 19 October that it will move about R$20 billion (US$4.0 billion) within 2027 federal spending. It says the total spending cap and the primary result target will stay the same.

How big is R$20 billion compared with the spending cap?

The ministry says it is a little over 1% of the spending subject to the cap. The cap is the rule that limits real growth in federal spending.

How does this affect the real?

The ministry gave no market-moving figure, and the real traded near R$5.05 per dollar on Monday afternoon. Investors will watch whether Congress keeps the cap intact.

What measures is the money for?

The ministry did not itemise the R$20 billion. Recent measures include a 15.04% Bolsa Família increase, the Desenrola 3.0 debt programme and support for micro-entrepreneurs.

World.title: Coast Guard member Lionel Logan critically injured, Julian Dyer shot in attack on SUV in Corozal
World.content:
Coast Guard member Lionel Logan critically injured, Julian Dyer shot in attack on SUV in Corozal

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A member of the Belize Coast Guard was critically injured and another man wounded after gunmen opened fire on a vehicle travelling along the Philip Goldson Highway near Carolina Village, Corozal District, on Sunday evening, October 18, 2026.

The victims have been identified as 35-year-old Lionel Logan, a Belize Coast Guard member from Libertad Village, and 35-year-old Julian Dyer, a construction worker from Corozal Town.

According to initial reports, the men were travelling in a black Chevrolet Equinox with several other passengers after leaving a football game in Carolina Village when a black van carrying approximately four men pulled alongside their vehicle. Occupants of the van reportedly opened fire on the SUV, striking both men.

Logan sustained multiple gunshot wounds to his left forearm, lower abdomen and the back of his head. He was transferred to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital in Belize City, where he was listed in critical condition. His current condition has not been independently confirmed.

Dyer suffered pellet injuries to his right forearm and lower abdomen. He was treated at the Corozal Community Hospital but subsequently discharged himself.

A nine-year-old girl travelling with her mother also sustained a minor cut to the palm of her right hand, reportedly caused by shattered glass. Both managed to escape from the vehicle during the attack.

The Chevrolet Equinox was later found abandoned in the San Antonio Village area with multiple apparent bullet holes and shattered windows.

The motive for the attack remains unknown, and no suspects have been publicly identified. Police investigations continue.

World.title: Deon Jones, Lloyd Faber injured as gunman opens fire on group socializing on King Street
World.content:
Deon Jones, Lloyd Faber injured as gunman opens fire on group socializing on King Street

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating an attempted murder incident in Belize City that left two men injured after a gunman opened fire on a group socializing on King Street on Saturday night, October 17, 2026.

The victims have been identified as 27-year-old Deon Jones and 43-year-old Lloyd Faber, a stevedore, both residents of Belize City.

According to police, around 10:20 p.m., four men were socializing in a yard on King Street when an unidentified male emerged from behind a building and fired several shots in their direction, striking Jones and Faber.

Police received reports of the shooting around 10:30 p.m. and responded to the scene, where they learned that both injured men had already been transported to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital for treatment.

The extent of their injuries has not been disclosed, and police have not established a motive for the attack.

The shooting comes amid renewed concerns about gun violence in Belize City, following a series of murders reported earlier this month.

Police investigations continue.

World.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs and OAS discuss Belize-Guatemala relations
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs and OAS discuss Belize-Guatemala relations

By Zoila Palma: Today, Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca met with Ambassador Antonia Urrejola, Special Representative of the Secretary General of the Organization of American States (OAS) for Belize-Guatemala relations, to discuss matters relating to the Belize-Guatemala relationship and ongoing regional engagement.

The meeting was attended by Oscar Arnold, Chief Executive Officer for Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, and Directors of International Affairs, Ambassador Ayesha Borland and Ambassador Alfonso Gahona.

World.title: Muffles College counsellor Hayden Mendez charged with sexual assault and encouraging child pornography
World.content:
Muffles College counsellor Hayden Mendez charged with sexual assault and encouraging child pornography

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 31-year-old counsellor at Muffles College in Orange Walk has been criminally charged following allegations of sexual misconduct involving a 17-year-old female student.

Hayden Mendez appeared in court on Monday, October 19, 2026, charged with sexual assault and encouraging child pornography. He was granted bail.

According to Assistant Superintendent of Police Stacy Smith, the investigation began after police discovered a screenshot circulating on social media suggesting sexually explicit interactions between the counsellor and the student.

Investigators subsequently visited the school, contacted the student and her parent, and involved the Human Services Department. Police recorded several statements and collected evidence before bringing charges against Mendez.

Smith indicated that the alleged incidents occurred between 2025 and 2026, describing the allegations as a breach of trust involving an adult employed at the institution.

Police are also conducting a separate investigation into how the school’s administration handled the allegations, including whether appropriate action was taken after the matter was brought to its attention.

Last week, BBN reported that Muffles College had placed a staff member on administrative leave after receiving an allegation of misconduct on October 6. The school pledged to cooperate with investigations by police and social services.

Police have not determined whether there are additional alleged victims and are encouraging anyone with relevant information or similar experiences to come forward.

Mendez has not been convicted of the offences, and the allegations remain before the court.

World.title: Belize hosts regional workshop to strengthen Tax compliance and Revenue management
World.content:
Belize hosts regional workshop to strengthen Tax compliance and Revenue management

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Tax Service Department, under the Ministry of Finance, is hosting the 3rd Compliance Risk Management (CRM) Community of Practice Workshop from October 19 to 22, 2026, at the Best Western Belize Biltmore Plaza in Belize City. The workshop aims to strengthen tax compliance and revenue management across the Caribbean.

The four-day event brings together tax administration representatives from Belize, Barbados, Curaçao, Guyana, Grenada and Jamaica, with technical support from the International Monetary Fund’s Fiscal Affairs Department and the Caribbean Regional Technical Assistance Centre. Participants are discussing ways to improve taxpayer compliance, protect government revenues and deliver more effective services while making better use of limited resources.

During the workshop, participating countries are sharing their experiences in applying Compliance Risk Management, including initiatives, results, challenges and lessons learned. Director General of the Belize Tax Service, Michelle Longsworth, emphasized the importance of using information to improve compliance. “The real value comes from how we use information – how we turn data into intelligence, intelligence into action, and action into measurable improvements in taxpayer compliance,” she stated.

The workshop comes as Belize continues efforts to modernize its tax administration, strengthen data-driven strategies and encourage voluntary compliance.

World.title: International News: Former Mexican Attorney General arrested on treason suspicion over U.S. agents’ role in drug raid
World.content:
International News: Former Mexican Attorney General arrested on treason suspicion over U.S. agents’ role in drug raid

By Zoila Palma: Former Chihuahua Attorney General César Jáuregui has been arrested on suspicion of treason after Mexican authorities alleged that he allowed U.S. personnel to participate in a drug raid without the authorization required under Mexican law.

Mexican Attorney General Ernestina Godoy announced the arrest on Saturday, following months of investigation.

According to Reuters, prosecutors allege that Jáuregui authorized U.S. agents to participate in an “irregular” raid on a suspected drug laboratory in April in Chihuahua, a northern Mexican state bordering the United States.

Godoy said the investigation found that he may have allowed foreign personnel to take part in operations reserved exclusively for Mexico’s national security forces.

The case has heightened sensitivities surrounding U.S. involvement in Mexican security operations.

In April, the United States confirmed that two employees of its embassy in Mexico City had died, without identifying their agencies. Sources familiar with the matter said the two were CIA officers involved in anti-narcotics efforts.

President Claudia Sheinbaum has maintained that Mexico welcomes intelligence sharing and bilateral cooperation against organized crime but does not permit U.S. agents or forces to participate directly in operations on Mexican territory.

World.title: International News: Super El Niño shows signs of expanding as Ocean temperatures surge
World.content:
International News: Super El Niño shows signs of expanding as Ocean temperatures surge

By Zoila Palma: New sea-surface temperature maps show an extensive area of unusually warm water across the equatorial Pacific, with another band of warming stretching south from Peru and Ecuador toward Chile.

The development has been described as a “second arm” of the ongoing Super El Niño, although meteorologists clarify that it is not a separate El Niño event, Yahoo reports.

In an October 16 bulletin, Peru’s multisector El Niño commission (ENFEN) reported that Pacific sea-surface temperatures continue to show positive anomalies with an upward trend. Meteorologists noted that the warming extends toward the southeast, with localized ocean temperatures exceeding historical averages by more than 3 degrees Celsius.

ENFEN expects coastal warming off Peru to remain at “extraordinary” intensity through January 2027, while very strong El Niño conditions in the central Pacific are expected to continue into February.

Climate scientist Zeke Hausfather has suggested that the event could become the strongest in 1,000 years if current models accurately predict its peak, although this remains a forecast rather than a confirmed record.

El Niño can disrupt trade winds and shift storm patterns, increasing the risk of flooding, landslides, coastal erosion and extreme weather in some regions.

World.title: Fisheries Department seizes over 1,000 feet of illegal gillnet
World.content:
Fisheries Department seizes over 1,000 feet of illegal gillnet

Photo by PG TV

By Zoila Palma: The Fisheries Department has reportedly retrieved more than 1,000 feet of illegally deployed gillnet during a night operation near the Temash-Sarstoon area, following reports of illegal fishing activity south of Punta Gorda.

PG TV first reported suspected illegal fishing in the area.

Fisheries officers responded by patrolling the waters and locating the illegal fishing gear.

Gillnets are illegal in Belize, and their use threatens the country’s marine resources.

The community has since expressed appreciation to the Fisheries Department for its quick response.

World.title: Fi Wi Land: Beyond the duppy stories, discover the value of Jamaica’s bats
World.content:
Often misunderstood and surrounded by folklore, bats are among nature’s hardest-working environmental protectors, helping to control insect populations, pollinate plants and disperse seeds. Discover more about these fascinating creatures as the Jamaica Observer in association with the National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA) premieres ‘Fi Wi Land’ on Monday.

In the debut episode, host Carlysia Ramdeen is joined by NEPA Environmental Officer Damany Calder who shares insights about bats, their importance to Jamaica’s ecosystems and why they deserve greater appreciation.

The new 12-week environmental series by the Jamaica Observer and NEPA explores Jamaica’s unique wildlife, ecosystems and natural resources while highlighting efforts to protect the island’s environment for future generations.

Catch the premiere on the Jamaica Observer’s YouTube channel and other digital platforms.

World.title: Proud moment for Barnswells as husband and wife conferred with national award
World.content:
Councillor Scean Barnswell and wife Danielle pose for a photograph after receiving their Badge of Honour for Gallantry at the 2026 Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards at King’s House on Monday, October 19. 2026. (Photo: Llewellyn Wynter)

It was a historic and proud moment for the Barnswell family from Clarendon, when the husband and wife team of Councillor Scean Barnswell and Danielle Anna-Marie Barnswell stood on the dais at King’s House Monday morning to accept their national award – the Badge of Honour for Gallantry, from Governor General Sir Patrick Allen.

The occasion was the 2026 Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards.

The Barnswells were among 149 Jamaicans who were honoured for outstanding contributions in various fields.

The two were recognised for their “quick and courageous” actions that led to the rescue of a six-year-old girl who was reportedly abducted from the St Thomas More Preparatory School in May Pen Clarendon on December 9 last year.

“In growing up you’re told to mind your business but in Jamaica, the children are all our business so in this case I’m happy we did that and I wouldn’t change anything,” said Mrs Barnswell during rehearsals for Monday’s ceremony.

Scean Barnswell is the councillor for the Hayes division in the Clarendon Municipal Corporation and a former Mayor of May Pen. He is looking to return to that position as the balance of power in the corporation recently swung from the Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) to the Opposition People’s National Party (PNP).

This came after the JLP-elected councillor for the May Pen North division, Tanya-Lee Williams, resigned from the JLP, giving the PNP a clear 12-10 majority in the corporation. The PNP has stated that this gives it the right to appoint the mayor and deputy mayor but a court injunction granted last Friday has stalled those plans. The PNP has said it will be going back to court.

According to reports from December 2025, Barnswell and his wife spotted a man walking with a small child along Bustamante Highway and, sensing something was wrong, immediately intervened. Their actions resulted in the safe recovery of the child and the capture of the suspect, who was arrested by the police.

In a statement at the time, the PNP described the incident as an act of humanity, noting that Councillor Barnswell showed decisive, selfless leadership in a moment of crisis. The party said his response reflected the values of community vigilance and public service and urged others to do likewise.

WATCH: Barnswell honoured for rescuing abducted six-year-old

The PNP also expressed gratitude to members of the public who raised the alarm and commended the Jamaica Constabulary Force for its swift response.

“It emphasised the importance of strong community–police partnerships in protecting children and preventing crimes of this nature,” the party said.

-Lynford Simpson

World.title: Fresh questions over MVP as Clayton twins linked to new track setup
World.content:
The twin sprinting duo of Tia (left) and Tina Clayton. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

Rumours of sprint twins Tia and Tina Clayton possibly leaving MVP Track Club for a new professional outfit being established by coach Corey Bennett – reportedly with funding from athletics wear giant Nike –have raised fresh questions about the future of one of Jamaica’s most successful athletics programmes.

Neither the Clayton sisters, Bennett nor Nike have publicly confirmed the reported move.

Observer Online reached out to the MVP President Bruce James for a confirmation or denial and his terse response was, “we do not respond to rumours”.

However, the rumours come at a particularly sensitive time for MVP, following the death of its founder and long-time head coach Stephen Francis on July 4 this year.

For over two decades, Francis was the standard bearer of MVP, building the club from its inception into an internationally respected sprinting powerhouse that produced world beaters including Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce, Elaine Thompson-Herah, Asafa Powell, Shericka Jackson, and now Kishane Thompson.

His demanding training methods, technical expertise and ability to identify and develop talent made MVP a major force in Jamaican and international athletics. Under his leadership, the club became synonymous with sprinting excellence and helped establish Jamaica as a dominant power on the global stage.

Francis’s death has therefore left more than a coaching vacancy. It has created questions about succession, athlete retention and whether the system he built can maintain its identity and success without its central figure.

The Clayton twins are among the club’s most promising younger professionals and represent an important part of its future. The sisters emerged from Edwin Allen High School under coach Michael Dyke before joining MVP in 2022 after signing professional contracts with Nike.

Both enjoyed outstanding junior careers, helping Jamaica win world under-20 titles. Tina has since established herself among the world’s leading senior sprinters. She won silver in the 100 metres at the 2025 World Athletics Championships in Tokyo before capturing the Diamond League Final title in Brussels in September 2026. Tia meanwhile has stepped out of her twin sister’s shadow and, at just age 19, placed a creditable seventh in the women’s 100m final at the Olympic Games.

Their development has been a significant part of MVP’s ongoing talent pipeline, making any potential departure noteworthy, even though no move has been confirmed.

The suggestion that Bennett could establish a new training group also raises broader questions about the next phase of Jamaican athletics, particularly as coaches seek to attract and retain elite athletes in an increasingly competitive professional environment.

It has been reported that promising hurdler Kerrica Hill has left MVP to join her high school coach Bennett. The two-time world Under-20 100 m champion’s departure is significant and follows that of Olympic bronze medallist Rasheed Broadbell, who joined the Lonnie Green coaching camp in the United States.

If the rumours prove true, the implications for MVP could extend beyond the loss of two talented sprinters. It would add to the pressure on the club to demonstrate that its coaching structure, athlete-development system and international appeal can endure beyond the man who built its reputation.

The challenge is whether MVP can successfully transition from a programme so closely identified with one influential coach into an organisation capable of sustaining its standards under new leadership.

For now, the Clayton twins’ future remains uncertain, and the reported Nike-backed Bennett project has yet to be confirmed. But the speculation has placed a spotlight on a bigger question: who will carry the MVP legacy forward in the post-Francis era?

World.title: ‘Cherish our heritage’
World.content:
Opposition Leader Mark Golding (right) shares a word with Minister of Culture Olivia Grange at the National Heritage Week Thanksgiving Service at Church of the Open Bible on Washington Boulevard, in St Andrew, on Sunday. At left is state minister in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce Delano Seiveright. (Photo: Karl Mclarty)

PASTOR of Lakes Pen Apostolic Church, Overseer Cassel Dunkley is urging Jamaicans to reclaim the everyday acts of kindness and respect that once brought communities together.

He argued that the country’s heritage is found not only in its national heroes, anthem, and history books, but also in the values passed down through generations as Jamaica confronts mounting challenges.

Dunkley, who was addressing the National Heritage Week Thanksgiving Church Service on Sunday at Church of the Open Bible on Washington Boulevard, in St Andrew, said Jamaica must preserve the traditions that taught people to care for their neighbours, help grieving families, and treat other people’s children as their own.

He recalled a time when a family experiencing a death could expect relatives and neighbours to arrive with food and other assistance, contrasting that tradition with what he described as a loss of community spirit.

“When somebody died in the country, granny came with a bunch of bananas, auntie came with something, cousin came with something.

Nowadays, when somebody dies, it becomes a party. We want beer, we want Red Stripe, and black stripe, and white stripe.

But I come from a heritage that when something happens, your neighbour is going to look out for you — [and] those are the things we want to get back to,” Dunkley said.

He also called for a return to the close community relationships in which neighbours shared responsibility for children and looked out for one another, regardless of whether they expected anything in return.

“We want to get back and cherish the heritage where your tears become my tears, when I try to do something to help you more than try to do something to belittle you,” he said.

Dunkley said Jamaica’s heritage must also be reflected in how people treat others. “We must cherish respect for all, irrespective of your belief.

We must learn to love, forgive, and respect each other. But sometimes we allow material things to shift our focus, and we judge people by the car they drive, we judge them by the place they live.

But remember… we are one blood,” he said. “Love those who can’t buy you a shirt.

Love those who can’t give you nothing in return. Because sometimes we only give to those who can give back to us, we only are kind to those who can be kind back to us.

But somebody around the corner is looking for your love, somebody who hurt you is looking and waiting for your forgiveness,” Dunkley said.

He argued that preserving the country’s heritage requires Jamaicans to remember the lessons taught by previous generations, including honesty, respect for others, and responsibility for the wider community.

Dunkley recalled how children were expected to return items they found if those items did not belong to them, saying such lessons should not be lost as the country develops.

“Do you remember the time in Jamaica when if you brought home a pen, your mother says, ‘Where did you get it from?’ and granny tied her head and said, ‘We are going to school with you in the morning because you have to give it back’? We couldn’t say ‘finders keepers’; we were taught to return the things that do not belong to us.

We cannot afford to lose that heritage,” he said. Beyond these everyday customs, Dunkley reminded the congregation of the sacrifices made by Jamaica’s national heroes and other leaders in shaping the country’s history.

Dunkley said Jamaicans have much to be thankful for, including the country’s educational institutions and the role the Church played and continues to play in society.

He urged Jamaicans not to allow negative news and the country’s problems to overshadow its achievements.

“But I borrow the words of [Governor General] Sir Patrick Allen. He said, ‘We can use what is right about Jamaica to fix what is not right,’ ” Dunkley said.

He also called for greater civic pride, including respect for the environment, and recalled school lessons that encouraged children to pick up litter and keep their surroundings clean.

Dunkley also called for Jamaica’s national anthem and pledge to be given greater prominence at public gatherings, arguing that the words and values they represent should remain part of the country’s everyday life.

He said Jamaica’s history and traditions should help guide the country through its present difficulties, adding that people must understand their past if they are to make sound decisions about the future.

“We must cherish our heritage! We might have different theological beliefs… but, brothers and sisters, we must embrace and understand where we are coming from — because if we don’t know where we are coming from we will not know where we are going,” said Dunkley.

World.title: PM wants security forces to get tougher on criminals
World.content:
HOLNESS...we must stop making excuses for men who carry illegal guns, terrorise communities, and prey upon the vulnerable.

PRIME Minister Dr Andrew Holness has urged the leadership of the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) to intensify its efforts to go after criminal gangs and the people who support them.

Holness, who returned to the island on Saturday, was immediately briefed by Police Commissioner Dr Kevin Blake about the developments in the Five Miles area off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine which left five men — JCF members Corporal Trevoy Shaw, and Constable Devoney Rose; and civilians Errol Hussey, his son Malique Hussey, and nephew Javoun Cogle — dead, and a 10-year-old girl nursing a gunshot wound.

In his response Holness offered condolence to the families of the dead cops, the hope for the full recovery of the injured child, and expressed relief that other civilians who were in the house escaped unharmed.

The prime minister said the reports on the incident provide a stark reminder that Jamaica cannot let its guard down or relax the laws.

“We must maintain our resolute posture against organised criminal violence. The emerging accounts of this incident point to a disturbing level of planning and coordination. You reported that there was misdirection, diversionary gunfire from outside, [and] there was support and prearranged transport. All of this must be fully investigated.

“We must uncover and dismantle every person, every network, every resource, every facilitator who enabled this violence,” added Holness.

He said the police account also reveals something even more chilling, that the gunmen were willing to use members of their own households as shields to protect themselves.

“This is the kind of evil that we are confronted with in our society. These men had a choice, they could have put down their weapons, they could have surrendered and had their day in court. Instead they chose lethal violence,” Holness said.

“But let me be blunt, we must separate these evil men from our society. We must stop making excuses for men who carry illegal guns, terrorise communities, and prey upon the vulnerable. They are not protectors; they are not justified by poverty, exclusion, or social injustice. They are not freedom fighters, they are not Robin Hoods, they are not rebels or misunderstood victims. They are parasites and pestilence upon our society,” declared Holness.

According to the prime minister, these criminals are obstructions to the progress of the society, which is better off without them.

“They must be identified, disarmed, arrested, prosecuted, and removed from our communities through the full force and uncompromising force of the law. There can be no moral equivalency. There can be no romanticising of guns; no glorifying of gunmen; and no tolerance for those who shelter finance, arm, and celebrate them. We must never comfort ourselves with the illusion that organised terror cannot exist in our communities,” said Holness.

He said the attack on the security forces on Friday has shaken members but it has not diluted the resolve of both the JCF and the Jamaica Defence Force.

Holness said the National Security Council will have its regular monthly meeting this week during which it we will review the situation.

“But I can tell you from now, commissioner… the policy direction is that you should intensify the operations that you have planned to target the criminals, the gang leaders, those who you have been pursuing with intelligence.

“Bring them forward. Intensify it. Because what this has shown is a new level of criminal organisation that is a threat to our national security. Whatever resources you need, we will discuss it but you should make a big push now to get as many of these who are just lying in wait to confront and challenge the security of the country,” added Holness.

He argued that Friday’s incident in Five Miles must be used as a watershed and a turning point as it underscored that there are people with criminal intent and the capability and wherewithal to unleash terror on the society.

“And we must meet them head on. We must meet them head on and maintain our civility and the rule of law. So the word to all gunman: ‘Tek weh unnuself!’ ” declared Holness.

World.title: Police step up hunt for alleged killer ‘Papa’
World.content:
Alleged gang enforcer Kenroy “Papa” Williams who has been linked to at least five murders.

AN islandwide manhunt is now on for Kenroy “Papa” Willis who the police have described as a “high-risk target” linked to at least five murders committed across sections of St Andrew between May 2024 and May 2025.

Jamaica Observer sources say 25-year-old Willis was the main target of an early morning operation last Friday in the Five Miles area, off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine, which left five men dead and a 10-year-old girl nursing gunshot wounds.

The dead men have since been identified as Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) members Corporal Trevoy Shaw and Constable Devoney Rose; and civilians Errol Hussey, his son Malique Hussey, and nephew Javoun Cogle.

According to the Observer sources, Malique Hussey, otherwise called Mal Boss, is a known associate of Willis who is of a Rose Hall District, Lawrence Tavern, St Andrew, address.

Willis has been identified in the JCF’s Violence Producers Workbook as an alleged enforcer of the Rose Hall gang and a suspect in several serious violent crimes, including murder, shootings and robberies.

He is specifically wanted in connection with the October 26, 2024 murder of Verne Ewan Joseph along Essex Hall Main Road.

Willis has also been linked to the killing of Alexian Daley in Mahoney District, Lawrence Tavern, on May 26, 2024; Matthew Williams, who was killed at Lawrence Tavern Square on June 14, 2024; Oshane Blackwood, who was killed along Brooks Level Road, Stony Hill, on May 11, 2025.

Three of the five killings occurred within approximately five weeks in 2024, all in communities in and around Lawrence Tavern. The sources say the police are now targeting several locations where Willis may have sought refuge or maintained connections, including Golden Spring, Lawrence Tavern, Glengoffe in St Catherine, and Bull Bay and Clarks Hill in St Andrew. The police have previously conducted targeted raids as part of their efforts to locate Willis, and Friday’s operation was believed to be the latest move by the cops to nab him. The sources say there was gunfire in areas outside the zone the police had cordoned off during the operation, and they suspect this was an effort by Willis, or his cronies, to distract them while they were being fired on from inside the house. Willis has remained the subject of police interest throughout 2026, with published reports identifying him as wanted for murder and under investigation in connection with other violent crimes. “Willis’s reported gang affiliation, alleged involvement in multiple murders, and associations with other suspected violent offenders have made him a subject of sustained police interest,” added the Observer source.

World.title: NUFF offers more than enough
World.content:
From left: Nadean Rawlings, director, NUFF; Alisa Jones, production assistant, NUFF; and Jesse Royal, recording artiste (Aceion Cunningham)

Negril Universal Film Festival (NUFF), formerly known as the Skylark Film Festival, brought four days of Jamaican and international storytelling from Thursday, October 8, to Sunday, October 11.

The weekend paired film screenings with conversations, industry sessions, culture and hands-on learning, creating a gathering for audiences and emerging film-makers alike.

The festival, now in its 7th staging, opened with a special 25th-anniversary screening of Stephanie Black’s landmark documentary

Life and Debt. The film’s examination of Jamaica and the forces shaping its economy provided a fitting starting point for a conversation about the issues it raised and how they resonate a quarter-century later.

On Friday, the programme shifted from film-maker development by day to a celebration of Jamaican storytelling in the evening. The WES Studios-sponsored Vertical Film-making Masterclass, led by Richard Lawson of Hyperlens Studios, offered practical insight into a changing screen format. Documentary shorts and opportunities to learn, connect, and exchange ideas rounded out the daytime programme.

Friday night’s Jamaican Film Block gave way to a special Jimmy Cliff tribute featuring his daughter Odessa Chambers. Storm Saulter then presented the first two episodes of his new

SKY-TV series,

Possession. An in-depth conversation and question-and-answer session invited the audience to explore the series and its creative vision with the film-maker.

World.title: 149 outstanding Jamaicans to be honoured today
World.content:
Members of the Jamaica Defence Force in rehearsal on Saturday for today’s Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards at King’s House. (Photos: Naphtali Junior)

Six Jamaicans will receive the nation’s fifth highest honour, the Order of Jamaica (OJ), at the 2026 Ceremony of Investiture and Presentation of National Honours and Awards today at King’s House.

They are the former Bank of Jamaica Governor Richard Byles; Minister of Energy, Transport and Telecommunications Daryl Vaz; Chief Executive Officer of Sagicor Group Jamaica Christopher Zacca; philanthropist Donette Chin-Loy Chang; former Government minister Maxine Henry-Wilson; and former Government minister Derrick Smith.

They will be among the 140 Jamaicans who will be recognised for their sterling contribution to nation-building. The ceremony is scheduled to take place on the lawns of King’s House, starting at 9:00 am.

Twenty-five people will be conferred with the Order of Distinction in the rank of Commander; 41 with the Order of Distinction in the rank of Officer; 33 with the Badge of Honour for Meritorious Service; and 30 with the Badge of Honour for Long and Faithful Service.

Three civilians will receive the Badge of Honour for Gallantry. They are Danielle Anna-Marie Barnswell and her husband, Councillor Scean Barnswell, as well as Susan Annmarie Higgins.

As customary, several members of the unformed groups will be awarded with the Medal of Honour for Meritorious Service — 25 from the Jamaica Constabulary Force; 13 from the Department of Correctional Service; 15 from the Jamaica Fire Brigade; and 12 from the Jamaica Defence Force.

The ceremony will be presided over by Governor General Sir Patrick Allen. Under the National Honours and Awards Act, promulgated on July 18, 1969, provision is made for those outstanding Jamaicans to be conferred with one of the honours of the Orders of the six Societies of Honour.

The six honours by rank are Order of National Hero, Order of the Nation, Order of Excellence, Order of Merit, Order of Jamaica, and the Order of Distinction. There is also the Medal of Honour and Badge of Honour, which recognises gallantry and meritorious service.

World.title: Trump says he is open to trilateral summit with Putin and Xi
World.content:
The president told reporters that such a meeting would focus on denuclearization, not the war in Ukraine as Moscow had suggested earlier.

President Donald Trump said Monday he was open to a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, but said such a meeting would not focus on the war in Ukraine.

Trump told reporters at the White House that he would participate in a summit with both leaders if the purpose was to discuss denuclearization. The comments came after reports that Putin had proposed that the three leaders meet on the sidelines of next month’s APEC summit in China to discuss how to end the war in Ukraine.

“I would do it, not so much for Ukraine,” Trump said. “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They have not been doing much. And the same thing with China. We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons, denuclearization. And anytime I can have a meeting on denuclearization.”

World.title: EU Parliament launches probe into fake email seeking to sway internal election
World.content:
The email disparaged the work of Portuguese EPP lawmaker Sebastião Bugalho ahead of the EPP’s vice-chair elections. When asked, Bugalho’s office said he “will obviously not comment on forged emails.”

Pedro López de Pablo, the EPP’s press director, said: “The group has been informed that there will be an investigation.”

The Parliament’s probe was announced by EPP group chair Manfred Weber to all the group’s lawmakers at a closed-door meeting on Monday afternoon, according to four people in the room. They were granted anonymity to discuss the sensitive internal matter.

Halicki sent his request for an investigation by Belgian authorities to Parliament President Roberta Metsola on Friday. “As I know, the Parliament immediately reacted, and the investigation has been launched,” he said, referring to the internal probe.

The email comes amid a fierce campaign for the EPP’s vice-chair positions, which are to be voted on on Tuesday. Twelve lawmakers, including Bugalho and Halicki, are battling it out for 10 spots.

World.title: After looting spree, France tells online resellers to crack down on traffic of stolen goods
World.content:
During a government press conference earlier in the day, Minister for Small Businesses Serge Papin said officials were working on “coordination between investigators and online platforms” to identify the individuals behind suspicious listings. A specific protocol is expected to be put in place, according to a government source speaking to POLITICO.

A spokesperson for Vinted France said the sale of stolen goods, or soliciting the purchase of such goods, is strictly prohibited on the platform. "We have a zero-tolerance policy on this matter," said the company representative. "Since this past weekend, our teams have taken immediate action to identify and remove listings that may involve stolen goods, and we have stepped up our monitoring of suspicious listings."

Other platforms weren't immediately available for comment.

The discussions with the reselling websites are also likely to touch on longer-term questions around platform responsibility and the monitoring of illicit trade within the EU’s digital marketplace.

The issue of looted goods sold on online marketplaces “is a new dimension and the Commission is happy to look at it in collaboration with French authorities," European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier told POLITICO.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed local authorities to enact “partial curfews” Monday evening to prevent further looting and rioting. Papin said a “special support fund” will be set up to provide financial assistance to the estimated 3,000 local businesses affected by the weekend’s unrest.

Eliza Gkritsi contributed to this report.

World.title: UK and Poland accuse Hegseth of downplaying allies’ role in Afghanistan
World.content:
But he added: “Except there were maybe five that contributed. It was actually closer to one or two that by the end were actually involved in kinetic operations. In fact the patch ISAF, we joked it meant ‘I Saw Americans Fighting’.”

All of NATO’s then-28 members participated in the U.S.-led war in Afghanistan, after the alliance invoked Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty – NATO’s collective defense clause – on September 12, 2001, a day after the terrorist attacks that took place on 9/11.

It remains the only time the article has been invoked in alliance history.

Asked about his comments Monday, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s official spokesperson pointed out that “thousands of British and allied families made huge sacrifices to play their significant part in that war and uphold our values,” while “more than 450 British personnel never returned.”

“Their sacrifice and that of other NATO forces was made in the service of collective security and in response to an attack on our ally,” he continued.

“We are incredibly proud of our armed forces, and their service and sacrifice will never be forgotten. And it is wrong to diminish their role.”

World.title: French PM orders ‘localized’ curfews in response to looting and unrest
World.content:
Lyon, Nice and Lille issued curfews on Monday evening, while Paris instituted a partial curfew and a ban on protests, both of which affected only some neighborhoods. Coulaine issued a curfew affecting only minors.

Those announcements came after an emergency meeting at the French interior ministry following scenes of widespread chaos that played out across France on Saturday. While President Emmanuel Macron attempted to reassure a worried public with a primetime address Sunday night, the speech was widely panned across the political spectrum as insufficient. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez submitted his resignation in the aftermath of the weekend’s unrest, but Macron refused to accept it.

The government is now scrambling to bat down allegations that it has mismanaged the affair and stop it from snowballing into a sustained movement like the Yellow Jackets of 2018 ahead of the spring presidential election, which far-right leader Marine Le Pen is favored to win.

Saturday’s demonstrations saw teachers and students, who have been blockading schools for weeks demanding more funding for schools, join forces with those upset about the rapidly rising cost of living — and while hundreds of thousands of people marched peacefully, violent incidents were observed in some of France’s largest cities, including Paris.

A website claiming to represent the Yellow Jacket movement launched calls for more protests this coming Saturday, and the country’s main unions are organizing strikes and protests on Nov. 5 in opposition to the government’s proposed budget, which includes €43 billion in savings.

While high schools are currently closed for holidays, some students are still protesting. The Louvre museum was closed due to a strike movement from students at an art history university located inside the palace.

World.title: The multiple sclerosis gap Europe cannot afford to ignore
World.content:
As Europe plans its response to the neurological disease burden, a fundamental measurement gap is being overlooked — and the cost of ignoring it is being felt.

A briefing requested earlier this year by the European Parliament’s Committee on Public Health (SANT) put it plainly: neurological diseases are one of Europe’s most urgent and rapidly expanding health, social and economic challenges. Published in February 2026, it calls for a coordinated European plan linking prevention, early diagnosis, research and innovation.1 But before Europe considers what that plan should look like, a foundational question demands attention: are we measuring the right things?

Multiple sclerosis (MS), a chronic, progressive disease of the central nervous system that disrupts communication between the brain and the body, offers a revealing case study. Consider a woman in her mid-30s, working, raising a family, managing what her neurologist calls “stable” MS. She has not slept properly in years, her memory has been slipping and she is cutting her hours at work. Her last clinical note reads: “No change.” On paper, she is stable, but in reality she is anything but.

Her story is not unusual. According to research commissioned by Sanofi*, the gap between what health systems measure and what people with MS experience may be costing individuals, families and economies more than we realize.3

The stakes for Europe

Over 3 million people globally live with MS and Europe has the highest prevalence, at 133 per 100,000 people.2,3 The condition strikes primarily during prime working years, meaning hundreds of thousands of people are navigating a progressive, unpredictable disease at precisely the point when inadequate support is felt most acutely.3

That support begins with measurement. And right now, the tools used to assess MS in clinical practice do not fully capture what people with the disease experience.3

The consequences extend far beyond the clinic: 82 percent of people with severe MS rely on unpaid family caregiving, yet this burden rarely appears in standard health data or policy design.3 When the full impact of disease is not measured, health systems can underestimate need, delay support, and overlook the wider effects on work, welfare and family life.3

The measurement gap

The Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), the primary tool used to measure MS disability, was developed in 1983 to assess walking ability. We now know that MS affects far more than mobility. Fatigue affects 94 percent of people with MS, while 75 percent report cognitive difficulties, but both are absent in the EDSS assessment.3 In a field where clinical consensus is rare, seven in ten neurologists agree: a more comprehensive approach is needed.3

Growing recognition of smouldering neuroinflammation has made the need for new methods of quantifying MS progression increasingly urgent. This slow, chronic disease activity can persist even when a patient appears clinically stable, with effects that are subtle, cumulative and easy to miss until significant damage has already occurred.4

This is why Sanofi initiated the development of the Smouldering Associated Worsening (SAW) Index+. The SAW Index Study — led by an international steering committee of leading MS clinicians, researchers and patient advocates — is due to complete in 2027. Based on hundreds of hours of in-depth qualitative research with people with MS, the goal of the SAW Index is to provide neurologists with a comprehensive measurement framework that bridges the gap between lived experience and what clinical tools are currently able to detect.

According to the European Multiple Sclerosis Platform, people with MS experience an average of 14 symptoms within the first five years of diagnosis, with fatigue, sensory problems, sleep disturbances, cognitive impairment and balance problems among the most common.5 These are precisely the experiences the SAW Index is designed to surface, replacing static labels like “moderately affected” with measurement metrics grounded in the experience and words of people with MS.

The cost of this gap

These aspects of MS can be challenging to quantify and are associated with substantial societal and economic burdens. Lifetime productivity loss per person with MS ranges from €394,000 in France to €668,000 in Germany.3 The cost profile shifts significantly as the disease progresses: in mild MS, direct healthcare costs dominate; in severe MS, indirect costs become the primary driver.3 Indeed, lost wages, absenteeism, early retirement, disability payments and the growing burden on unpaid carers outweigh medical costs in many countries, placing growing long-term pressure on social insurance and disability systems.3

Early identification of progression could change that trajectory, extending years of employment, preserving household income, and reducing long-term dependence on disability and social benefits.3,6 That is a cost-avoidance opportunity current measurement frameworks are missing.

Progress in motion

There is no single fix, but there is momentum.

MS care has advanced significantly in recent decades: diagnosis is happening earlier, treatment options have expanded and the focus is shifting from relapse control alone to slowing long-term disability progression.7 Furthermore, there is growing recognition of the importance of cognition, mental health, rehabilitation and the day-to-day realities that shape whether people living with MS can remain independent and active.8

The challenge now is to ensure policy keeps pace with that progress, and better measurement is part of the answer. If Europe wants health spending to deliver lasting value, it should see these improvements not as costs to be managed, but as investments in independence, participation, productivity and more sustainable health systems.

Time to act

The European Parliament’s SANT Committee has called for a fully funded European neurological health plan — one with the scale and ambition of Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan, aligning health, research and societal action in a unified framework.1 MS offers a clear and immediate test case for what that ambition looks like in practice.

But ambitious plans require accurate data. If Europe is serious about a coordinated response to neurological disease, getting measurement right is not a secondary concern; it is the foundation on which everything else depends.

The people living with MS across the continent cannot wait for the tools that measure their disease to catch up with the science that understands it. Neither should policymakers.

World.title: Adipositas: Sparen kann für den Staat teuer werden
World.content:
Das deutsche Gesundheitssystem beschränkt sich auf die Behandlung von Folgeerkrankungen der Adipositas, etwa Typ-2-Diabetes oder Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen. Deren Behandlung ist medizinisch notwendig. Die politische Frage lautet jedoch, ob es auf Dauer wirtschaftlich sinnvoll ist, vor allem die Folgen der Adipositas zu finanzieren, anstatt Adipositas direkt zu behandeln. Das ist vor dem Hintergrund des demografischen Wandels und mangelnder Fachkräfte besonders relevant. Eine vom Institut der deutschen Wirtschaft veröffentlichte Prognose geht davon aus, dass Deutschland bis 2036 rund 4,3 Millionen Arbeitskräfte fehlen könnten. Adipositas ist nicht die Ursache des Fachkräftemangels und auch nicht die alleinige Lösung. Sie ist aber ein Faktor, der die Erwerbsfähigkeit beeinträchtigen kann. Eine Gesundheitspolitik, die Menschen länger gesund im Arbeitsleben halten will, muss solche Zusammenhänge berücksichtigen.

Entscheidend ist nicht allein, ob eine Therapie kurzfristig zusätzliche Kosten verursacht.

Der Blick ins Ausland zeigt, dass die politische Debatte über die Versorgung von Adipositas auch anders geführt werden kann. In England hat der staatliche Gesundheitsdienst NHS mit einem stufenweisen Rollout medikamentöser Therapien begonnen. Vorgesehen ist der Zugang zunächst für Erwachsene mit einem Body-Mass-Index von mindestens 35 kg/m2 und mindestens einer Begleiterkrankung. Die Behandlung erfolgt über spezialisierte Dienste und soll zunehmend auch in Hausarztpraxen angeboten werden. Grundlage sind Empfehlungen des englischen Instituts NICE. Nach dessen Schätzungen könnten in England rund 3,4 Millionen Erwachsene grundsätzlich die Kriterien für eine Behandlung erfüllen.

Das englische Modell setzt auf definierte medizinische Kriterien, einen schrittweisen Zugang und die Einbettung in bestehende Versorgungsstrukturen. Gerade darin liegt der gesundheitspolitische Unterschied zu der Debatte in Deutschland. Hierzulande richtet sich der Blick fast reflexartig auf die Kosten moderner Arzneimittel und Therapien. Das ist angesichts knapper Kassen nachvollziehbar, greift aber zu kurz. Entscheidend ist nicht allein, ob eine Therapie kurzfristig zusätzliche Kosten verursacht. Zu berücksichtigen sind ebenso Kosten unbehandelter oder zu spät behandelter Erkrankungen und demgegenüber mögliche Einsparungen durch vermiedene Folgeerkrankungen, weniger Arbeitsausfälle und einen längeren Verbleib im Erwerbsleben. Für Deutschland stellt sich also die grundsätzliche Frage: Soll die medikamentöse Behandlung von Adipositas weiterhin aus der Regelversorgung ausgeschlossen bleiben oder braucht es, ähnlich wie in England, einen zielgerichteten und stufenweisen Zugang für Menschen mit Adipositas?

Gesundheit als Investition

Eine moderne Adipositas-Versorgung ist eine Investition in die Stabilität von Gesundheitswesen, Arbeitsmarkt und Sozialversicherung zugleich. Zugelassene medikamentöse Therapien sollten dort eingesetzt werden können, wo sie medizinisch angezeigt sind. Ernährungs-, Bewegungs- und Verhaltenstherapie bleiben auch weiterhin wichtige Bestandteile, reichen aber in manchen Fällen nicht aus. Notwendig ist ein Versorgungskonzept, das Prävention, Früherkennung und leitliniengerechte Behandlung verbindet.

Wer nur kurzfristige Ausgaben betrachtet, riskiert, langfristig höhere Belastungen zu finanzieren.

Gerade in Zeiten knapper Kassen verlangt ein verantwortungsvoller Haushalt eine vollständige Kostenrechnung. Die entscheidende Frage lautet daher nicht allein, was eine Behandlung kostet, sondern auch, welche Kosten durch Nichtbehandlung entstehen. Wer nur kurzfristige Ausgaben betrachtet, riskiert, langfristig höhere Belastungen zu finanzieren.
